knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subexpression Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of sharing identical computational nodes in lifted relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two occurrences denote the same deterministic subexpression \(s(x)\). Let the duplicated relaxation use variables \(z_1,z_2\), matching copies \(K(x,z_1)\) and \(K(x,z_2)\) of one defining relaxation, and occurrence constraints involving the respective duplicate variables. Let the shared formulation be obtained by replacing both variables by \(z_s\), imposing \(K(x,z_s)\), and making the same substitution in all occurrence constraints. Under the identification \(z_1=z_2=z_s\), the shared relaxation equals the slice of the duplicated relaxation satisfying \(z_1=z_2\). Its projection onto the original variables is therefore contained in the projection of the unlinked duplicated relaxation. If \(K(x,z)\) is the exact relation \(z=s(x)\), both exact formulations have the same projection onto the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When duplicate occurrences use matching defining relaxations, replacing their separate auxiliary variables by one shared variable is equivalent to adding equality between the duplicates. This preserves the exact model and cannot enlarge the projected continuous relaxation.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Identifying the duplicate variables preserves the exact lifted model and produces a projected relaxation contained in that of the corresponding unlinked duplicated formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Envelope Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex-envelope lower bounds on compact convex domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\operatorname{conv}_C f\) denote the greatest closed convex function majorized by \(f\) on \(C\). For every closed convex function \(q:C\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(q(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in C\), one has \(q(x)\le\operatorname{conv}_C f(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in C\). Consequently, \(\min_{x\in C}q(x)\le\min_{x\in C}f(x)\), and \(\min_{x\in C}\operatorname{conv}_C f(x)=\min_{x\in C}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every closed convex underestimator yields a valid lower bound. The closed convex envelope dominates every such underestimator pointwise and has the same minimum value as the original function.
assumptions_latex: The set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
The function \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is lower semicontinuous and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every closed convex underestimator yields a valid lower bound, and the closed convex envelope is pointwise strongest and has the same minimum as \(f\).

notation.meaning: closed convex envelope of f on C

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-level RLT construction for bounded polynomial models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a bounded polynomial feasible set. Generate valid polynomial relations by multiplying selected valid inequalities, including bound factors \(x_i-l_i\ge0\) and \(u_i-x_i\ge0\), in sign-preserving combinations. Introduce \(y_\alpha\) for each selected monomial \(x^\alpha\), replace every occurrence of that monomial consistently by \(y_\alpha\), and retain the resulting linear equalities and inequalities. The lifted polyhedron \(R\) contains \(\{(x,(x^\alpha)_\alpha):x\in F\}\). Consequently, minimizing the linearized objective over \(R\) gives a lower bound on its minimum over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RLT multiplies valid constraints and bounds, replaces selected monomials by shared lifted variables, and solves the resulting linear relaxation to obtain a valid lower bound.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on a box \(B=[l,u]\).
The vector \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) satisfies \(\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal quadratic convexification on a finite box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f_{\alpha}(x)=f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\) for \(x\in B\). Since each product \((x_i-l_i)(u_i-x_i)\) is nonnegative on \(B\), \(f_{\alpha}(x)\le f(x)\). Its Hessian is \(\nabla^2 f_{\alpha}(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\), which is positive semidefinite by assumption; hence \(f_{\alpha}\) is convex on \(B\). Therefore \(\min_{x\in B}f_{\alpha}(x)\le\min_{x\in B}f(x)\), with equality of function values at every vertex of \(B\).

knowledge_statements.title: DC Minorants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex minorants derived from affine majorants of the subtracted DC component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f=g-h\) on \(C\), where \(g,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex. For any affine function \(a:C\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for all \(x\in C\), define \(m(x)=g(x)-a(x)\). Then \(m\) is convex and satisfies \(m(x)\le f(x)\) throughout \(C\). Hence \(\inf_{x\in C}m(x)\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a DC function g minus h, subtracting an affine upper bound of h from g gives a convex minorant and therefore a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
The function has a DC decomposition \(f=g-h\) on \(C\), with \(g\) and \(h\) convex.
An affine function \(a\) satisfies \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(m=g-a\) is a convex minorant of \(f\) on \(C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite polyhedral minorant of \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is a function \(p:C\to\mathbb{R}\) of the form \(p(x)=\max_{1\le j\le k}\{a_j^\top x+b_j\}\), where \(k<\infty\) and \(a_j^\top x+b_j\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\) and every \(j\). The function \(p\) is convex and piecewise affine, satisfies \(p(x)\le f(x)\) on \(C\), and therefore obeys \(\inf_{x\in C}p(x)\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral minorant is the maximum of finitely many affine functions that all lie below the target function, so its minimum gives a valid lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: DC-to-Polyhedral Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion using a polyhedral lower model and an affine upper model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(f=g-h\) on \(C\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are convex. Let \(p\) be a polyhedral convex function satisfying \(p(x)\le g(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), and let \(a\) be affine with \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in C\). The function \(q(x)=p(x)-a(x)\) is polyhedral convex and satisfies \(q(x)\le f(x)\) throughout \(C\). Thus \(q\) is a polyhedral minorant obtained from the DC representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral lower model of the positive DC component minus an affine upper model of the subtracted component is a polyhedral minorant of the DC function.

A polyhedral convex function \(p\) satisfies \(p(x)\le g(x)\) on \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Minorant Tightness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and uniform tightness characterization for converted DC-polyhedral minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g-h\) and \(q=p-a\) on \(C\), with \(p(x)\le g(x)\) and \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in C\). For every \(x\in C\), the minorant gap is \(f(x)-q(x)=[g(x)-p(x)]+[a(x)-h(x)]\), with both component gaps nonnegative. Consequently, \(q(x)=f(x)\) if and only if \(p(x)=g(x)\) and \(a(x)=h(x)\). For any \(S\subseteq C\), bounds \(0\le g(x)-p(x)\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(0\le a(x)-h(x)\le\varepsilon_h\) for all \(x\in S\) imply \(0\le f(x)-q(x)\le\varepsilon_g+\varepsilon_h\) for all \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The converted minorant gap is the sum of the two nonnegative component gaps. It is zero exactly where both component models are exact, and uniform component-gap bounds add to give a uniform bound on the total gap.
assumptions_latex: The functions satisfy \(f=g-h\) and \(q=p-a\) on \(C\).
The component models satisfy \(p(x)\le g(x)\) and \(a(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).
All component gaps used in the stated bounds are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minorant gap equals the sum of the component gaps; pointwise exactness requires and is implied by exactness of both components, and uniform component bounds add.

notation.meaning: uniform upper bounds on the component gaps

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Minorant Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-based lower bound for a Lipschitz objective on a compact metric domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a compact metric space, let \(L\ge 0\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le Ld(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in X\), and let \(k\ge1\) be an integer with evaluated points \(x^1,\ldots,x^k\in X\). Define \[m_k(x)=\max_{1\le j\le k}\{f(x^j)-Ld(x,x^j)\}.\] Then \(m_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and \[\ell_k:=\min_{x\in X}m_k(x)\le f^*:=\min_{x\in X}f(x).\] If an additional evaluated point is incorporated in the same way, then \(m_{k+1}(x)\ge m_k(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and consequently \(\ell_{k+1}\ge\ell_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative Lipschitz constant and at least one sampled point, the maximum of the sample-based Lipschitz cones globally underestimates the objective. Its minimum is a monotone lower bound on the global optimum.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a compact metric space.
\(L\ge0\) and \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le Ld(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\in X\).
\(k\ge1\) and \(x^1,\ldots,x^k\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_k\le f^*\) and \(\ell_{k+1}\ge\ell_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Duality Gap under Nested Compact Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An asymptotic exactness result for Lagrangian dual bounds on nested localized subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the feasible set of the underlying problem. knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the bound obtained by minimizing a partial Lagrangian over the retained domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a nonempty set, let \(f:X	o\mathbb R\), \(g:X	o\mathbb R^m\), and \(h:X	o\mathbb R^q\), and define \[p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}.\] For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(
u\in\mathbb R^q\), the Lagrangian is \[L(x;\lambda,
u)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)+
u^{\mathsf T}h(x),\] and the corresponding Lagrangian bound is the extended-real value \[b(\lambda,
u)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x;\lambda,
u).\] It satisfies \(b(\lambda,
u)\le p^*\). When \(b(\lambda,
u)>-\infty\), it supplies a finite certified lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT optimality and the Lagrangian dual of an inequality-constrained QCQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous quadratic objective and quadratic inequalities, without an assumed convexity of the original QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let q_k(x)=x^TQ_kx+2g_k^Tx+\alpha_k, with Q_k=Q_k^T, and consider q^*=\inf\{q_0(x):q_k(x)\le 0,\ k=1,\ldots,m\}. Define L(x,\lambda)=q_0(x)+\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_kq_k(x) for \lambda\ge0. If \bar x is optimal and a constraint qualification such as MFCQ holds at \bar x, then there exists \lambda\ge0 such that \nabla_xL(\bar x,\lambda)=0 and \lambda_kq_k(\bar x)=0 for every k. Conversely, a feasible \bar x satisfying these conditions is globally optimal if L(\cdot,\lambda) is convex. The Lagrangian-dual value d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_xL(x,\lambda) satisfies d^*\le q^*. Zero duality gap means d^*=q^*; strong duality additionally requires attainment of d^*. A positive gap may occur in the nonconvex case, while d^* admits a semidefinite-programming formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous QCQP with symmetric quadratic matrices, an optimum satisfying a constraint qualification such as MFCQ has nonnegative multipliers satisfying Lagrangian stationarity and complementary slackness. Feasibility, these multiplier conditions, and convexity of the corresponding Lagrangian suffice for global optimality. The Lagrangian dual always provides a lower bound; equality is zero gap, equality with dual attainment is strong duality, and a gap may occur for nonconvex QCQPs. The dual value can be formulated as an SDP.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R^n
q_k(x)=x^TQ_kx+2g_k^Tx+\alpha_k,\quad Q_k=Q_k^T,\quad k=0,\ldots,m
q_k(x)\le0,\quad k=1,\ldots,m
\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m
\text{For KKT necessity, a constraint qualification such as MFCQ holds at }\bar x
\text{For sufficiency, }\bar x\text{ is feasible and }L(\cdot,\lambda)\text{ is convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla_xL(\bar x,\lambda)=0,\quad \lambda_kq_k(\bar x)=0\ (\forall k);\qquad d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_xL(x,\lambda)\le q^*.

u)\) is the dual bound. For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a dual-feasible pair \((\lambda,

children.title: Duality-Gap Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Situations where dual constructions provide weak global certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between guaranteed strong duality and potentially strict Lagrangian lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak duality always gives \(d^*\le p^*\). For a convex primal problem with proper closed convex data, affine equality constraints, and a Slater point, strong duality gives \(d^*=p^*\) and dual attainment under the usual finiteness conditions. Outside this regime, equality is not guaranteed. More sharply, if \(v(u)\) is the perturbation value function, then the Lagrangian dual value at the unperturbed right-hand side is its closed convex envelope value \(v^{**}(0)\); therefore \[p^*-d^*=v(0)-v^{**}(0).\] Nonconvexity or failure of lower semicontinuity of \(v\) at \(0\) can thus create a positive gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slater regularity yields zero gap for convex programs. In general, the gap equals the difference between the perturbation value and its closed convex envelope at zero.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual optimal values are interpreted in the extended reals.
For the strong-duality clause, the primal data are convex and Slater feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*=p^*\) under the stated convex regularity; generally \(p^*-d^*=v(0)-v^{**}(0)\).

notation.meaning: lower-semicontinuous convex biconjugate of the value function

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of a minimization problem and suppose its lifted image satisfies \(T(F)\subseteq R_K\), where \(R_K=\{y:Ay=b,\ y\in K\}\) and \(K\) is a closed convex cone. If the objective has the lifted form \(f(x)=\langle c,T(x)\rangle\) on \(F\), then the conic relaxation value \[\ell_K=\inf\{\langle c,y\rangle:Ay=b,\ y\in K\}\] satisfies \(\ell_K\le p^*\). If \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) induce relaxation sets with \(R_{K_2}\subseteq R_{K_1}\), then \(\ell_{K_1}\le\ell_{K_2}\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing over a conic outer approximation gives a valid lower bound. A smaller nested relaxation set gives a bound at least as strong.
assumptions_latex: \(T(F)\subseteq R_K\).
The lifted objective agrees with the primal objective on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_K\le p^*\), with monotone strengthening under nested conic relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order matrix lifting bound for a quadratically expressed nonconvex minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a quadratic problem in \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), introduce \(X\) to represent \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) and rewrite every quadratic expression linearly in \((x,X)\). Replacing \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) by \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\] yields a semidefinite outer relaxation because every rank-one lifted feasible point satisfies this constraint. If \(\ell_{\mathrm{SDP}}\) is the minimum of the lifted linear objective subject to the translated linear constraints and this PSD constraint, then \(\ell_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le p^*\). Equality holds whenever an optimal relaxation solution has \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) and its extracted \(x\) is primal feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the rank-one quadratic lifting equation by a positive-semidefinite constraint gives an SDP lower bound; rank-one recovery establishes exactness.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraints admit a quadratic lifting.
All primal feasible points map into the stated SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le p^*\), with equality under feasible rank-one recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Hierarchy Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic bound interface for nested conic or moment relaxation levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_r\) be the feasible set of relaxation level \(r\), expressed through affine constraints and membership in a tractable convex cone, and let \(T_r(F)\subseteq R_r\). Suppose compatible projections satisfy \(\pi_r(R_{r+1})\subseteq R_r\) and preserve the lifted objective. Defining \[\ell_r=\inf_{y\in R_r}\langle c_r,y\rangle,\] one obtains \[\ell_r\le\ell_{r+1}\le p^*.\] Thus each level exposes the same solver interface—linear objective, affine equations, and conic membership—while projection compatibility transfers validity and monotonicity between adjacent levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible nested conic relaxations produce monotone lower bounds while sharing a standard affine-conic solver interface.
assumptions_latex: Every primal feasible point has a feasible lift at each level.
Adjacent-level projections preserve feasibility inclusion and objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_r\le\ell_{r+1}\le p^*\) for every hierarchy level \(r\).

children.title: Semidefinite Scalability Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Scalability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and storage costs limiting interior-point solution of semidefinite relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a dense semidefinite program containing one unrestricted PSD block of order \(m\). Explicitly storing that symmetric block requires \(m(m+1)/2=\Theta(m^2)\) scalar entries. In the dense arithmetic model, forming or factoring an order-\(m\) positive-definite matrix costs \(\Theta(m^3)\) operations, so any interior-point implementation performing such a factorization has per-iteration cost at least \(\Omega(m^3)\) and block-storage cost \(\Omega(m^2)\). Additional coupling constraints can make the Newton-system cost larger. Hence liftings whose PSD order grows rapidly encounter quadratic memory and at least cubic dense-factorization barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense PSD block of order m needs quadratic storage, while interior-point factorization incurs at least cubic arithmetic per iteration; coupling constraints may increase this cost.
assumptions_latex: The PSD block is dense and stored explicitly.
The computational model uses classical dense matrix factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block incurs \(\Omega(m^2)\) storage and at least \(\Omega(m^3)\) dense factorization work per interior-point iteration.

notation.meaning: order of the dense PSD block

knowledge_statements.title: Successive Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic epigraph outer-relaxation workflow driven by valid separating inequalities and certified lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be compact, let \(F\subseteq X\) be nonempty, and let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\). Define the feasible epigraph \[E=\{(x,t)\in F\times\mathbb R:t\ge f(x)\}.\] Starting from an outer set \(R_0\supseteq E\), at iteration \(k\) solve \[(x^k,t^k)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,t)\in R_k}t,\qquad \ell_k=t^k.\] Maintain an incumbent value \(u_k=f(\hat x^k)\) for some \(\hat x^k\in F\), updating it whenever a better feasible point is found. If \(u_k-\ell_k\le\varepsilon\), stop and return \(\hat x^k\) with the bounds \(\ell_k\le p^*\le u_k\). Otherwise, if \((x^k,t^k)\notin E\), obtain an affine inequality valid for every point of \(E\) and violated by \((x^k,t^k)\), intersect \(R_k\) with that inequality to form \(R_{k+1}\), and repeat. If \((x^k,t^k)\in E\), then \(x^k\) is globally optimal and the procedure may terminate with zero gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the epigraph coordinate over an outer relaxation, maintain a feasible incumbent, and repeatedly separate any relaxation optimizer lying outside the true epigraph. The lower and upper bounds certify termination, while a relaxation optimizer in the true epigraph is globally optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is compact and \(\varnothing\ne F\subseteq X\).
Each relaxation subproblem attains its minimum.
Every generated affine inequality is valid for all of \(E\) and violated by the current point outside \(E\).
A feasible incumbent is available whenever a finite upper-bound certificate is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_k\le p^*\le u_k\), and \(u_k-\ell_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal incumbent.

knowledge_statements.title: Successive Underestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone lower-envelope refinement using globally valid minorants of the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and suppose that after evaluating any \(z\in X\), an oracle returns a function \(m(\cdot;z)\) satisfying \(m(x;z)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Given evaluated points \(x^1,\ldots,x^k\in X\) with \(k\ge1\), define \[q_k(x)=\max_{1\le j\le k}m(x;x^j),\qquad u_k=\min_{1\le j\le k}f(x^j).\] Compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}q_k(x),\qquad \ell_k=q_k(x^{k+1}).\] If \(u_k-\ell_k\le\varepsilon\), return a sampled point attaining \(u_k\). Otherwise evaluate \(f(x^{k+1})\) and set \[q_{k+1}(x)=\max\{q_k(x),m(x;x^{k+1})\},\qquad u_{k+1}=\min\{u_k,f(x^{k+1})\}.\] Then \(\ell_k\le f^*\), and the next lower bound satisfies \(\ell_{k+1}\ge\ell_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Form the maximum of all available global minorants, minimize it to obtain a lower bound and the next sample, and stop when that bound is within tolerance of the best sampled value. Otherwise add the new minorant and continue, producing nondecreasing lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and each underestimator subproblem attains its minimum.
\(m(x;z)\le f(x)\) for all \(x,z\in X\).
\(k\ge1\) evaluated points are available and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_k\le f^*\), \(\ell_{k+1}\ge\ell_k\), and \(u_k-\ell_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal sampled point.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation-oracle procedure for tightening an outer relaxation while preserving all feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), and let \(q:R_0\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(q(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Given a separation oracle, at iteration \(k\) solve \[x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R_k}q(x).\] If the oracle certifies \(x^k\in F\), return that feasibility certificate. Otherwise obtain \((a_k,b_k)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\) satisfying \[a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\quad\text{for every }x\in F,\qquad a_k^{\mathsf T}x^k>b_k,\] and update \[R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le b_k\}.\] Thus \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\), while \(x^k\notin R_{k+1}\). At a resource limit, \(\inf_{x\in R_k}q(x)\) remains a valid lower bound on \(p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the relaxed objective over the current Euclidean outer set. If its optimizer is infeasible, generate a globally valid affine inequality that excludes it and intersect the relaxation with that inequality. Every iteration preserves the original feasible set and its lower-bound certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R_0\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
\(f:F\to\mathbb R\), \(q:R_0\to\mathbb R\), and \(q(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\).
Each relaxation subproblem attains its minimum.
Every returned affine inequality is valid for every point of \(F\) and violated by the current infeasible optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\) and \(x^k\notin R_{k+1}\), while \(\inf_{x\in R_k}q(x)\le p^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(R\) and \(\bar x\), a separation procedure invokes an exact oracle that either returns \((a,\beta)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in R\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>\beta\), or reports that no supported separator was found. The procedure stops after producing one or more violated inequalities, establishing membership of \(\bar x\) in \(R\), or declaring oracle failure.

children.title: Cut Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Filtering and prioritization of available cuts.

assumptions_latex: Every candidate cut is valid for the original feasible set \(F\).
The selected cut family is finite at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding selected cuts preserves \(F\subseteq R_k\) while potentially tightening the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and progress requirements for selecting cuts from a generated pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(S_k\subseteq\mathcal C_k\) be the cuts selected by a policy and define \(R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in S_k}\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\}\). Validity of every candidate cut implies \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\), independently of the ranking rule. A selection policy is progress-preserving for a sequence of relaxation solutions \((x_k)\) when, whenever a cut with violation at least \(\varepsilon>0\) recurs indefinitely, the policy selects such a cut after finitely many subsequent iterations. Validity preserves lower bounds; the progress condition prevents permanent starvation of uniformly violated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy may rank cuts arbitrarily, but selected cuts must remain valid and persistently significant violations must not be postponed forever.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Selection Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Cut validity correctly implies nested valid relaxations, but the starvation condition does not identify a persistent cut or consistently defined cut family across changing pools \(\mathcal C_k\). No source supports the proposed policy condition or its claimed progress role.

children.title: Separation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Weak, costly, or numerically unreliable separation regimes.

assumptions_latex: Separation is required to be strict.
The relaxation set need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict separation can fail for an infeasible point lying in the closure of the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete boundary showing why closedness matters for strict separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^2:v>0\}\) and \(\bar x=(0,0)\). Then \(R\) is convex and \(\bar x\notin R\), but \(\bar x\in\operatorname{cl}R\). There is no \((a,\beta)\) such that \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) for all \(x\in R\) while \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>\beta\): continuity would extend the non-strict inequality to every point of \(\operatorname{cl}R\), including \(\bar x\). Thus infeasibility alone does not guarantee a strictly violated separating cut when the relaxation is nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point outside a nonclosed convex set may lie on its closure, making strict separation impossible despite infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). For every \(k\geq0\) and \(C\in\mathcal P_k\), let \(\ell_{k,C}:C\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(\ell_{k,C}(x)\leq f(x)\) for all \(x\in C\), and define \(L_k=\min_{C\in\mathcal P_k}\inf_{x\in C}\ell_{k,C}(x)\). If every child \(D\in\mathcal P_{k+1}\) contained in \(C\in\mathcal P_k\) satisfies \(\ell_{k+1,D}(x)\geq\ell_{k,C}(x)\) for all \(x\in D\), then \(L_k\leq L_{k+1}\leq f^*\). If, in addition, \(\max_{C\in\mathcal P_k}\sup_{x\in C}(f(x)-\ell_{k,C}(x))\to0\), then \(L_k\to f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested partition refinement gives nondecreasing valid lower bounds. If child estimators dominate their parent estimators and their errors vanish uniformly, those bounds converge to the global minimum.

At iteration \(k\), compute valid cell bounds, set \(L_k\) to their minimum, discard every cell whose lower bound is at least \(U_k\), and refine selected remaining cells by strengthening their relaxations or partitioning their domains. top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapters 3–4: GOP theory, algorithmic organization, implementation, and studies

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative GOP workflow using primal upper bounds, relaxed-dual lower bounds, qualifying cuts, and connected-variable bound combinations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P^{UBD}=U\), \(R^{LBD}=L\), the bound-combination stores, \(K=1\), \(K^{\mathrm{feas}}=K^{\mathrm{infeas}}=\varnothing\), an initial \(\mathbf y^1\), and \(\epsilon>0\). At iteration \(K\): (1) solve the primal problem at \(\mathbf y^K\); if feasible, store its multipliers and set \(P^{UBD}\leftarrow\min\{P^{UBD},P^K(\mathbf y^K)\}\), and otherwise solve the relaxed primal and store its multipliers; (2) retain previous Lagrange functions whose qualifying constraints hold at \(\mathbf y^K\); (3) for every \(B_l\in CB\), solve the corresponding relaxed-dual subproblem with the applicable feasible-primal optimality cuts or infeasible-primal feasibility cuts, storing each feasible solution; (4) choose the smallest stored value \(\mu_B^{\min}\), set \(R^{LBD}=\mu_B^{\min}\) and \(\mathbf y^{K+1}\) to its associated stored parameter, and delete that stored pair; (5) stop if \(R^{LBD}>P^{UBD}-\epsilon\), otherwise increment \(K\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize upper and lower bounds, bound-combination storage, an initial y, feasibility-history sets, and a tolerance. Each iteration solves the primal problem at the current y. A feasible primal supplies multipliers and an upper-bound update; an infeasible primal is replaced by a relaxed primal supplying feasibility-cut multipliers. Previously generated Lagrange functions are retained only when their qualifying constraints hold. A relaxed-dual subproblem is then solved for every connected-variable bound combination, and feasible solutions are stored. The smallest stored relaxed-dual value becomes the lower bound and its associated y becomes the next iterate. The method stops when the lower bound exceeds the upper bound minus epsilon.
assumptions_latex: CB\text{ is the set of bound combinations for the connected }\mathbf x\text{ variables}
U\gg0,\quad L\ll0,\quad \epsilon>0
\mathbf y^1\in Y\text{ is selected and the primal, relaxed-primal, and relaxed-dual subproblems are defined}
\mu_B^{\mathrm{stor}}\text{ contains a feasible stored value whenever Step 4 is invoked}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R^{LBD}\leftarrow\min\mu_B^{\mathrm{stor}},\qquad \mathbf y^{K+1}\leftarrow\mathbf y^{\mathrm{stor}}\!\left(\arg\min\mu_B^{\mathrm{stor}}\right),\qquad \text{stop when }R^{LBD}>P^{UBD}-\epsilon

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{Initialize storage, }P^{UBD}=U,\ R^{LBD}=L,\ Y^1,\ \epsilon,\text{ and bounds on the inner constraints}.\\&\text{At iteration }k,\text{ solve the primal at }Y^k\text{ and set }P^{UBD}\leftarrow\min\{P^{UBD},Z^k\};\text{ if infeasible, solve a relaxed primal}.\\&\text{Add the resulting Lagrangian constraint, or an infeasibility cut, to the relaxed dual and solve it}.\\&\text{Choose the smallest stored }\mu_B,\text{ set }R^{LBD}\text{ to that value and }Y^{k+1}\text{ to its associated point, then remove the pair}.\\&\text{Stop when }R^{LBD}\ge P^{UBD}-\epsilon;\text{ otherwise increment }k\text{ and repeat}.\end{aligned}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize storage, primal and relaxed-dual bounds, a starting point, a tolerance, and lower and upper bounds on the inner constraints. At each iteration, solve the primal problem and update the upper bound; if the primal is infeasible, solve a relaxed primal. Add a Lagrangian constraint or feasibility cut to the relaxed dual and solve it. Select the smallest stored relaxed-dual value as the new lower bound and use its associated point for the next iteration. Stop when the lower bound is at least the upper bound minus the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \text{The problem is a bilevel linear program}
K^{\max}\text{ is the selected storage horizon}
\epsilon>0
\text{The auxiliary bound problems provide lower and upper bounds for the inner constraints}
P^{UBD}\text{ and }R^{LBD}\text{ are valid primal upper and relaxed-dual lower bounds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R^{LBD}\ge P^{UBD}-\epsilon\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{terminate according to the prescribed bound-gap test}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limit identity for linearized GOP Lagrangians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence lemma for relaxed-dual iterates and the corresponding primal multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the relaxed-dual solutions satisfy \(\mathbf y^k\to\bar{\mathbf y}\) and the corresponding primal Lagrange multipliers satisfy \((\lambda^k,\mu^k)\to(\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\), then, for every bound vector \(\mathbf x^{B_j}\),
\[
\left.L(\mathbf x^{B_j},\bar{\mathbf y},\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\right|_{\mathbf x^k}^{\operatorname{lin}}=P(\bar{\mathbf y}),
\]
where \(P(\bar{\mathbf y})\) denotes the primal optimum at \(\bar{\mathbf y}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modified GOP primal–relaxed-dual algorithm for bilevel linear programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bilevel-linear specialization of GOP primal–relaxed-dual decomposition using residual-bound preprocessing, infeasibility cuts, stored relaxed-dual states, and a bound-gap stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\epsilon>0\), initialize \(P^{UBD}=U\), \(R^{LBD}=L\), the storage arrays, and a starting point \(Y^1\). For each residual \((Ax+By-b)_i\), solve the two auxiliary problems with objectives \(\pm(Ax+By-b)_i\), subject to \((Ax+By-b)_j\le0\) for \(j\ne i\), to obtain its lower and upper bounds. At iteration \(k\): (1) solve the primal problem at \(Y^k\), store its multipliers, and, when a primal objective \(Z^k\) is obtained, update \(P^{UBD}\leftarrow\min\{P^{UBD},Z^k\}\); if the primal is infeasible, solve the relaxed primal and store its multipliers; (2) add the current Lagrange-function constraint to the relaxed-dual problem, or the prescribed infeasibility cut for an infeasible primal, solve it, and store \((\mu_B^{stor}(k),y^{stor}(k))\); (3) select the smallest stored value \(\mu_B^{\min}\), set \(R^{LBD}=\mu_B^{\min}\) and \(Y^{k+1}=Y^{\min}\), and delete that stored pair; (4) stop if \(R^{LBD}\ge P^{UBD}-\epsilon\), and otherwise increment \(k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize primal and relaxed-dual bounds, storage, a starting state, and bounds on the inner residuals. Each iteration solves the primal or its relaxed substitute, adds the corresponding Lagrange constraint or infeasibility cut to the relaxed dual, stores the relaxed-dual result, selects and removes the stored state with the smallest bound value, and stops when the lower and upper bounds differ by at most the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \epsilon>0
U\text{ and }L\text{ are the large positive and negative initialization values specified by the algorithm}
Y^1\text{ is a selected starting point}
\text{The required primal, relaxed-primal, relaxed-dual, and residual-bounding subproblems are formed as specified}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R^{LBD}\ge P^{UBD}-\epsilon\implies\text{termination};\quad R^{LBD}<P^{UBD}-\epsilon\implies k\leftarrow k+1\text{ and repetition of the iteration}

source_refs.locator: 3.13 Reformulation of the Relaxed Dual as a Single MILP Problem p. 126

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the relaxed-dual feasible set is \(D=\bigcup_{j=1}^m\{z:A_jz\leq b_j\}\). Introduce \(\delta_j\in\{0,1\}\), impose \(\sum_{j=1}^m\delta_j=1\), and replace each disjunct by \(A_jz\leq b_j+M_j(1-\delta_j)\), where every component of \(M_j\) is a valid bound over the common bounded domain. Projection of the resulting mixed-integer linear feasible set onto \(z\) equals \(D\). Consequently, optimizing the linear relaxed-dual objective over the disjunction is equivalent to solving this single MILP; invalid or infinite big-\(M\) constants destroy that equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary selectors and valid finite big-M bounds combine finitely many linear relaxed-dual disjuncts into one exact MILP.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Dual MILP Reformulation

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each active node \(s\), solve its GOP relaxed-dual relaxation to obtain \(L_s\). Since the relaxation contains the node-feasible set, \(L_s\) does not exceed any feasible objective value in that region. Therefore \(L_s\geq U\) certifies that node \(s\) cannot improve the feasible incumbent and may be pruned. If the active regions cover all feasible points not already validly fathomed and \(L=\min_sL_s\), then \(L\leq f^*\leq U\). Thus \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) certifies global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. If no active node remains and all removed nodes were validly fathomed, the incumbent is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid node lower bounds justify pruning against a feasible incumbent. When active nodes cover every unresolved feasible point, their smallest bound certifies the global gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a feasible incumbent value \(U\) and active regions with valid lower bounds \(L_s\), where the active regions cover every feasible point not already validly fathomed. Select an active region, use its relaxed-dual solution to propose primal parameters, solve the corresponding primal subproblem, and decrease \(U\) whenever a better globally feasible point is found. Propagate the incumbent to all nodes and fathom every region satisfying \(L_s\geq U\). Generate valid additional relaxed-dual constraints or covering child regions whenever the selected region remains unresolved. For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), stop with a global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate when the active set is nonempty and \(U-\min_sL_s\leq\varepsilon\); if the active set is empty after valid fathoming, stop with a global optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinated search maintains global coverage, turns relaxed-dual candidates into primal trials, propagates feasible incumbents, and stops only with a valid global gap or exhausted-tree certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Three failures invalidate the integrated search certificate. If a node relaxation excludes a feasible point, \(L_s\) need not be a lower bound and pruning by \(L_s\geq U\) may remove a global optimizer. If branching children do not cover their parent, an optimizer can disappear without a pruning certificate. If \(U\) comes from a point infeasible for the original problem, it is not an upper bound and can cause erroneous fathoming. Therefore GOP integration requires relaxation validity, exhaustive regional coverage, and globally feasible incumbents; numerical tolerances must preserve these inequalities conservatively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GOP tree integration is unsound if relaxations exclude feasible points, branching leaves gaps, or the incumbent is not globally feasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordinator maintains a feasible incumbent value \(U\), the outstanding task set \(\mathcal T\), and a valid lower bound \(L_s\) for each \(s\in\mathcal T\). The outstanding task regions cover every feasible point not already validly fathomed. Workers solve assigned primal or relaxed-dual regional subproblems and return feasible points, valid bounds, cuts, or covering child regions. The coordinator monotonically decreases \(U\), atomically records returned results, cancels a task only when it is infeasible or satisfies \(L_s\geq U\), and inserts every unresolved covering child before retiring its parent. For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), termination is permitted when \(\mathcal T=\varnothing\), or when \(\mathcal T\neq\varnothing\) and \(U-\min_{s\in\mathcal T}L_s\leq\varepsilon\). Under reliable accounting and eventual task completion, execution order does not alter these pruning and gap certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed GOP coordinator preserves global coverage and valid bounds while merging worker results, and terminates only after exhaustive accounting or a certified global gap.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Relaxation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical LP interface for a lifted outer relaxation of a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original problem have feasible set \(F\) and value \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). An LP interface supplies variables \(z\in\mathbb R^p\), a polyhedron \(P=\{z:Az\le b,\ Ez=d\}\), a lifting \(T:F\to P\), and coefficients \(c,c_0\) satisfying \(c^\top T(x)+c_0\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). It submits \[L_{\mathrm{LP}}=\inf_{z\in P}(c^\top z+c_0).\]If the LP solver returns a certified optimal or dual-feasible lower bound \(L\le L_{\mathrm{LP}}\), the interface exports \(L\) as a valid lower bound on \(f^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear interface sends a lifted polyhedral outer relaxation to an LP solver and exports only certified solver lower bounds for the original minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(F\ne\varnothing\).
\(T(F)\subseteq P\) and \(c^\top T(x)+c_0\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le L_{\mathrm{LP}}\le f^\star\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Relaxation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex-QP interface for a lifted global relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the original feasible set and \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). A quadratic interface supplies \(z\in\mathbb R^p\), \(Q\succeq0\), affine constraints \(Az\le b\), \(Ez=d\), and a lifting \(T:F\to R\), where \(R=\{z:Az\le b,\ Ez=d\}\). It requires \(q(T(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\), with \(q(z)=\tfrac12z^\top Qz+c^\top z+c_0\), and submits \[L_{\mathrm{QP}}=\inf_{z\in R}q(z).\]Only a certified lower estimate of this convex QP value may be exported as a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic interface submits a convex lifted QP whose feasible image contains every original feasible point and whose objective underestimates the original objective.

\(T(F)\subseteq R\) and \(q(T(x))\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in F\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-to-Quadratic Escalation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional replacement of an LP relaxation by a tighter convex quadratic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node, construct lifted relaxation sets \(R_Q\subseteq R_L\) containing every lifted original feasible point, where \(R_L\) is polyhedral and \(R_Q\) adds convex quadratic constraints. Minimize the common linear epigraph objective \(t\) first over \(R_L\), obtaining \(L_L\). If the LP bound is certified and a prescribed escalation predicate \(E\)—for example, an excessive incumbent gap or violated quadratic strengthening—holds, solve \(L_Q=\inf\{t:(z,t)\in R_Q\}\). Export \(L_Q\) only when certified; otherwise retain \(L_L\). Stop when neither escalation nor further node processing is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the linear relaxation first, invoke a tighter convex quadratic relaxation when a declared trigger holds, and retain the strongest certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(R_Q\subseteq R_L\).
Both relaxation sets contain the lifted feasible set of the original node problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_L\le L_Q\le f^\star\), so certified escalation cannot weaken the node lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the original feasible set, let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be its objective, and define \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Fix integers \(p,m,r\ge1\). A convex nonlinear interface supplies a convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), convex functions \(\phi,g_1,\ldots,g_m:C\to\mathbb R\), an affine map \(h:C\to\mathbb R^r\), and a lifting \(T:F\to C\) satisfying \(g_i(T(x))\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(h(T(x))=0\), and \(\phi(T(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). It submits \[L_C=\inf\{\phi(z):z\in C,\ g_i(z)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h(z)=0\}.\] A solver value is exposed to global search only when it is a certified lower estimate of \(L_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface submits a convex nonlinear outer relaxation with an underestimating objective and accepts only certified lower estimates from the convex solver.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of an original minimization problem with objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and value \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be a closed convex cone with dual cone \(K^*=\{s\in\mathbb R^p:s^\top z\ge0\ \text{for all }z\in K\}\). A conic interface supplies a lifting \(T:F\to K\) satisfying \(AT(x)=b\) and \(c^\top T(x)+c_0\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\), and submits the primal relaxation \[L_K=\inf\{c^\top z+c_0:Az=b,\ z\in K\}\] together with the dual \[D_K=\sup\{b^\top y+c_0:c-A^\top y\in K^*\}.\] Any validated dual-feasible \(y\) supplies a global lower bound, irrespective of whether dual attainment is established.

children.title: Dual-Bound Recovery
children.top_down_role: Extraction of candidate lower bounds from relaxation-solver outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of a rigorous lower bound from an approximate conic dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal conic relaxation \(\inf\{c^\top z+c_0:Az=b,\ z\in K\}\), let a solver return an approximate multiplier \(\widehat y\). A recovery procedure constructs \(y\) and \(s\) satisfying the exact or outward-rounded identities \(s=c-A^\top y\) and \(s\in K^*\). The recovered scalar \(L=b^\top y+c_0\), rounded downward when arithmetic is inexact, is a verifiable lower-bound certificate. If no such repair can be validated, the approximate dual objective is not exported as a rigorous bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair an approximate dual solution into a validated dual-feasible point, then evaluate its objective downward to obtain a rigorous lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
The primal conic model is a valid relaxation of the original minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=b^\top y+c_0\le f^\star\) whenever \(c-A^\top y\in K^*\).

children.title: Dual-Bound Validation

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility checks required before accepting a conic dual objective as a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a candidate pair \((y,s)\) for the conic dual, validation checks \(s=c-A^\top y\) and \(s\in K^*\) using exact arithmetic or certified enclosures. If an enclosure proves both conditions, compute \(L\le b^\top y+c_0\) with directed downward rounding. The tuple \((y,s,L)\), together with the verified residual and cone-membership enclosures, certifies \(L\le L_K\). A tolerance-only test such as a small norm of \(c-A^\top y-s\) is insufficient unless its effect is converted into a rigorous bound correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate the dual equation, cone membership, and downward-rounded objective; small numerical residuals alone do not certify a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(K^*\) admits a sound membership or enclosure test.
All rounding errors used by validation are bounded outward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validated \((y,s,L)\) implies \(L\le L_K\le f^\star\).

children.title: Postsolve Bound Reconstruction

knowledge_statements.title: Postsolve Bound Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact transfer of a presolved relaxation bound to the original node formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose presolve maps the original relaxation to a reduced problem with objective \(\widetilde f(w)\) and records an exact objective relation \(f_R(z)=\alpha\widetilde f(w)+\beta\), where \(\alpha>0\), for corresponding feasible points in both formulations. If \(\widetilde L\le\inf_w\widetilde f(w)\) is certified, postsolve reconstructs \(L=\alpha\widetilde L+\beta\), using downward rounding when needed. Eliminated variables, fixed-variable contributions, objective scaling, and constant offsets must all be included in the recorded transformation; otherwise no bound is reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the recorded positive objective scaling and offset to a certified presolved bound, accounting for every eliminated contribution and rounding downward.
assumptions_latex: Presolve preserves the relaxation value through \(f_R=\alpha\widetilde f+\beta\) with \(\alpha>0\).
The reduced bound \(\widetilde L\) is certified.

children.title: Invalid-Bound Rejection

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid-Bound Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a numerical relaxation value must not drive pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proposed minimization lower bound \(L\) is rejected whenever its supporting certificate fails validation, its objective transformation cannot be reconstructed, its dual residual or cone membership is known only up to an unaccounted tolerance, or its solver status does not entail a lower bound. The rejected value must not update the node bound and must not justify pruning under the test \(L\ge U\), where \(U\) is an incumbent value. The workflow may retain the value solely as a heuristic diagnostic explicitly marked nonrigorous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject any bound lacking a validated certificate or complete objective reconstruction; it cannot update the node lower bound or prune against an incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The workflow requires rigorous lower bounds for deterministic pruning.
\(U\) is the objective value of a validated incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An invalid \(L\) cannot justify the pruning implication \(L\ge U\Rightarrow\) discard the node.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Domain Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive interval subdivision on one bounded decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with box domain \(X=\prod_{j=1}^n[\ell_j,u_j]\), select an index \(k\) with \(\ell_k<u_k\) and a split point \(s\in(\ell_k,u_k)\). Create children \(X^-\) and \(X^+\) by replacing the factor \([\ell_k,u_k]\) with \([\ell_k,s]\) and \([s,u_k]\), respectively, leaving all other factors unchanged. Apply reduction and bounding independently to both children. A node is terminal for this branching rule when every eligible interval meets its prescribed width tolerance or another stopping rule applies.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching on the range of an auxiliary variable representing a nonlinear expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an extended formulation contain an auxiliary variable \(v\) representing an expression \(g(x)\), with current certified range \([a,b]\). Choose \(s\in(a,b)\) and create two child relaxations by adding \(v\in[a,s]\) and \(v\in[s,b]\), respectively; equivalently, impose the corresponding restrictions on \(g(x)\) when no explicit auxiliary variable is retained. Recompute expression relaxations on each restricted range, then reduce and bound both children. Branching stops for this expression when its range width meets the prescribed tolerance or the representation no longer permits a sound range split.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the certified range of a nonlinear expression or its auxiliary variable, then rebuild relaxations separately on the two covering child ranges.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible parent point satisfies \(v=g(x)\in[a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two child feasible sets cover the parent feasible set, and their expression ranges have widths strictly below \(b-a\).

knowledge_statements.title: Term Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching on an auxiliary variable representing a nonlinear term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a factorable formulation containing an auxiliary variable \(w=t(z)\) with current interval \([\ell_w,u_w]\), choose \(s\in(\ell_w,u_w)\). Create two children by imposing respectively \(w\le s\) and \(w\ge s\), propagate each restriction through the defining relation \(w=t(z)\), and rebuild its convex relaxation. Discard any infeasible child; otherwise retain both children. Stop branching on this term when \(u_w-\ell_w\le\tau\), where \(\tau>0\), and return the surviving subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split an auxiliary term’s range, propagate each half through its defining expression, rebuild relaxations, and retain feasible children until the term interval is sufficiently narrow.

\(\ell_w<u_w\) and \(\tau>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-to-Term Granularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hierarchy induced by decomposing a factorable expression into auxiliary terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e(x)\) be represented by a directed acyclic computation graph \(G=(V,E)\). Expression branching partitions the range of the root node representing \(e\); term branching partitions the range of any selected internal node \(v\in V\). Introducing an auxiliary variable \(w_v\) and equality \(w_v=t_v(w_{\operatorname{pa}(v)})\) for every internal node yields the finest term-level representation. Coarser granularities arise by contracting connected subgraphs and branching only on their aggregate outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expression branching acts at a graph root; term branching acts at internal operations. Contracting or expanding computation subgraphs produces intermediate branching granularities.
assumptions_latex: \(e\) admits a finite directed acyclic factorable representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching granularity is determined by which computation-graph nodes receive explicit range variables and may be partitioned.

notation.meaning: auxiliary output variable for node v
parents of node v in the graph

children.title: Representation-Dependent Branching

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algebraically Equivalent Graphs Can Expose Different Branches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete noninvariance of graph-induced branchable ranges under algebraic reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{On }x\in[0,1],\quad e_1(x)=x-x=e_2(x)=0.\text{ A syntax-driven interval graph for }e_1\text{ may enclose its subtraction output by }[-1,1],\text{ whereas a simplified graph for }e_2\text{ exposes only }\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equivalent expressions x minus x and zero can produce different graph-induced auxiliary ranges and hence different branching candidates.
assumptions_latex: The graph for e_1 is evaluated without dependency-eliminating simplification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_1=e_2\text{ pointwise, but their graph-induced branching candidate sets may differ.}
knowledge_statements.title: Algebraically Equivalent Graphs Can Expose Different Branches
Representation-Dependent Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of available branching objects on the chosen factorable reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two extended formulations \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) project onto the same feasible set in the original variables \(x\). If their computation graphs expose different auxiliary variables or term ranges, then their admissible term-branching disjunctions can differ, even though \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_1)=\operatorname{proj}_x(F_2)\). Consequently, child relaxations and their lower bounds need not coincide under corresponding splits. Representation-dependent branching is therefore not invariant under equivalent reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent formulations may expose different branchable terms, producing different child relaxations and bounds despite representing the same original feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) are valid extended formulations with the same projection in \(x\).
Branching may act on formulation-specific auxiliary terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The available branching disjunctions and resulting relaxation bounds may depend on the selected representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Subdivision Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial branching by a covering subdivision of the current region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current compact region \(R\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), select finitely many compact children \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) satisfying \(R=\bigcup_{i=1}^m R_i\) and \(\operatorname{int}(R_i)\cap\operatorname{int}(R_j)=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\). Construct the restricted optimization subproblem and a valid lower bound on each \(R_i\), discard certified infeasible or dominated children, and insert all remaining children into the active collection. Repeated subdivision terminates according to the solver’s global gap or region-size criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition a compact search region into interior-disjoint covering pieces, bound each restricted problem, prune certified pieces, and retain the rest for further subdivision.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is compact.
Each child bound is valid for its restricted subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained children, together with safely pruned regions, account for the entire parent region \(R\).
