No theorem connecting the selected score to certified progress is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{arg\,max}_jS_j\text{ is a selection rule, not a progress certificate.}

notation.meaning: Heuristic or trial-derived score for candidate j.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Scores Do Not Certify Progress
Relaxation-Informed Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch selection driven by information from the current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an active region \(R	imes W\), solve a valid relaxation and obtain a relaxation solution \((\hat x,\hat w)\). For each admissible branching object \(j\), compute a score \(S_j\) from relaxation information, such as relaxation violation, envelope gap, or predicted child-bound improvement. Choose \(j^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_j S_j\), select a valid split producing children whose union covers the parent feasible set, and resolve or update the child relaxations. Ties are settled by a fixed rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score admissible splits using relaxation violations, envelope gaps, or predicted bound gains; branch on a highest-scoring object while preserving complete coverage.
assumptions_latex: The parent relaxation is valid and has solution \((\hat x,\hat w)\).
Every admissible split covers the parent feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected branch maximizes the prescribed relaxation-based score among current candidates without excluding any parent-feasible point.
review_flags: A direct source is required for the stated generic scoring formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Relaxation-Informed Branching, but the generic maximum-score formulation combining violation, envelope-gap, and predicted-bound-improvement criteria has no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-node selection by the strongest global-bound priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, maintain an active set \(\mathcal A\) whose node \(N\) has a valid lower bound \(L(N)\). At each iteration select \(N_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{N\in\mathcal A}L(N)\), remove it, and either prune it or branch and insert its surviving children. Update the incumbent upper bound whenever a better feasible point is found. Stop when \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\) or when the incumbent satisfies the prescribed gap test against \(\min_{N\in\mathcal A}L(N)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, repeatedly process an active node with the smallest valid lower bound and stop when no nodes remain or the global gap is acceptable.
assumptions_latex: Every active-node lower bound \(L(N)\) is valid.
The active set is finite at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active node with the best current lower bound is processed, and the minimum active bound remains a valid global lower bound.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node N

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports branch-and-bound best-bound node selection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The best-bound minimization policy is standard, precise, and correctly classified as an algorithm, but the record supplies no inspectable source locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-First Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LIFO traversal of the active branch-and-bound tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain active nodes in a stack \(\mathcal S\). Initialize \(\mathcal S\) with the root. At each iteration pop the most recently inserted node \(N\); prune it when infeasibility or bound dominance is certified, otherwise process it and push its surviving children in a fixed order. Continue along the last pushed child before returning to siblings. Stop when \(\mathcal S\) is empty or when a valid global termination test is satisfied, and return the incumbent and certified bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store active nodes on a stack, always process the newest node, and backtrack only after its descendants are processed or pruned.
assumptions_latex: Pruning tests and node bounds are valid.
Each branching operation creates finitely many children.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nodes are traversed in last-in-first-out depth-first order without changing the validity of pruning or global termination certificates.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports depth-first branch-and-bound traversal.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LIFO algorithm matches depth-first branch-and-bound traversal and preserves the distinction between ordering and certification, but no source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Breadth-Oriented Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-prioritized traversal of the active search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each node \(N\) a depth \(d(N)\), with root depth zero. At iteration \(k\), select an active node from \(\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{N\in\mathcal A_k}d(N)\), using a fixed secondary priority among nodes at equal depth. Prune or branch the selected node and insert its surviving children at depth \(d(N)+1\). Stop when the active set is empty or a valid global gap test holds, returning the incumbent and the certified global bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Always process an active node of minimum tree depth, using a fixed tie-breaker, so shallower levels are handled before deeper ones.
assumptions_latex: The root has depth zero and every child has parent depth plus one.
Node pruning and global-gap tests are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No active node at a greater depth is selected while an active node at a smaller depth remains.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports breadth-oriented branch-and-bound search.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimum-depth selection rule accurately captures breadth-oriented search and is correctly classified, but the record lacks a supporting source and locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Oriented Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node priority designed to improve the feasible incumbent quickly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, maintain an incumbent value \(U\) and assign every active node \(N\) a deterministic promise score \(P(N;U)\), where smaller scores represent greater predicted ability to produce a feasible point below \(U\). Select \(N_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{N\in\mathcal A}P(N;U)\), process or prune it using valid certificates, and update \(U\) after each improved feasible point. Stop only under a valid global termination test; the promise score controls order but never certifies pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prioritize nodes predicted to improve the incumbent, while reserving pruning and termination for valid bounds and feasibility certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(P(N;U)\) is defined for every active node.
Pruning does not rely solely on the heuristic promise score.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Search order favors predicted incumbent improvement while correctness remains governed by valid bounds and certificates.
review_flags: The generic promise-score formalization requires a direct solver-workflow source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm appropriately separates heuristic ordering from valid pruning, but the deterministic promise-score formalization is not canonical enough to retain without a direct source.

children.title: Hybrid Search Order
children.top_down_role: Search orders combining multiple fixed node-selection criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Search Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed combination of multiple active-node priority rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_1(N),\ldots,Q_r(N)\) be node-priority measures and let \(\alpha_i\ge0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i=1\). For every active node, compute normalized values \(\widetilde Q_i(N)\) and the hybrid score \(H(N)=\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i\widetilde Q_i(N)\). Select a node minimizing \(H\), with deterministic tie-breaking, then process, prune, or branch it. Continue until a valid global termination test holds; only valid bounds and feasibility tests may justify pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine several normalized node priorities with fixed weights and process a node minimizing the combined score, without using that score as a pruning certificate.
assumptions_latex: All normalized priorities \(\widetilde Q_i(N)\) are defined on the active set.
The weights are nonnegative and sum to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected node minimizes the prescribed fixed hybrid priority, while certification remains independent of that priority.
review_flags: Hybrid search has several incompatible implementations; this weighted-score version needs a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A fixed weighted combination is one possible hybrid search order, but the leaf title does not uniquely imply normalized weighted scoring. A source is required for this particular algorithmic realization.

children.title: Adaptive Search Order
children.top_down_role: Search orders that change selection criteria using observed search state.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Search Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online modification of active-node priorities from observed search progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta_k\in\Theta\) parameterize a node-priority score \(H_{\theta_k}(N)\). At iteration \(k\), select \(N_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{N\in\mathcal A_k}H_{\theta_k}(N)\), process it, and observe search data \(y_k\), such as bound improvement, incumbent improvement, or node-processing cost. Update \(\theta_{k+1}=T(\theta_k,y_k)\) by a specified deterministic rule. Pruning and stopping continue to use valid certificates independently of the adaptive priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update node-priority parameters from observed search progress, then choose nodes under the revised score while keeping certification independent of adaptation.
assumptions_latex: \(H_\theta(N)\) and the update map \(T\) are defined for all encountered states.
Pruning and termination use valid certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Search order responds to observed performance without compromising correctness of bounds, pruning, or termination.
review_flags: The node path does not determine a unique adaptive update rule; a direct source is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parameter-update framework fits adaptive search ordering at an abstract level, but no citation supports this specific score-and-update-map model or its claimed scope.

children.title: Search-Mode Switching
children.top_down_role: Triggers governing transitions among node-selection modes.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Mode Switching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-triggered switching among distinct active-node selection modes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\{m_1,\ldots,m_r\}\) be search modes with priority rules \(H_m\). Initialize a mode \(m_0\). At iteration \(k\), select an active node minimizing \(H_{m_k}\), process it, and evaluate a specified trigger \(g(m_k,z_k)\), where \(z_k\) records search state. Set \(m_{k+1}=g(m_k,z_k)\); otherwise retain \(m_k\). Switching changes only node order, while valid bounds, pruning certificates, and the global stopping test remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use explicit state-based triggers to switch among node-priority modes; switching affects processing order but not valid pruning or termination logic.
assumptions_latex: Each mode defines a priority for every active node.
The switching map \(g\) is specified and deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active search mode evolves according to the trigger map without altering the validity of global certificates.

notation.meaning: search state observed at iteration k

review_flags: A source is needed to support the abstract trigger-based switching formalization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The state-dependent mode-switching algorithm matches the leaf concept and keeps certification separate from ordering, but its abstract trigger-map formalization lacks a supporting source.

children.title: Adaptive Search Instability
children.top_down_role: Oscillation, starvation, or overhead caused by responsive search policies.

assumptions_latex: The active-region queue is finite at each iteration and every queued region has a valid lower bound.
The adaptive policy may change its scoring rule using the complete search history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a fairness condition, global convergence is not guaranteed: an improving infinite nested sequence of regions may remain unprocessed.

notation.meaning: priority score assigned at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: adaptive queue policies require a fairness or exhaustive-selection safeguard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic branch-and-bound failure caused by history-dependent, nonfair region selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_k\) be the active regions and let the policy select \(R_k\in\operatorname{argmin}_{R\in\mathcal Q_k}s_k(R)\), where \(s_k\) may depend on the full history. If there exists an infinite nested sequence \(R^{0}\supset R^{1}\supset\cdots\) containing a global minimizer, but some \(R^{j}\) and all its descendants are never selected after a finite iteration, then valid bounds alone do not force the global optimality gap to close. Thus an adaptive policy can lose convergence unless it guarantees fairness, such as eventual selection of every region that remains active indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A history-dependent search order can permanently starve regions containing a global minimizer; valid bounds do not restore convergence without a fairness safeguard.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Search Instability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the fairness condition and claimed global-convergence failure require a source specific to deterministic region-selection branch-and-bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hereditary Lower Bounds under Regional Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe propagation of a certified parent lower bound to child regions; independent refinement and reusable solver state remain sibling concerns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let region \(R\) be replaced by children \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) with \(R_i\subseteq R\) and \(R\cap F\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^m(R_i\cap F)\). If \(L(R)\leq\inf_{x\in R\cap F}f(x)\) and \(\widehat L(R_i)\leq\inf_{x\in R_i\cap F}f(x)\), using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), then \[L(R_i):=\max\{L(R),\widehat L(R_i)\}\] is a valid lower bound for child \(R_i\). Replacing the parent by these children preserves validity, and the minimum inherited bound on this branch cannot be smaller than \(L(R)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid parent lower bound remains valid for each child and can be strengthened by taking the maximum with a child-specific bound.
assumptions_latex: Each child region is contained in its parent.
The children cover the parent's unresolved feasible portion.
The parent and child-specific lower bounds are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every child, \(\max\{L(R),\widehat L(R_i)\}\leq\inf_{x\in R_i\cap F}f(x)\), and the branch's inherited lower bound cannot decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Hereditary Lower Bounds under Regional Partitioning

assumptions_latex: The problem is minimization over a feasible set, and each active region has a certified lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The queue minimum is a valid global lower bound, and any region whose lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound may be discarded.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for region R

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: branch-and-bound lower-bound invariant and pruning rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queue-level invariant for minimization branch-reduce-bound workflows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(R\in\mathcal Q\), validity means \(L(R)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in R\cap F\}\), with the infimum interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(R\cap F=\varnothing\). Consequently, \(L_{\mathrm{glob}}=\min_{R\in\mathcal Q}L(R)\) is a lower bound on every feasible objective value represented by the active queue. Given a feasible incumbent value \(U\), any region satisfying \(L(R)\geq U\) cannot contain a point improving the incumbent and may be removed without excluding a better solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain certified regional lower bounds; their queue minimum is global, and regions bounded no better than the incumbent can be pruned.
knowledge_statements.title: Regional Lower-Bound Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but no citation supports it. The global interpretation also requires the active queue to be nonempty and to cover every unresolved feasible region.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate Feasibility Does Not Supply a Certified Upper Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification boundary for accepting incumbent candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:x\geq1\}\), whose optimum is \(f^*=1\). For \(\delta>0\), the candidate \(\bar x=1-\delta\) violates the original constraint. If a numerical feasibility tolerance accepts it and stores \(f(\bar x)=1-\delta\) as an upper bound, the purported upper bound is invalid because \(1-\delta<f^*\). A certified incumbent therefore requires original-model feasibility or a rigorous repair producing a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tolerance-feasible but actually infeasible candidate can lie below the true optimum and is not a certified incumbent.
assumptions_latex: No rigorous feasible repair is performed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\notin F,\qquad f(\bar x)=1-\delta<f^*=1.

notation.meaning: Numerically accepted but actually infeasible candidate

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Feasibility Does Not Supply a Certified Upper Bound

assumptions_latex: Every accepted incumbent point is feasible for the original minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent value is nonincreasing and remains a valid upper bound on the global optimum.

notation.meaning: incumbent feasible point after update k
incumbent objective value after update k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incumbent management invariant for minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-incumbent invariant for minimization workflows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(U_0=+\infty\) if no feasible point is known; otherwise set \(U_0=f(x^0)\) for a verified feasible \(x^0\). When a newly verified feasible point \(y^k\) is obtained, update \(U_{k+1}=\min\{U_k,f(y^k)\}\) and retain a point attaining that value; otherwise set \(U_{k+1}=U_k\). Then \(U_{k+1}\leq U_k\), and whenever \(U_k<+\infty\), \(U_k\geq f^*\), where \(f^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update the incumbent only with verified feasible points. Its objective value decreases monotonically and remains an upper bound on the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Upper-Bound Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incumbent invariant is mathematically standard and the property role fits, but the record supplies no inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity invariant for sequentially selecting bounding procedures under a cumulative work budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(L(R)=-\infty\) and spent cost \(s=0\). A scheduling policy may select any next method \(j\) using currently available information, provided its execution respects the budget. After obtaining a certified \(L_j(R)\), set \(L(R)\leftarrow\max\{L(R),L_j(R)\}\) and update \(s\). Stop before the cumulative budget is exceeded or when \(L(R)\geq U\). The returned finite \(L(R)\) is certified independently of the scheduling policy; no generic claim of optimal scheduling or positive expected value follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run affordable bounding methods in any chosen order, retain the maximum certified result, and separate bound validity from claims about policy efficiency.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted method output is certified for R.
The scheduler accounts for cumulative cost and has incumbent value \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(R)\leq\inf_{x\in R\cap F}f(x),\qquad L(R)\geq U\Longrightarrow R\text{ is safely prunable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Safe Budgeted Scheduling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Menu Budget Envelope and Pareto Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ex post strength–cost comparison for a finite menu of certified regional bounding methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be finite, and let method \(j\in J\) produce a certified lower bound \(L_j(R)\) with accounted cost \(c_j(R)\geq0\). Define \(B_R(C)=\max\{L_j(R):j\in J,\ c_j(R)\leq C\}\), with value \(-\infty\) when the set is empty. Then \(B_R(C)\) is nondecreasing in \(C\) and is a valid regional lower bound whenever finite. If \(L_j(R)\geq L_i(R)\) and \(c_j(R)\leq c_i(R)\), deleting method \(i\) leaves \(B_R\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite method menu, the strongest certified bound affordable under a budget is monotone in the budget, and an ex post dominated method does not affect that envelope.
assumptions_latex: All methods bound the same regional minimization problem.
\(J\) is finite and costs use one accounting convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1\leq C_2\Longrightarrow B_R(C_1)\leq B_R(C_2)\leq\inf_{x\in R\cap F}f(x).

notation.meaning: Best certified bound in the finite menu with individual cost at most C
Accounted cost of method j on R

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Menu Budget Envelope and Pareto Elimination

assumptions_latex: Each bounding method returns a certified lower bound for the same region.
Bounding methods have estimated computational costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A stronger bound should be computed only when its expected pruning or gap-reduction benefit justifies its additional cost; validity is preserved regardless of the choice.

notation.meaning: lower bound from method j on region R

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity-preserving selection among bounds with differing strength and cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision principle for selecting among certified regional bounding procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed region \(R\), method \(j\) dominates method \(i\) in strength when \(L_j(R)\geq L_i(R)\), but it may cost more. A strength-cost policy chooses \(j\) using only information available before or during bounding and may stop refinement once the estimated value of additional computation is nonpositive. Every returned value must remain certified; in particular, if several valid bounds have been computed, the managed bound is \(L(R)=\max_j L_j(R)\). Pruning is permitted when \(L(R)\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose bound strength according to expected pruning value versus computational cost, while retaining the maximum of all certified bounds already computed.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Strength–Cost Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits, but expected computational value and its stopping threshold are not formally defined, and no source supports this policy formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence and Eventual Pruning under Consistent Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional consequence of asymptotically exact certified candidate bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_R^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in R\cap F\}\in\mathbb R\). Suppose \(\widehat L_t(R)\leq f_R^*\) for every \(t\), \(\widehat L_t(R)\to f_R^*\), and \(L_0(R)\leq f_R^*\). Define \(L_t(R)=\max\{L_0(R),\widehat L_1(R),\ldots,\widehat L_t(R)\}\). Then \(L_t(R)\) is nondecreasing and converges to \(f_R^*\). If a feasible incumbent satisfies \(U<f_R^*\), then \(L_t(R)\geq U\) for all sufficiently large \(t\), so the regional objective-bound test eventually prunes R.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Running maxima of asymptotically exact certified regional bounds converge to the regional optimum and eventually prune a region separated strictly above the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(f_R^*\) is finite.
Every candidate is a valid regional lower bound and the candidates converge to \(f_R^*\).
Eventual pruning additionally requires \(U<f_R^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_t(R)\uparrow f_R^*,\qquad U<f_R^*\Longrightarrow\exists T\ \forall t\geq T:\ L_t(R)\geq U.

notation.meaning: Certified candidate bound at stage t

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence and Eventual Pruning under Consistent Refinement

assumptions_latex: Each refinement stage produces a certified lower bound for the same region.
Previously computed certified bounds remain available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Taking the maximum with the previous bound yields a monotone sequence of valid regional lower bounds.

notation.meaning: managed bound after refinement stage t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotone aggregation of successively strengthened certified bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone staged refinement of a regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a region \(R\), an initial certified bound \(L_0(R)\), an incumbent \(U\), and refinement procedures indexed by \(t\). At stage \(t+1\), compute a certified candidate \(\widehat L_{t+1}(R)\) using additional relaxation effort and set \(L_{t+1}(R)=\max\{L_t(R),\widehat L_{t+1}(R)\}\). Stop when \(L_{t+1}(R)\geq U\), a prescribed resource limit is reached, or the selected improvement test fails. Output the last \(L_t(R)\); it is valid and satisfies \(L_{t+1}(R)\geq L_t(R)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refine a region in stages and keep the maximum certified bound obtained so far, stopping on pruning, low improvement, or a resource limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Bound Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The staged procedure appropriately uses the algorithm role, and maximum aggregation preserves validity. A source and a precise definition of the selected improvement test are still required.

children.title: Bound Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of valid regional or relaxation bounds across related search states.

assumptions_latex: A stored lower bound was certified on a parent region.
The new region is a subset of that parent and the objective and constraints are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parent lower bound remains valid on the descendant and may be reused, although it need not be tight.

notation.meaning: stored certified lower bound on P

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: restriction to a subset preserves a valid minimization lower bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe inheritance of certified bounds from parent to descendant regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(R\subseteq P\) and \(L(P)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in P\cap F\}\). Since \(R\cap F\subseteq P\cap F\), monotonicity of the infimum under set restriction gives \(L(P)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in R\cap F\}\). Therefore the descendant may initialize its managed bound with \(L_0(R)=L(P)\). Reuse is invalid if the stored value was only heuristic, or if changes to the model destroy the stated set inclusion or alter the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified parent-region lower bound remains valid for any unchanged descendant subregion, though recomputation may produce a stronger bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subset-inheritance property is correct for unchanged minimization data and fits the leaf, but no citation with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Subsolver Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Initialization of relaxation subsolvers from retained computational states.

assumptions_latex: The subsolver accepts an initial state independently of its correctness certificate.
The subsolver's termination test verifies feasibility and bound validity for the current regional problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transferred state may accelerate computation, but only newly verified current-region outputs may affect pruning or certification.

notation.meaning: stored state from a related solve

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: warm starts are computational hints whose outputs require current-instance verification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-safe warm starting of regional bounding or feasibility subsolvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the current subproblem \(\mathcal P_R\) and a stored state \(z^{\mathrm{old}}\) consisting of compatible primal, dual, basis, or algorithmic data. Project or discard components that violate the current variable domains, initialize the subsolver with the remaining state, and solve \(\mathcal P_R\). Accept an output \(z_R\) only after the current subsolver verifies its required feasibility, dual-feasibility, or relaxation certificate. The warm start itself supplies no bound certificate; stopping and pruning decisions use only quantities verified for \(\mathcal P_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a regional subsolver from compatible stored state, but use its results only after all certificates are revalidated for the current subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Subsolver Warm Starts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the broad treatment of primal, dual, basis, and algorithmic warm-start states requires authoritative support specifying compatibility and current-instance certificate checks.

children.title: Reuse Validity Domains
children.top_down_role: Regional and model-state limits governing safe reuse.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate-preserving restriction of a cached pointwise lower model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(q_{\mathrm{old}}(x)\leq f_{\mathrm{old}}(x)\) for every \(x\in D_{\mathrm{old}}\). If \(D_{\mathrm{new}}\subseteq D_{\mathrm{old}}\) and \(f_{\mathrm{new}}(x)=f_{\mathrm{old}}(x)\) for every \(x\in D_{\mathrm{new}}\), then \(q_{\mathrm{old}}(x)\leq f_{\mathrm{new}}(x)\) on \(D_{\mathrm{new}}\). Consequently, minimizing \(q_{\mathrm{old}}\) over \(D_{\mathrm{new}}\) gives a lower bound for minimizing \(f_{\mathrm{new}}\) over any feasible subset of \(D_{\mathrm{new}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached underestimator remains valid after domain restriction when the current objective agrees with the old objective on the new domain.
assumptions_latex: The cached model is a pointwise underestimator on its recorded domain.
The current domain is contained in that domain and objective semantics agree there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_{\mathrm{old}}\leq f_{\mathrm{new}}\text{ on }D_{\mathrm{new}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Concrete Underestimator Reuse Test

assumptions_latex: A reusable state is accompanied by the model data and domain assumptions under which it was certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse is certificate-preserving exactly on instances satisfying the stored state's validity predicate; outside that domain, revalidation is required.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cached certificates are reusable only under their recorded assumptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate defining where cached bounds, cuts, or solver states remain valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stored state \(s\), define its reuse domain by \(D_s=\{d:V_s(d)=\mathrm{true}\}\). The predicate \(V_s\) must check every assumption used by the stored certificate, including unchanged objective and constraint semantics, compatible parameter values, and the required relation between old and current variable domains. Direct certificate-bearing reuse is permitted only when \(d\in D_s\). If \(d\notin D_s\), the state may be used solely as an untrusted computational hint and every bound, feasibility claim, or pruning consequence must be rederived for the current instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached state is directly reusable only on model and region data satisfying every assumption recorded with its certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Reuse Validity Domains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the predicate is defined only abstractly. The claim that it characterizes certificate-preserving reuse exactly needs a source or a complete formal specification of the certificate assumptions.

children.title: Stale-State Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Change Invalidates a Cached Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete stale-state failure with an unchanged domain and altered objective semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(D=[0,1]\), let \(f_{\mathrm{old}}(x)=x\) and \(f_{\mathrm{new}}(x)=x-1\). The cached value \(L_{\mathrm{old}}=0\) is valid for the old problem because \(\inf_D f_{\mathrm{old}}=0\), but it is invalid for the current problem because \(\inf_D f_{\mathrm{new}}=-1<0\). Thus an unchanged domain does not preserve a lower-bound certificate after an objective change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the objective can invalidate a cached lower bound even when the domain is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The cached bound is reused without validation after the objective changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathrm{old}}=0>\inf_{x\in[0,1]}f_{\mathrm{new}}(x)=-1.

notation.meaning: Objectives before and after the model change

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Change Invalidates a Cached Lower Bound

assumptions_latex: A cached state is used after at least one assumption supporting its certificate has changed.
No current-instance revalidation is performed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cached quantity may cease to be a valid bound or feasibility certificate, so pruning based on it can remove a globally optimal region.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: changing certificate assumptions can invalidate cached pruning information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanism for unvalidated cached bounds or solver certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cached bound satisfying \(L_{\mathrm{old}}\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F_{\mathrm{old}}\}\) need not satisfy \(L_{\mathrm{old}}\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in F_{\mathrm{new}}\}\). For example, let \(f(x)=x\), \(F_{\mathrm{old}}=[1,2]\), and \(F_{\mathrm{new}}=[0,2]\). The cached value \(L_{\mathrm{old}}=1\) is valid for the old domain but invalid for the new one, whose optimum is \(0\). If an incumbent \(U=1/2\) is available, stale pruning using \(L_{\mathrm{old}}\geq U\) incorrectly discards a region containing the global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a certificate's domain can invalidate a cached bound; stale pruning may then discard a region containing the true global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-State Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nontrivial extreme face, positivity of the minimum construction quantity beta guarantees that the associated inequality is a facial cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backward Inverse Contractors Must Retain Every Branch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for noninjective primitive operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v=\phi(u)\), a backward contractor is sound only if \(\{u\in U:\phi(u)\in V\}\subseteq B_\phi(U,V)\subseteq U\). For \(v=u^2\), \(U=[-2,2]\), and \(V=[1,4]\), both inverse branches \([-2,-1]\) and \([1,2]\) must be retained. A box-valued contractor may return their hull \([-2,2]\), but returning only one branch is unsafe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward propagation through a noninjective operation must preserve every inverse branch; keeping one branch can delete feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: The backward output is represented by one interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi^{-1}(V)\cap U\subseteq B_\phi(U,V)\text{ is necessary for soundness.}

notation.meaning: backward inverse contractor for primitive phi

knowledge_statements.title: Backward Inverse Contractors Must Retain Every Branch

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Propagation Strength Depends on Graph Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation dependence of interval forward-backward propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Algebraically equivalent expression graphs can produce different interval contractions because local interval evaluation does not generally recover dependencies between repeated occurrences. On \(X=[-1,1]\), direct interval evaluation of \(x-x\) gives \([-2,2]\), whereas simplifying the same expression to the constant zero gives \([0,0]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent expression representations need not propagate equally strongly; dependency handling and graph construction affect interval bounds.
assumptions_latex: Ordinary interval arithmetic evaluates primitive graph operations locally without symbolic dependency recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_G=f_{G'}\text{ pointwise does not imply identical interval propagation on }G\text{ and }G'.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Strength Depends on Graph Factorization

assumptions_latex: Each elementary expression operator has an inclusion-isotonic interval extension.
Initial intervals enclose every feasible value of the corresponding graph variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Forward and backward interval propagation preserves all feasible assignments and either contracts domains or detects an empty relaxation.

notation.meaning: current interval of graph variable v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard interval forward-backward propagation on factorable expression graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval forward-backward propagation on a factorable expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each operation by \(v=\phi_v(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\) in a directed acyclic graph \(G\). In a forward sweep replace \(X_v\) by \(X_v\cap\Phi_v(X_{u_1},\ldots,X_{u_m})\), where \(\Phi_v\) is an inclusion-isotonic interval extension. In a backward sweep, intersect each \(X_{u_i}\) with a valid interval inverse image of \(X_v\) under \(\phi_v\). Repeat according to the propagation schedule. Output the contracted intervals; if any \(X_v=\varnothing\), declare the interval relaxation infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate intervals forward through expression operators and backward through valid inverse images, preserving feasible points while tightening domains or detecting emptiness.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits expression-graph propagation, but validity requirements for the backward interval inverse images and the resulting infeasibility declaration need a specific interval-analysis source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of strongest individual box contractors to detect joint infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]^2\), \(F_1=\{(x,y)\in X:x-y=0\}\), and \(F_2=\{(x,y)\in X:(x-y)^2=1/4\}\). Both \(\operatorname{hull}(F_1)\) and \(\operatorname{hull}(F_2)\) equal \(X\), so their exact individual hull contractors leave \(X\) unchanged, yet \(F_1\cap F_2=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even the strongest box contraction of each constraint separately can stagnate on a jointly infeasible system.
assumptions_latex: Propagation stores only interval coordinate domains and processes the constraints separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_1(X)=C_2(X)=X,\qquad F_1\cap F_2=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: individual constraint relations within the box

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Wise Propagation Is Incomplete

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness of finite constraint-contractor sequences regardless of order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\bigcap_{i=1}^mF_i\), and suppose \(F_i\cap X\subseteq C_i(X)\subseteq X\). For every finite sequence \(i_0,\ldots,i_{k-1}\), iterates \(X^{t+1}=C_{i_t}(X^t)\) satisfy \(F\cap X^0\subseteq X^k\subseteq X^0\). Scheduling may change contraction strength and cost but not finite-sequence soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any finite ordering of sound individual-constraint contractors preserves every jointly feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Every applied contractor is sound for its associated constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\cap X^0\subseteq C_{i_{k-1}}\circ\cdots\circ C_{i_0}(X^0).
knowledge_statements.title: Schedule-Independent Soundness

assumptions_latex: Each constraint contractor is inclusion-preserving: it never removes a point satisfying that constraint.
The current box contains every feasible point under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sequential contractor application preserves the feasible set while producing a nested sequence of boxes; an empty box certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box contraction by individual constraint contractors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial box \(X^0\) and contractors \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) satisfying \(F_i\cap X\subseteq C_i(X)\subseteq X\) for every box \(X\), choose a schedule \(i_k\) and update \(X^{k+1}=C_{i_k}(X^k)\). Then \(F\cap X^0\subseteq X^k\subseteq X^{k-1}\) for every \(k\), where \(F=\bigcap_iF_i\). Stop at emptiness, a fixed point, or a prescribed contraction tolerance. Output the final box; if it is empty, the original box contains no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply inclusion-preserving contractors constraint by constraint. The boxes shrink without losing feasible points, and an empty result certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Based Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contractor iteration and empty-box certificate are internally consistent and the algorithm role fits, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination on a Finite Bound Lattice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient finite-termination condition for exact-change FBBT iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every attainable coordinate endpoint belongs to a finite set, boxes are never enlarged, and every nonterminal sweep strictly tightens at least one endpoint. Then exact-change FBBT terminates after finitely many strict contractions at either the empty box or a common fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FBBT terminates finitely when attainable bounds form a finite lattice and every unfinished sweep makes a strict change.
assumptions_latex: Every attainable lower and upper endpoint belongs to a finite set.
Every sweep produces emptiness, makes no change, or strictly tightens an endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Only finitely many strict contractions are possible.}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination on a Finite Bound Lattice

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common Fixed Point of FBBT Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fixed-point target for a finite family of propagation operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For contractive propagation operators \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), a box \(X^*\) is a common fixed point when \(C_i(X^*)=X^*\) for every \(i\). If a sweep applies every operator and each application leaves the current box unchanged, the resulting box is a common fixed point. Such closure does not certify feasibility or exact feasible hulls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common fixed point is a box no constituent propagation operator can shrink further; it need not contain a feasible point.
assumptions_latex: The fixed-point test applies every constituent operator to the current unchanged box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall i,\ C_i(X^*)=X^*\bigr)\text{ certifies propagation closure, not feasibility.}
knowledge_statements.title: Common Fixed Point of FBBT Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fairness Does Not Guarantee Finite Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between sound nested iteration and finite fixed-point attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Contractivity, solution preservation, and a fair schedule imply nested sound boxes but do not imply finite attainment of a common fixed point. Infinitely many strict contractions may converge to a limiting box, so finite execution requires an explicit finite-lattice, tolerance, pass, or resource stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair sound propagation can tighten forever without finitely reaching its limiting fixed point.
assumptions_latex: No descending-chain condition is imposed on attainable interval endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{fairness plus contractivity}\not\Rightarrow\text{finite termination}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fairness Does Not Guarantee Finite Termination

assumptions_latex: All propagation operators are inclusion-preserving and contractive on interval boxes.
The update schedule is fair whenever iteration continues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iteration produces nested feasible-set enclosures and terminates at an approximate common fixed point or with an empty-box infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: current interval box at sweep k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed-point iteration of contractive inclusion-preserving FBBT operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated FBBT sweeps to a common approximate fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(X^0\) with the regional variable bounds and define one fair propagation sweep \(T\) from the available expression and constraint contractors. For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), set \(X^{k+1}=T(X^k)\). Stop and declare infeasibility if \(X^{k+1}=\varnothing\); otherwise stop when \(X^{k+1}=X^k\), or when a prescribed measure satisfies \(d(X^{k+1},X^k)\leq\tau\). Output \(X^{k+1}\). Inclusion preservation ensures that every iterate contains all feasible points in \(X^0\), while contractivity gives \(X^{k+1}\subseteq X^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeat fair FBBT sweeps until emptiness or negligible contraction. Every iterate encloses the original feasible points and is contained in its predecessor.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point FBBT Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but inclusion preservation, contractivity, and fairness alone do not guarantee finite termination at a fixed point or positive-tolerance test. The box-distance measure also lacks a definition, and no source supports the stated termination claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Optimization FBBT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-constraint auxiliary optimization used as a feasibility-based domain-reduction operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(g(x)\le 0\) be one constraint. For every selected coordinate \(i\), solve or validly bound the auxiliary problems \(L_i=\inf\{x_i:x\in B,\ g(x)\le0\}\) and \(U_i=\sup\{x_i:x\in B,\ g(x)\le0\}\). If the auxiliary feasible set is empty, return infeasible. Otherwise replace \(B\) by \(B'=[\ell',u']\), where \(\ell'_i=\max\{\ell_i,L_i\}\), \(u'_i=\min\{u_i,U_i\}\), and unselected bounds remain unchanged. Repeat across constraints until no prescribed bound improvement occurs or a stopping tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize selected variables over each constraint and the current box; intersect the resulting ranges with the box, or certify infeasibility when an auxiliary feasible set is empty.
assumptions_latex: \(B=[\ell,u]\) is a nonempty finite box.
Each reported auxiliary bound is valid for the corresponding constraint-feasible subset of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in B:g(x)\le0\}\subseteq B'\subseteq B\), unless the auxiliary problem certifies that the set is empty.

notation.meaning: auxiliary lower and upper bounds for coordinate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operator is mathematically sound under the stated validity assumptions, but auxiliary coordinate optimization is ordinarily associated with OBBT. A specific source is needed to establish that this single-constraint construction belongs in the Auxiliary-Optimization FBBT container.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally checkable certificates produced by sound bound-propagation steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in B:g_j(x)\le0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). A propagation infeasibility certificate is either: (i) a derived interval bound \(x_i\in[\ell'_i,u'_i]\) with \(\ell'_i>u'_i\); or (ii) an inclusion evaluation \(G_j(B)\) satisfying \(\inf G_j(B)>0\). The certificate must include the sequence of sound contractor or interval-inclusion operations producing the contradiction. In case (i), soundness implies every point of \(F\) satisfies two incompatible bounds; in case (ii), \(g_j(x)>0\) throughout \(B\). Hence \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty propagated bound or an interval evaluation strictly violating a constraint certifies that the current box contains no feasible point, provided every recorded propagation step is sound.
assumptions_latex: Each propagation operation preserves every feasible point in its input box.
Each \(G_j(B)\) encloses \(\{g_j(x):x\in B\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recorded contradiction certifies \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: feasible subset of the current box

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation certificate for an equality constraint over the current box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)=0\) be required on a box \(B\), and let \(H(B)\) enclose \(\{h(x):x\in B\}\). If \(0\notin H(B)\), then no point of \(B\) satisfies the equality, so the box is infeasible for the full constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inclusion-valid equality range that excludes zero certifies infeasibility of the current box.
assumptions_latex: \(H(B)\) encloses every value \(h(x)\) for \(x\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\notin H(B)\Longrightarrow\{x\in B:h(x)=0\}=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: validated interval enclosure of the equality residual

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Range Exclusion Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical Infeasibility Status Is Not a Propagation Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification boundary for floating-point propagation contradictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numerical report that a propagated interval is empty or a constraint is violated is not by itself a certificate unless every bound used in the contradiction has a verified validity direction. Inward rounding, an unsound inverse branch, or an unverified solver status can create a false contradiction despite the presence of a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation pruning is certifying only when its contradiction can be replayed from rigorously valid bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{unverified numerical contradiction}\not\Rightarrow F\cap B=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Infeasibility Status Is Not a Propagation Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle count excluding the internal cost of globally solving each auxiliary problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If lower and upper endpoints are computed separately for every coordinate in \(I\), full processing uses \(2|I|\) global auxiliary optimization solves and therefore at most \(2n\) solves. Reused, redundant, or symmetry-derived endpoints can reduce this count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate minimization and maximization require two global auxiliary solves per processed coordinate.
assumptions_latex: Each non-reused endpoint is computed by one separate global auxiliary problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{aux}}\le 2|I|\le2n.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Problem Count for Exact OBBT

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact OBBT and uncertified local coordinate optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proposed lower endpoint \(\widehat L_i\) preserves \(F\) only if \(\widehat L_i\le L_i\), and a proposed upper endpoint \(\widehat U_i\) preserves \(F\) only if \(\widehat U_i\ge U_i\). An unvalidated local auxiliary solution need not satisfy these inequalities and can exclude a feasible extreme point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local auxiliary solutions are not exact OBBT certificates: an overestimated minimum or underestimated maximum may remove feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(F\ne\varnothing\).
The coordinate extrema are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L_i>L_i\ \lor\ \widehat U_i<U_i\implies F\nsubseteq\{x:\widehat L_i\le x_i\le\widehat U_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Certification Requirement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated full-coordinate exact OBBT with an unchanged feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(F\), once every endpoint of \(H(F)=\prod_i[\min_Fx_i,\max_Fx_i]\) has been imposed, recomputing all coordinate extrema over the same \(F\) leaves the box unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeating full exact OBBT over the same feasible set produces no further tightening.
assumptions_latex: \(F\ne\varnothing\).
Every coordinate extremum is attained.
The feasible set and all processed endpoints are unchanged between passes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H(F\cap H(F))=H(F).
knowledge_statements.title: Idempotence of Full Exact OBBT

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of exact OBBT only for the coordinate endpoints actually optimized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(F\), let \(L_i=\min_{x\in F}x_i\) and \(U_i=\max_{x\in F}x_i\). Every valid lower bound on coordinate \(i\) is at most \(L_i\), and every valid upper bound is at least \(U_i\). Thus exact OBBT gives the tightest bounds for each processed endpoint; it gives the complete interval hull \(H(F)=\prod_i[L_i,U_i]\) only when both endpoints of every coordinate are processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact auxiliary optimum is the sharpest valid bound for its processed endpoint. The complete interval hull is obtained only when all lower and upper endpoints are processed.
assumptions_latex: \(F\ne\varnothing\).
Every stated minimum and maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i^{\mathrm{valid}}\le L_i\le U_i\le u_i^{\mathrm{valid}}\), with \(B'=H(F)\) when all endpoints are processed.
knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Endpoint Sharpness
Exact OBBT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-wise tightening over the exact node-feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a box \(B=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and exact feasible set \(F=\{x\in B:g_j(x)\le0,\ h_k(x)=0\}\), solve globally, for every selected coordinate \(i\), \(L_i=\min_{x\in F}x_i\) and \(U_i=\max_{x\in F}x_i\). If \(F=\varnothing\), fathom the box. Otherwise set \(\ell'_i=L_i\), \(u'_i=U_i\) for selected coordinates and retain the old bounds elsewhere. Output \(B'=[\ell',u']\). These are the tightest coordinate bounds representable by an axis-aligned box containing \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally minimize and maximize each selected variable over the exact feasible region. The resulting interval hull is the tightest enclosing axis-aligned box, or infeasibility fathoms the node.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is compact and all constraint functions are continuous.
Each auxiliary optimization problem is solved to global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(F\ne\varnothing\), then \(F\subseteq B'\subseteq B\) and no smaller valid coordinate interval contains the projection of \(F\).

notation.meaning: exact feasible region in the current box
exact extrema of coordinate i over F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-extremization construction is standard, but no source supports the exact-OBBT terminology. Moreover, the interval-hull optimality claim applies to the complete axis-aligned hull only when both endpoints of every coordinate are optimized; with selected coordinates it must be restricted to the selected endpoints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp soundness requirements for relaxation-based coordinate contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Provided \(F\subseteq R\), a relaxation-derived lower endpoint is sound when \(\underline v_i\le\inf_{x\in R}x_i\), and an upper endpoint is sound when \(\overline v_i\ge\sup_{x\in R}x_i\). If outer containment fails or a bound is certified on the wrong side, the contracted interval need not contain \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound relaxation OBBT requires an outer relaxation and outward-valid bounds on its coordinate extrema.
assumptions_latex: The intended retained set is \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq R,\ \underline v_i\le\inf_Rx_i,\ \overline v_i\ge\sup_Rx_i\implies F\subseteq\{x:\underline v_i\le x_i\le\overline v_i\}.

notation.meaning: certified outward bounds on relaxation extrema

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Containment and Bound-Direction Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison using complete coordinate hulls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F\subseteq R\), then \(H(F)\subseteq H(R)\). Equality holds exactly when every coordinate has the same infimum and supremum over \(F\) and \(R\), even when \(F\ne R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact feasible-set interval hull is never weaker than the hull of an outer relaxation.
assumptions_latex: All coordinate extrema used in the hulls are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq R\implies H(F)\subseteq H(R).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact OBBT Dominates Relaxation OBBT

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of exact coordinate ranges from nested valid outer relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F\subseteq R_2\subseteq R_1\), then \(\inf_{R_1}x_i\le\inf_{R_2}x_i\le\inf_Fx_i\) and \(\sup_Fx_i\le\sup_{R_2}x_i\le\sup_{R_1}x_i\) for every coordinate. Hence \(H(R_2)\subseteq H(R_1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested tighter outer relaxation gives coordinate bounds at least as strong as a weaker relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The relevant extrema are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq R_2\subseteq R_1\implies H(R_2)\subseteq H(R_1).
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity with Relaxation Strength
Relaxation-Based OBBT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe coordinate tightening by optimizing over an outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq B=[\ell,u]\) be the exact node-feasible set and let \(R\) be a tractable relaxation satisfying \(F\subseteq R\subseteq B\). For each selected coordinate \(i\), compute valid bounds \(\underline v_i\le\inf_{x\in R}x_i\) and \(\overline v_i\ge\sup_{x\in R}x_i\), using exact relaxation optima when available. Set \(\ell'_i=\max\{\ell_i,\underline v_i\}\) and \(u'_i=\min\{u_i,\overline v_i\}\), retaining unselected bounds. If \(R=\varnothing\) or some \(\ell'_i>u'_i\), declare the node infeasible; otherwise output \(B'=[\ell',u']\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize variables over an outer relaxation and intersect the resulting valid ranges with the current box. Empty relaxation or inconsistent bounds safely certify node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq B\).
Optimization outputs are valid lower and upper bounds for the relaxation extrema.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(F=\varnothing\), or \(F\subseteq B'\subseteq B\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outer-relaxation inclusions and directions of the valid extrema bounds give a sound reduction, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the relaxation-based OBBT formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between match-or-improve and fixed-margin improvement cutoffs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the cutoff \(f(x)\le\bar f-\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon=0\) retains feasible points tied with the incumbent, whereas \(\varepsilon>0\) requires improvement by at least \(\varepsilon\). Strict improvement without a fixed margin is expressed by \(f(x)<\bar f\), not by the non-strict zero-margin cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-margin non-strict cutoff retains ties; a positive margin requires a specified improvement.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(\bar f,0)=\{x\in F:f(x)\le\bar f\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Tie-Retention Convention

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cutoff Emptiness Is Not Original Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical meaning of an infeasible incumbent-cutoff auxiliary region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: It is possible that \(F\ne\varnothing\) while \(C(\bar f,\varepsilon)=\varnothing\). Thus certified cutoff-set emptiness proves only that no feasible point satisfies \(f(x)\le\bar f-\varepsilon\), not that the original node is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty cutoff problem certifies absence of a sufficiently improving point, not absence of every feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar f\) is a valid feasible incumbent value.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(\bar f,\varepsilon)=\varnothing\centernot\implies F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutoff Emptiness Is Not Original Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of lowering the cutoff threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(C(\bar f,\varepsilon)=\{x\in F:f(x)\le\bar f-\varepsilon\}\). If \(\bar f_2-\varepsilon_2\le\bar f_1-\varepsilon_1\), then \(C(\bar f_2,\varepsilon_2)\subseteq C(\bar f_1,\varepsilon_1)\), and their exact interval hulls have the same inclusion whenever both sets are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower cutoff threshold retains a subset of the points retained by a higher threshold, so its exact interval hull cannot be wider.
assumptions_latex: The same feasible set and objective are used.
Both compared cutoff sets are nonempty when their hulls are invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar f_2-\varepsilon_2\le\bar f_1-\varepsilon_1\implies H(C(\bar f_2,\varepsilon_2))\subseteq H(C(\bar f_1,\varepsilon_1)).
knowledge_statements.title: Cutoff-Set Monotonicity
Incumbent-Cutoff OBBT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: OBBT restricted to solutions capable of improving a known incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of \(f(x)\) over the node-feasible set \(F\subseteq B\), and let \(\bar f\) be an incumbent objective value. Choose a strict-improvement tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and define \(F_{\bar f}=\{x\in F:f(x)\le\bar f-\varepsilon\}\), or an outer relaxation of this set. Minimize and maximize every selected \(x_i\) over that cutoff set and intersect the resulting valid coordinate ranges with \(B\). If the cutoff set or its outer relaxation is certified empty, fathom the node because it contains no solution improving the incumbent by \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add an incumbent objective cutoff before bound tightening. The reduced box retains every sufficiently improving feasible point, while an empty cutoff relaxation permits safe node fathoming.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with valid incumbent value \(\bar f\).
The auxiliary feasible region contains every point in \(F_{\bar f}\).
All returned coordinate bounds are valid for that auxiliary region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output box contains \(F_{\bar f}\); certified emptiness implies \(F_{\bar f}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: feasible points meeting the incumbent cutoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cutoff construction is sound, including when an outer relaxation is used, but a source is required for this OBBT variant and its improvement convention. In particular, epsilon equal to zero retains incumbent ties and therefore is not a strict-improvement cutoff.

children.title: Selective OBBT
children.top_down_role: OBBT restricted to chosen variables, constraints, or search regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle count for a prescribed set of lower and upper endpoint targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{L,U\}\), separately processing every selected endpoint requires at most \(|T|\) auxiliary optimization solves, compared with \(2n\) for all endpoints. Reuse can reduce this count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selective OBBT uses at most one separate auxiliary solve per selected endpoint.
assumptions_latex: Each non-reused selected endpoint is handled by one auxiliary problem.
Repeated passes are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{aux}}\le|T|\le2n.
knowledge_statements.title: Selective OBBT Auxiliary-Solve Count

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Soundness Is Independent of Target Completeness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of processing any prescribed subset of endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq B\). For any target set \(T\), intersecting targeted endpoints with valid bounds for \(R\) and leaving all other endpoints unchanged yields \(F\subseteq B_T\subseteq B\). Omitting a target can weaken contraction but cannot by itself invalidate the reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any subset of endpoints may be processed soundly; selection affects strength and cost, not validity, when every imposed bound is certified.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R\subseteq B\).
Every imposed endpoint bound is valid for \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq B_T\subseteq B.

notation.meaning: box after processing target set T

knowledge_statements.title: Soundness Is Independent of Target Completeness
Selective OBBT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: OBBT applied only to a chosen subset of variable-bound targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a box \(B=[\ell,u]\), an outer relaxation \(R\subseteq B\) containing the relevant feasible set, and a selected target set \(T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{L,U\}\), solve only the auxiliary problems indicated by \(T\): minimize \(x_i\) for \((i,L)\in T\) and maximize \(x_i\) for \((i,U)\in T\). Intersect each resulting valid bound with \([\ell_i,u_i]\); leave every untargeted endpoint unchanged. Stop after processing \(T\), or earlier if an auxiliary problem certifies \(R=\varnothing\). Output the reduced box or an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run only chosen lower- or upper-bound auxiliary problems. Valid targeted improvements preserve all relevant feasible points, while untargeted endpoints remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The relevant feasible set is contained in \(R\subseteq B\).
Every computed auxiliary bound is valid for \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced box contains the relevant feasible set and changes only endpoints indexed by \(T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selective-endpoint algorithm is mathematically sound and fits the terminal container, but no source with a specific locator supports this formulation of selective OBBT.

children.title: Adaptive OBBT
children.top_down_role: OBBT whose effort changes in response to search progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive OBBT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback-controlled revision of OBBT targets or effort during the solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At solver state \(s_k\), let a policy \(\pi\) choose an OBBT configuration \(a_k=\pi(s_k)\), specifying target endpoints, relaxation strength, tolerances, and resource limits. Apply the corresponding sound OBBT operator to the current box \(B_k\), obtaining \(B_{k+1}\subseteq B_k\) or an infeasibility certificate. Record observable outcomes such as bound improvement and computational cost, update \(s_{k+1}\), and repeat while the policy requests further work. Stop when infeasibility is certified, the policy rejects all actions, or the prescribed OBBT budget is exhausted; output the last box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feedback policy changes OBBT targets and effort using observed tightening and cost. Each chosen operator remains sound, so adaptation cannot remove relevant feasible points.
assumptions_latex: Every OBBT configuration selected by \(\pi\) uses a valid outer relaxation and valid auxiliary bounds.
The initial box contains the relevant feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every non-infeasible output \(B_k\) contains the relevant feasible set and satisfies \(B_{k+1}\subseteq B_k\).

notation.meaning: observable solver state at stage k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic feedback scheme preserves soundness when every selected OBBT operator is sound, but no source establishes this framework as an adaptive-OBBT algorithm family or supports the listed configuration dimensions and stopping rules.

children.title: OBBT Target Selection
children.top_down_role: Criteria for choosing variables or nodes for tightening.

knowledge_statements.title: OBBT Target Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A budgeted score-based rule for selecting variable-bound OBBT subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{L,U\}\) be the available bound endpoints. At solver state \(s\), assign each endpoint \(e\in E\) a nonnegative priority score \(q_e(s)\) and a positive estimated processing cost \(c_e(s)\). Given a budget \(C\ge 0\), one budgeted target-selection rule chooses any set \(T\) satisfying \[T\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{S\subseteq E}\left\{\sum_{e\in S}q_e(s):\sum_{e\in S}c_e(s)\le C\right\}.\] Only endpoints in \(T\) are submitted to the subsequent OBBT step. This is one possible selection policy and is not required for OBBT soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One target-selection policy chooses the variable endpoints having maximum total priority under an estimated processing-cost budget. This policy controls effort but is not a universal requirement for valid OBBT.
assumptions_latex: \(q_e(s)\ge 0\) for every \(e\in E\).
\(c_e(s)>0\) for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected set \(T\) satisfies \(\sum_{e\in T}c_e(s)\le C\).

notation.meaning: priority score for endpoint e at state s
estimated processing cost for endpoint e at state s

children.title: OBBT Effort Escalation
children.top_down_role: Policies governing increases or reductions in tightening effort.

knowledge_statements.title: OBBT Effort Escalation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone escalation through increasingly costly valid OBBT configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix configurations \(a_1,\ldots,a_p\) with nondecreasing resource limits or relaxation strength. Starting from \(B_0\), apply configuration \(a_r\) to obtain a sound reduction \(B_r\subseteq B_{r-1}\) or an infeasibility certificate. After stage \(r\), escalate to \(a_{r+1}\) only if a prescribed trigger holds, such as insufficient bound improvement, unresolved relaxation weakness, or favorable predicted benefit relative to cost. Stop upon infeasibility, adequate tightening, exhaustion of the total budget, or completion of stage \(p\). Return the last nonempty box and the stage outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply progressively stronger or costlier OBBT configurations when explicit triggers justify them. Soundness at every stage preserves feasible points despite changing effort.
assumptions_latex: Each configuration defines a sound OBBT operator on its input box.
The escalation order and stopping triggers are fixed before each decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned box contains the relevant feasible set and is nested within \(B_0\).

notation.meaning: OBBT configuration at escalation stage r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The staged algorithm is sound under its assumptions and fits the terminal container, but the escalation family, ordering criteria, and trigger examples lack an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Contractors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound box-reduction operators implemented with validated interval operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the solution set of a fixed constraint system. An interval contractor is a map \(C\) from axis-aligned boxes to axis-aligned boxes, allowing the empty box, such that for every input box \(B\), \[S\cap B\subseteq C(B)\subseteq B.\] The map is implemented using inclusion-valid interval operations, such as interval evaluation, inverse propagation, or interval Newton steps. If \(C(B)=\varnothing\), then \(S\cap B=\varnothing\). A contractor is idempotent when \(C(C(B))=C(B)\), but idempotence is not required for soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval contractor maps each box to a contained box while retaining every solution of the fixed constraint system lying in the input box. An empty contracted box certifies that the input box has no solution.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the solution set of a fixed constraint system.
Every interval operation used to implement \(C\) is inclusion-valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every box \(B\), \(S\cap B\subseteq C(B)\subseteq B\), and \(C(B)=\varnothing\) implies \(S\cap B=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: solution set of the fixed constraint system

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Interval Methods for Global Optimization p. 47

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal box-valued contractor associated with a solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define \(C^*(B)=\operatorname{hull}(S\cap B)\), with \(C^*(B)=\varnothing\) if \(S\cap B=\varnothing\). Then \(C^*\) is idempotent and every interval contractor \(C\) for \(S\) satisfies \(C^*(B)\subseteq C(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interval hull of all solutions in the input box is the strongest possible box-valued contractor and is idempotent.
assumptions_latex: Contractor outputs are axis-aligned boxes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C^*(C^*(B))=C^*(B),\qquad C^*(B)\subseteq C(B).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Interval-Hull Contractor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed algebra of multiple contractor applications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C_1,C_2\) are interval contractors for \(S\), then \(C_2\circ C_1\) and the box intersection \(C_1(B)\cap C_2(B)\) preserve \(S\cap B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composition and intersection preserve contractor soundness.
assumptions_latex: \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) preserve \(S\) on every input box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\cap B\subseteq(C_2\circ C_1)(B),\qquad S\cap B\subseteq C_1(B)\cap C_2(B).
knowledge_statements.title: Closure Under Composition and Intersection

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf contains the preservation definition, exact interval-hull representation, idempotence distinction, and empty-box test. The proposed composition record is sound but deferred to Composite Contractor Schedules. Particular algorithms and scheduling policies are excluded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas Certificate for Empty Linear Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual certificate validating an empty linear-relaxation contractor output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), if \(y\ge0\), \(A^Ty=0\), and \(b^Ty<0\), then \(P=\varnothing\). If the original regional feasible set satisfies \(F\subseteq P\), the same vector certifies \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorously checked Farkas multiplier certifies that the polyhedral relaxation, and hence the contained original feasible set, is empty.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P\).
The multiplier relations are verified rigorously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\ge0,\ A^Ty=0,\ b^Ty<0\Longrightarrow P=\varnothing\Longrightarrow F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Certificate for Empty Linear Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for inexact coordinate extrema used in contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To raise a lower bound safely, \(\widehat L_i\le\inf_{x\in P}x_i\) is required; to lower an upper bound safely, \(\widehat U_i\ge\sup_{x\in P}x_i\) is required. A value on the opposite side of either extremum can remove points of \(P\) and therefore feasible points of \(F\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate LP coordinate bounds must be outward-valid; wrong-side bounds can delete feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P\subseteq B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat L_i\le\inf_Px_i,\qquad \widehat U_i\ge\sup_Px_i\text{ are sufficient validity directions.}
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe LP Bound Direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of exact coordinate contractions from nested polyhedral outer relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq P_1\subseteq P_2\subseteq B\), and let \(C_{P_j}\) use exact coordinate extrema over \(P_j\). Then \(\inf_{P_1}x_i\ge\inf_{P_2}x_i\) and \(\sup_{P_1}x_i\le\sup_{P_2}x_i\), hence \(C_{P_1}(B)\subseteq C_{P_2}(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tighter nested polyhedral relaxation gives coordinate contraction at least as strong as a looser relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are nonempty.
The coordinate extrema used are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_1\subseteq P_2\Longrightarrow C_{P_1}(B)\subseteq C_{P_2}(B).
knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Relaxation Contraction Dominance
Linear-Relaxation Contractors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box contraction obtained by bounding coordinate extrema over a valid linear outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq B=[\ell,u]\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(P=\{x\in B:Ax\le b\}\) satisfy \(F\subseteq P\). For each selected coordinate \(i\), obtain valid numbers \(\underline v_i\) and \(\overline v_i\) such that \(\underline v_i\le\inf_{x\in P}x_i\) and \(\overline v_i\ge\sup_{x\in P}x_i\); exact linear-programming optima may be used.
