Define \(C_P(B)\) by replacing the selected interval with \([\max\{\ell_i,\underline v_i\},\min\{u_i,\overline v_i\}]\) and leaving unselected bounds unchanged. If \(P\) is certified empty, set \(C_P(B)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear-relaxation contractor obtains outward-valid coordinate bounds from a polyhedral outer relaxation and intersects them with the current box. Certified infeasibility of the relaxation yields an empty contractor output.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P\subseteq B\).
Each reported lower bound is no greater than the corresponding relaxation infimum.
Each reported upper bound is no less than the corresponding relaxation supremum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq C_P(B)\subseteq B\), and \(P=\varnothing\) implies \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: outward-valid bounds on coordinate extrema over P

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local consistency of one continuous constraint over interval variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constraint relation \(R_c\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and box \(D\), let \(H_c(D)=\operatorname{hull}(R_c\cap D)\). The box \(D\) is hull-consistent for \(c\) exactly when \(H_c(D)=D\). Every sound box-valued contractor \(C_c\) for this constraint satisfies \(H_c(D)\subseteq C_c(D)\subseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box is hull-consistent for one constraint when it equals the interval hull of that constraint's feasible tuples. The exact hull is the strongest sound box-valued contraction.
assumptions_latex: Contractor outputs are axis-aligned boxes.
Every tuple in \(R_c\cap D\) is preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_c(D)=D\iff D\text{ is hull-consistent for }c,\qquad H_c(D)\subseteq C_c(D)\subseteq D.

notation.meaning: exact hull contractor for constraint c

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Wise Hull Consistency
Constraint-Programming Contractors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-consistency operators for continuous constraints represented by interval domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let variables have interval domains \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_n)\) and let \(c\) be a constraint with relation \(R_c\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). A constraint-programming contractor for \(c\) is an operator \(C_c\) satisfying \(C_c(D)_i\subseteq D_i\) for every \(i\) and \(R_c\cap(D_1\times\cdots\times D_n)\subseteq C_c(D)_1\times\cdots\times C_c(D)_n\). It may enforce a chosen local consistency by projection and propagation. If any output domain is empty, the original domain box contains no tuple satisfying \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint-programming contractor shrinks interval variable domains while preserving every tuple satisfying its constraint. An empty output domain certifies that the current box violates that constraint.
assumptions_latex: Each variable domain \(D_i\) is an interval.
The propagation rule is sound for the constraint relation \(R_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every solution of \(c\) in the input domain box remains in the contracted domain box; an empty component proves local infeasibility.

notation.meaning: current interval domain of variable i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The preservation property is a sound contractor definition and fits the continuous constraint-programming container. An inspectable source is required to support the terminology and its relationship to local-consistency propagation over interval domains.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Consistency Does Not Imply Joint Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed failure boundary for propagation across multiple constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed example claims that both exact hull contractors leave the box unchanged although the constraints are jointly infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated claim is false because }\operatorname{hull}(R_{c_2}\cap D)=\{(1,1)\}\ne D.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Consistency Does Not Imply Joint Feasibility

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is the solution-preserving single-constraint contractor, exact hull consistency, strongest-box characterization, and empty-domain test. The incorrect proposed counterexample is deferred. Interval arithmetic implementations, linear relaxations, multi-constraint scheduling, and composite schedules are excluded to sibling leaves.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven composite scheduling that reruns contractors affected by tightened bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Q\leftarrow\{1,\ldots,m\}.\text{ While }Q\ne\varnothing,\text{ remove }i,\ X\leftarrow C_i(X),\text{ return }\varnothing\text{ if }X=\varnothing,\text{ and reinsert every contractor whose inputs may be affected by coordinates tightened by }C_i.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a dependency worklist to rerun sound contractors whenever relevant bounds change, stopping at quiescence, infeasibility, or a prescribed budget.
assumptions_latex: Every C_i is contracting and solution-preserving.
Dependency information conservatively includes every contractor affected by a changed coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\in X_0:F(x)\}\subseteq X_{\mathrm{returned}}\subseteq X_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Worklist Contractor Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order dependence of finite or early-stopped composite contractor schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: C_2(C_1(X))\text{ and }C_1(C_2(X))\text{ are both sound for sound contracting }C_1,C_2,\text{ but may differ or be incomparable. Without further commutativity, idempotence, and common-fixed-point conditions, neither one-pass result must equal propagation quiescence.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different contractor orders remain sound but can produce different boxes, and one sweep need not reach propagation quiescence.
assumptions_latex: C_1 and C_2 are contracting and solution-preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_2(C_1(X))\text{ and }C_1(C_2(X))\text{ may be incomparable while both preserve every target solution in }X.
knowledge_statements.title: Schedule Order Affects Contraction Strength
Composite Contractor Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential composition of sound domain contractors at one branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a node box \(X\), constraints \(F\), and sound contractors \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), initialize \(X^{(0)}=X\). For sweep \(r=0,1,\ldots\), apply a prescribed schedule \(i_{r,1},\ldots,i_{r,q_r}\) by \(X^{(r,j)}=C_{i_{r,j}}(X^{(r,j-1)};F)\), with \(X^{(r,0)}=X^{(r)}\), and set \(X^{(r+1)}=X^{(r,q_r)}\). Stop when \(X^{(r+1)}=\varnothing\), the relative width decrease is at most \(\tau\), or \(r+1=R\). Return \(X^{(r+1)}\). Soundness means every feasible point of the input box remains in each contracted box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply several sound contractors in a fixed or adaptive order until infeasibility, negligible shrinkage, or a sweep limit; their composition preserves every feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a box.
Each \(C_i\) is contracting and feasibility-preserving.
\(\tau\ge 0\) and \(R\in\mathbb N\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in X:F(x)\text{ holds}\}\subseteq X^{(r+1)}\subseteq X\).

notation.meaning: a chosen scalar width measure for a box

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Composite Contractor Schedules container, but no citation supports the particular sweep schedule, relative-width stopping rule, or budgeted variant. The scalar relative-width decrease is also invoked without being explicitly defined in the statement.

children.title: Root Reduction
children.top_down_role: Domain reduction concentrated before substantial tree exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Root Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain reduction performed once before the initial branching operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a constrained minimization problem over the initial box \(X_0\), initialize \(Y_0=X_0\). Apply a sound reduction operator \(R\) repeatedly by \(Y_{k+1}=R(Y_k;\bar f)\), where \(\bar f\) is the current incumbent value, until \(Y_{k+1}=\varnothing\), \(\operatorname{wid}(Y_k)-\operatorname{wid}(Y_{k+1})\le \tau\operatorname{wid}(Y_k)\), or \(k+1=K\). If the result is empty, certify root infeasibility or cutoff; otherwise use the final box as the root of the search tree and perform no further reduction under this policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contract the initial domain to a fixed point or budget limit before branching, then use the reduced box as the search-tree root.
assumptions_latex: \(X_0\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a box containing the original feasible region.
\(R\) preserves every feasible point whose objective is below \(\bar f\).
\(\tau\ge0\) and \(K\in\mathbb N\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned root \(Y\) satisfies \(\{x\in X_0:x\text{ feasible},\ f(x)<\bar f\}\subseteq Y\subseteq X_0\).

source_refs.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

source_witnesses.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record is mathematically plausible and algorithm is the appropriate kind, but the cited general-algorithm section has not been shown to support repeated root reduction followed by a policy of no descendant reduction. That policy-specific claim requires source confirmation.

children.title: Per-Node Reduction
children.top_down_role: Domain reduction invoked throughout node processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Node Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound domain reduction applied independently whenever a search-tree node is processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When a live node with box \(X_v\) is selected, set \(Y_{v,0}=X_v\) and iterate \(Y_{v,k+1}=R(Y_{v,k};\bar f)\) until emptiness, a prescribed contraction tolerance, or a local budget is reached. Prune node \(v\) if \(Y_{v,k+1}=\varnothing\) or a valid lower bound on \(Y_{v,k+1}\) is at least \(\bar f\). Otherwise compute bounds and branch using the final reduced box. Reapply this procedure at every subsequently selected child, using the incumbent available when that child is processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every selected node, contract its box using the current incumbent; prune it when empty or cutoff-dominated, and otherwise bound and branch the reduced box.
assumptions_latex: Each node box \(X_v\subset\mathbb R^n\) contains its represented subproblem.
\(R\) preserves feasible points with objective below \(\bar f\).
Node lower bounds are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No point capable of improving \(\bar f\) is removed from an unpruned node or lost by a valid pruning decision.

source_refs.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

source_witnesses.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

children.title: Root-to-Tree Reduction Transfer
children.top_down_role: Propagation of root-level reductions into descendant search states.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-to-Tree Reduction Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance of a soundly reduced root domain by every descendant node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_0\subseteq X_0\) be obtained by a sound root reduction, and construct every descendant box solely by partitioning its parent and applying sound contractors. Then each descendant box \(X_v\) satisfies \(X_v\subseteq Y_0\). Moreover, every point in \(X_0\setminus Y_0\) was already certified infeasible or unable to improve the root cutoff, so it need not be reconsidered at descendants. Root-derived constraints or variable bounds may be transferred to all descendants only while their validity conditions, including any cutoff used to derive them, remain satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Descendants inherit the reduced root domain and globally valid deductions; cutoff-dependent deductions transfer only while their original validity conditions remain true.
assumptions_latex: The root reduction is sound for the stated cutoff.
Children are formed by subsets of their parents.
Every later contractor is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every descendant \(v\), \(X_v\subseteq Y_0\subseteq X_0\), and no improving feasible point excluded at the root is required later.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inheritance statement is plausible under the stated subset and soundness assumptions, and property is the correct kind. No source is supplied for transferring root deductions, especially deductions whose validity depends on an incumbent cutoff.

children.title: Per-Node Cost Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Tree regimes where repeated reduction costs outweigh pruning gains.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Node Cost Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A break-even condition for activating optional reduction at a search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), let \(c_v\ge0\) be the expected cost of reduction, \(p_v\in[0,1]\) the probability that reduction immediately prunes the node, \(s_v\ge0\) the expected downstream work saved conditional on immediate pruning, and \(d_v\ge0\) the expected additional work saved by contraction when the node survives. Under an additive expected-work model, activate reduction exactly when \(p_vs_v+(1-p_v)d_v>c_v\); equality is the break-even boundary. A hard local budget \(B_v\) additionally requires \(c_v\le B_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run node reduction when its expected avoided downstream work exceeds its expected cost and the reduction fits the node’s local budget.
assumptions_latex: The cost and savings estimates are finite and conditional on information available at node \(v\).
Expected work is additive under the scheduling model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reduction is cost-favorable precisely when \(p_vs_v+(1-p_v)d_v-c_v>0\), subject to \(c_v\le B_v\).

notation.meaning: expected reduction cost at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The break-even inequality is correct under the explicitly assumed additive model and condition fits the container, but the quantities and decomposition form a local decision model with no supporting source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Periodic Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction activated at fixed node, depth, or time intervals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional invocation count for the processed-node indexing convention proposed in the deferred periodic policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For indices \(t=0,\ldots,N-1\), period \(q\ge1\), and offset \(r\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\), the number of indices satisfying \(t\equiv r\pmod q\) is \[A_N=\begin{cases}0,&N\le r,\\1+\left\lfloor\dfrac{N-1-r}{q}\right\rfloor,&N>r.\end{cases}\] Consequently \(A_N\le\lceil N/q\rceil\). If each invoked reduction costs at most \(C_R\), then \(W_R(N)\le A_NC_R\le\lceil N/q\rceil C_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated processed-node convention, a period-q schedule activates at most ceiling(N/q) times among N states.
assumptions_latex: N\in\mathbb N_0.
q\in\mathbb N,\ q\ge1.
r\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}.
Each activation costs at most C_R\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_N\le\lceil N/q\rceil\quad\text{and}\quad W_R(N)\le\lceil N/q\rceil C_R.

notation.meaning: number of scheduled activations among the first N indexed states

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Activation Count
Periodic Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction activated at a fixed frequency during node processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer period \(q\ge1\) and an offset \(r\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\). Number processed search-tree nodes by \(t=0,1,\ldots\). Before bounding or branching node \(v_t\), invoke a sound reduction operator if and only if \(t\equiv r\pmod q\); otherwise process its current domain unchanged. An invoked reduction terminates at emptiness, a contraction tolerance, or its local work budget. An empty reduced domain is pruned, while a nonempty reduced domain replaces the node domain for subsequent bounding and branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invoke sound domain reduction every fixed number of processed nodes, respecting a local stopping budget, and continue search from the contracted domain.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb N\) with \(q\ge1\).
The reduction operator is sound.
Node processing has a deterministic sequence index \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reduction is invoked exactly on \(\{t:t\equiv r\pmod q\}\), without excluding any feasible improving point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The modular activation rule is a coherent periodic scheduling algorithm, but no citation establishes this processed-node indexing variant, its offset convention, or its placement before bounding or branching.

children.title: Stagnation-Triggered Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction activated after insufficient bound, incumbent, or domain progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation-Triggered Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction activated after insufficient bound or domain progress over a finite observation window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For processed node states indexed by \(t\), choose a window \(w\ge1\), tolerances \(\epsilon_b,\epsilon_x\ge0\), and cooldown \(h\ge0\). Define bound progress \(\Delta_b(t)=L_t-L_{t-w}\) and relative domain progress \(\Delta_x(t)=1-\operatorname{wid}(X_t)/\operatorname{wid}(X_{t-w})\). If \(\Delta_b(t)\le\epsilon_b\) and \(\Delta_x(t)\le\epsilon_x\), and at least \(h\) states have elapsed since the previous activation, invoke sound reduction. Stop reduction at emptiness, sufficient contraction, or its work budget; otherwise continue ordinary node processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trigger reduction when both bound improvement and domain shrinkage remain below calibrated thresholds over a window, subject to a cooldown.
assumptions_latex: Comparable states \(t-w\) and \(t\) have finite lower bounds and positive widths.
\(w\ge1\), \(h\ge0\), and both tolerances are nonnegative.
The invoked reduction is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An activation occurs only when the stated stagnation predicate and cooldown condition both hold.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound at state t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The candidate gives a coherent algorithm, but the joint bound-and-width stagnation predicate, window comparison, and cooldown convention are policy-specific and unsupported. A source is needed to determine the intended mathematical variant.

children.title: Reduction Trigger Calibration
children.top_down_role: Selection of cadence or stagnation thresholds for reduction activation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empirical Trigger Calibration Need Not Minimize Population Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample boundary for interpreting an empirically selected trigger parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta=\{a,b\}\), let the workload assign probability \(1/2\) to each of \(I_1,I_2\), and choose \(M>2\) with \[W(a,I_1)=0,\quad W(a,I_2)=M,\quad W(b,I_1)=W(b,I_2)=1.\] A training sample containing only \(I_1\) uniquely selects \(a\), although \(\mathbb E[W(a,I)]=M/2>1=\mathbb E[W(b,I)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trigger can be empirically best on the training instances yet worse in expected work on the target workload.
assumptions_latex: I_1 and I_2 each have population probability 1/2.
The realized training sample contains only I_1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\widehat W(\theta)\quad\text{but}\quad a\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E[W(\theta,I)].

notation.meaning: work of parameter choice theta on instance I
large work incurred on the unobserved instance type

knowledge_statements.title: Empirical Trigger Calibration Need Not Minimize Population Work
Reduction Trigger Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical selection of trigger parameters by minimizing total expected solver work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be a finite set of admissible trigger parameters and \(\mathcal I\) a calibration distribution of problem instances. For \(\theta\in\Theta\), define capped work \(W(\theta,I)=\min\{T(\theta,I),T_{\max}\}+\lambda N_R(\theta,I)\), where \(T\) is measured solver work and \(N_R\) counts reduction activations. Select \(\hat\theta\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}|\mathcal S|^{-1}\sum_{I\in\mathcal S}W(\theta,I)\) on a training sample \(\mathcal S\), then report performance on disjoint validation instances. Calibration must not alter contractor soundness or pruning validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose trigger thresholds on training instances to minimize capped solver work plus reduction overhead, then evaluate the fixed choice on separate validation instances.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) is finite and all runs use a common work measure and cap.
Training and validation instances are disjoint samples from the intended workload.
Every calibrated policy retains sound reduction and pruning rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat\theta\) minimizes empirical penalized work over \(\Theta\); calibration changes efficiency parameters but not correctness conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The empirical calibration principle is internally coherent, but the capped penalized objective and train-validation protocol are locally chosen and have no citation. The source uncertainty concerns the exact calibration formulation rather than only exposition.

children.title: Trigger Thrashing Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Excessive reduction caused by unstable or oversensitive activation signals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activation-count bound under an explicit cooldown convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(N\) decision states indexed by \(0,\ldots,N-1\). If at least \(h\ge0\) nonactivation states occur between consecutive activations, then consecutive activation indices differ by at least \(h+1\), and \[A_N\le\begin{cases}0,&N=0,\\1+\left\lfloor\dfrac{N-1}{h+1}\right\rfloor,&N\ge1,\end{cases}=\left\lceil\dfrac{N}{h+1}\right\rceil.\] If each activation costs at most \(C_R\), then \(W_R(N)\le\lceil N/(h+1)\rceil C_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring h nonactivation states between activations limits their number among N states to ceiling(N/(h+1)).
assumptions_latex: N\in\mathbb N_0.
h\in\mathbb N_0.
At least h nonactivation decision states separate consecutive activations.
Each activation costs at most C_R\ge0 for the work bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_N\le\left\lceil\frac{N}{h+1}\right\rceil\quad\text{and}\quad W_R(N)\le\left\lceil\frac{N}{h+1}\right\rceil C_R.

notation.meaning: required nonactivation states between consecutive activations
activation count among N decision states

knowledge_statements.title: Cooldown Activation Bound
Trigger Thrashing Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A failure regime where repeated triggers consume work without commensurate domain or bound progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each reduction activation costs at least \(c_{min}>0\), and an activation is called ineffective when it produces width decrease below \(\delta_x\) and lower-bound increase below \(\delta_b\). If the trigger has no cooldown and its predicate remains true after an ineffective activation, then it may reactivate at every subsequent decision state. Over \(m\) such states the excess reduction work is at least \(mc_{min}\), while certified progress remains below \(m\delta_x\) in accumulated width decrease and \(m\delta_b\) in accumulated bound increase. A positive cooldown or hysteresis condition excludes immediate reactivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without cooldown or hysteresis, an unchanged trigger can repeatedly launch ineffective reductions, causing linear overhead with negligible contraction or bound improvement.
assumptions_latex: Every activation costs at least \(c_{min}>0\).
The trigger predicate can remain true after ineffective reduction.
No cooldown or state-changing hysteresis is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(m\) consecutive ineffective activations, overhead is at least \(mc_{min}\); imposing a positive cooldown prevents activation at every decision state.

notation.meaning: minimum work cost per reduction activation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct role, but the claimed thrashing bounds rely on policy-dependent progress measures, and the assertion about a positive cooldown depends on an unstated counting convention. No source is provided for this model.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Aware Reduction Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online scheduling that activates reduction only when predicted savings justify its computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each eligible node \(v\), estimate reduction cost \(\hat c_v\), immediate-pruning probability \(\hat p_v\), saving after pruning \(\hat s_v\), and saving from contraction without pruning \(\hat d_v\). Form \(G_v=\hat p_v\hat s_v+(1-\hat p_v)\hat d_v-\hat c_v\). Invoke sound reduction when \(G_v>\eta\) and its cumulative cost remains within budget \(B\); otherwise proceed directly to bounding or branching. After observing the reduction outcome and realized cost, update the estimators. Terminate each invocation at emptiness, its contraction tolerance, or a local cost limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate each reduction’s net work savings, invoke it only above a margin and within budget, and update estimates from observed outcomes.
assumptions_latex: All estimates use information available before the activation decision.
The invoked reduction operator is sound.
\(B\ge0\) and decision margin \(\eta\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scheduler activates node \(v\) only if \(G_v>\eta\) and the remaining reduction budget covers \(\hat c_v\).

notation.meaning: predicted net work saving at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed scheduler fits the topic and algorithm kind, but its gain estimator, activation margin, budget accounting, and online estimator updates constitute an unsupported custom algorithm. A source is required for the exact formulation.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
\(x'\) is feasible and \(U'=f(x')\).
Every \(L_v\) is a valid lower bound on its node.
Every cutoff contractor preserves all feasible points satisfying \(f(x)<U'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\ge U'\Rightarrow v\) is safely prunable, and cutoff contraction preserves every feasible \(x\) with \(f(x)<U'\); the retained domains may also contain points that do not improve the incumbent.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of a new feasible objective value through all live minimization subproblems.

source_refs.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization with incumbent feasible point \(x^I\) and value \(U=f(x^I)\). After finding a feasible point \(x'\) with \(f(x')<U\), set \(U'=f(x')\) and propagate the cutoff constraint \(f(x)<U'\) to every live node. A node \(v\) with valid lower bound \(L_v\ge U'\) may be pruned. Any sound cutoff contractor may additionally remove points satisfying \(f(x)\ge U'\), provided it preserves every feasible point satisfying \(f(x)<U'\). Consequently, every feasible point that can improve the incumbent remains represented by an unpruned node, while retained domains may still contain infeasible or nonimproving points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A better incumbent tightens the global objective cutoff. Nodes whose valid lower bounds meet the cutoff may be pruned, and sound cutoff contraction preserves every feasible improving point, although surviving domains can still contain nonimproving points.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Cutoff Propagation

source_witnesses.locator: 8.3 Global Optimization Algorithm p. 276

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality handling when incumbent cutoffs are used either to find one optimum or to retain every global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=f(x^I)\) for a verified feasible incumbent in a minimization problem, and let \(L_v\) be a valid lower bound for node \(v\). If only the optimal value or one global minimizer is required, propagating \(f(x)<U\) and pruning when \(L_v\ge U\) is sound. If every global minimizer must remain represented, equality cannot generally be discarded: propagation must preserve feasible points with \(f(x)\le U\), and lower-bound pruning requires \(L_v>U\) unless another certificate proves that the node contains no unreported minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict improving cutoff is sufficient for finding an optimal value or one optimizer, but retaining all optimal ties requires preserving equality unless another certificate excludes them.
assumptions_latex: \(x^I\) is feasible and \(U=f(x^I)\).
Every \(L_v\) is a valid node lower bound.
The pruning convention matches the requested solution-output semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{one optimizer: }L_v\ge U\text{ is admissible};\qquad \text{all optimizers: }L_v=U\text{ alone is insufficient for pruning}.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node v

knowledge_statements.title: Cutoff Strictness and Requested Output

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic node-selection policy and completeness boundary for incumbent-responsive priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), assign each live node \(v\in\mathcal A_k\) a score \(p_k(v)=\Phi(v,x_k^I,U_k)\), where \((x_k^I,U_k)\) is the current verified incumbent, and select a score-minimizing node according to a prescribed tie rule. Scores may combine bounds, depth, incumbent distance, or other heuristic information, but they justify no pruning. The completeness guarantee of the underlying branch-and-bound method is retained only if every persistently live node is eventually selected or is first removed by a sound fathoming certificate. Without this fairness property, an optimizer-containing node may be starved indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incumbent-dependent scores may reorder live nodes but cannot prune them; persistent nodes must eventually be processed or soundly fathomed to retain search completeness.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_k\) is finite at each selection event.
\((x_k^I,U_k)\) is a verified incumbent pair.
All node deletion uses independent sound fathoming certificates.
The selection policy is fair for persistently live nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\text{ persistently live}\Longrightarrow v\text{ is eventually selected or soundly fathomed};\qquad p_k(v)\text{ alone is not a pruning certificate}.

notation.meaning: current incumbent-dependent priority score of node v

knowledge_statements.title: Admissible Incumbent-Dependent Node Ordering
Incumbent-Driven Node Priorities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-first node selection biased toward regions near a current incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each live node \(v\), maintain a valid lower bound \(L_v\), a representative point \(z_v\), depth \(d_v\), and current incumbent \(x^I\) with value \(U\). Define \(P_v=L_v+\alpha\,D(z_v,x^I)-\beta d_v\), where \(D\ge0\) is a prescribed distance measure and \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\). Select a node minimizing \(P_v\), breaking ties deterministically. Whenever the incumbent changes, recompute affected priorities. Independently of priority, prune every node with \(L_v\ge U\). Priority changes processing order only and therefore does not replace valid bounding, pruning, or exhaustive-search conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank live nodes using lower bounds, distance to the incumbent, and depth; recompute after incumbent changes while retaining ordinary safe pruning rules.
assumptions_latex: The live-node set is finite at each selection event.
Each \(L_v\) is a valid node lower bound.
Tie-breaking and distance measure \(D\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A selected node lies in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_v P_v\); pruning remains valid only through \(L_v\ge U\), not through priority values.

notation.meaning: distance from a node representative to the incumbent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The priority rule is coherently presented as an algorithm and correctly separates ordering from pruning, but the affine score is a local formalization with no citation. Its effect on global-search completeness also depends on fairness or exhaustive node-processing conditions not specified here.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Solution-Pool Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent feedback from multiple feasible points in deterministic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a minimization problem over a feasible set \(F\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), and a finite pool \(P\subseteq F\), initialize the incumbent value by \(U:=\min_{x\in P}f(x)\) and retain a minimizer \(x^U\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)\). Whenever a new feasible point \(y\in F\) is found, insert it into \(P\), update \(U:=\min\{U,f(y)\}\), and select a corresponding incumbent. For every active region \(R\) having a valid lower bound \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\), fathom \(R\) when \(L(R)\ge U-\varepsilon\). Stop when no active region remains; output \(x^U\), \(U\), and the retained pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain all discovered feasible points, update the best objective value, and use that value to discard regions whose lower bounds cannot improve the incumbent beyond tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq F\) is finite and nonempty.
\(L(R)\le \inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\) for every active region \(R\).
\(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(R)\ge U-\varepsilon\Longrightarrow \inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\ge U-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: best objective value represented in the pool
valid lower bound over region R

source_refs.locator: 3.5 The Global Optimization (GOP) Algorithm p. 84

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 The Global Optimization (GOP) Algorithm p. 84

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and Cutoff Information in a Primal Pool
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information and basic update cost of an append-only feasible pool used solely for incumbent-cutoff feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite nonempty feasible pools \(P_k\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq F\), let \(U_k=\min_{x\in P_k}f(x)\). Then \(U_{k+1}\le U_k\). If downstream pruning accesses a pool only through the test \(L(R)\ge U_k-\varepsilon\), the pair consisting of \(U_k\) and one attaining pool member is sufficient for that feedback: pools with the same best value induce identical cutoff tests. With a cached incumbent, appending one evaluated feasible point and updating the best value take \(O(1)\) comparisons, while retaining all \(k\) points requires \(O(k)\) storage, excluding feasibility-check and objective-evaluation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best pool value improves monotonically and is sufficient for cutoff-only feedback; cached updates are constant-time, while retaining every point uses linear storage.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq F\) are finite and nonempty.
The downstream rule uses the pool only through its best objective value.
Objective values of inserted verified feasible points are already available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_{k+1}\le U_k,\qquad \min_{x\in P}f(x)=\min_{x\in Q}f(x)\Longrightarrow P\text{ and }Q\text{ induce the same cutoff test}.

notation.meaning: feasible solution pool after update k
best objective value represented in the pool

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Cutoff Information in a Primal Pool
Infeasibility Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of a search region by a sound infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\le 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m,\ h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,p\}\), and let \(R\subseteq X\) be a search region. An infeasibility-fathoming certificate is any finitely verifiable object \(c_R\) for which a sound verifier establishes \(F\cap R=\varnothing\). Examples include a valid relaxation of the regional constraints whose feasible set is empty, or a valid lower bound \(\ell_i(R)>0\) on some inequality function \(g_i\) throughout \(R\). Once the verifier accepts \(c_R\), deleting \(R\) from the active partition cannot delete a feasible point or a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region may be closed when a verifiable, sound certificate proves that none of its points satisfies all original constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(R\subseteq X\).
The certificate verifier is sound for the original regional constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_R\text{ accepted}\Longrightarrow F\cap R=\varnothing\).

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Infeasible Primal Problems p. 82

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Infeasible Primal Problems p. 82

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Dominance Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-bound pruning relative to the current feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization over \(F\), let \(x^U\in F\) be an incumbent with \(U=f(x^U)\), and let \(R\) be an active region. If \(L(R)\) is a certified lower bound satisfying \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\), then \(L(R)\ge U-\varepsilon\) certifies that no point in \(F\cap R\) improves the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\). Hence \(R\) may be pruned in an \(\varepsilon\)-global search. For exact pruning, take \(\varepsilon=0\); equality may be pruned when only one global minimizer is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid regional lower bound that reaches the incumbent cutoff proves that the region contains no sufficiently better feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: \(x^U\in F\) and \(U=f(x^U)\).
\(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\).
\(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(R)\ge U-\varepsilon\Longrightarrow f(x)\ge U-\varepsilon\ \text{for every }x\in F\cap R\).

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Exactness Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional closure when a relaxation optimum is feasible for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a region and let \(F_R=F\cap R\) be its original feasible set. Suppose a relaxation has feasible set \(Q_R\supseteq F_R\) and attains its minimum at \(\hat x\in Q_R\), with value \(L_R=f(\hat x)\). If \(\hat x\in F_R\), then \(L_R\) is both a valid lower bound on the original regional optimum and an attained original objective value. Consequently \(f(\hat x)=\min_{x\in F_R}f(x)\), so the region is solved exactly and may be fathomed after \(\hat x\) is submitted to the incumbent mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an optimizer of a valid regional relaxation also satisfies every original constraint, it is a regional global optimizer and the region may close.
assumptions_latex: \(F_R\subseteq Q_R\).
\(\hat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q_R}f(x)\).
\(\hat x\in F_R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\hat x)=\min_{x\in F_R}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: original feasible set restricted to region R
feasible set of the regional relaxation

children.title: Region Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Certificates supporting removal of individual search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Region Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified removal of one subregion from the unresolved domain in deterministic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) over a feasible set \(F\subseteq D\). Let \(E\subseteq D\) be proposed for exclusion, let \(K\subseteq D\setminus E\) be retained, and let \(\varepsilon\ge 0\). A region-exclusion certificate soundly verifies at least one of the following: (i) \(F\cap E=\varnothing\); (ii) an incumbent \(x^U\in F\cap K\), with \(U=f(x^U)\), and a valid bound \(L(E)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap E}f(x)\) satisfying \(L(E)\ge U-\varepsilon\); or (iii) a map \(T:F\cap E\to F\cap K\) satisfying \(f(Tx)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap E\). Alternative (ii) permits exclusion in a search requiring an \(\varepsilon\)-global solution. Alternative (iii) preserves the global minimum value and one representative minimizer, but need not preserve every minimizer. In each case the verified condition must hold throughout \(E\), so the applicable search specification permits replacing the unresolved domain by \(D\setminus E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete subregion may be removed when it is certified infeasible, unable to improve the incumbent by more than the allowed tolerance, or dominated pointwise by retained feasible points; the applicable output convention must be stated.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq D\), \(E\subseteq D\), and \(K\subseteq D\setminus E\).
\(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
The accepted predicate is sound over every feasible point in \(E\).

children.title: Region Exhaustion
children.top_down_role: Coverage-based accounting supporting completion of regional search.

knowledge_statements.title: Region Exhaustion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure by complete processing of a finite regional subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a parent region \(R\) be represented by finitely many child regions \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\) satisfying \(F\cap R\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k R_i\). Suppose each child has a valid terminal certificate showing infeasibility, incumbent dominance, exact regional solution, or replacement by further children whose union covers its feasible portion. If every resulting leaf is terminally certified and every feasible point of \(R\) belongs to at least one certified leaf, then \(R\) is exhausted. It may be removed from the active search without losing any feasible point capable of changing the required global-search output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parent region is exhausted when its children cover every feasible point and every leaf has been conclusively processed or validly replaced by covered descendants.
assumptions_latex: \(F\cap R\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k R_i\).
Every leaf certificate is sound.
The descendant subdivision is finite at certification time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\text{ exhausted}\Longrightarrow R\text{ contains no unresolved required solution}\).

notation.meaning: child regions covering the parent's feasible portion

children.title: Exclusion Coverage Accounting

knowledge_statements.title: Exclusion Coverage Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic accounting for complete certified closure of an initial domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_0\) be the initial domain, let \(A\) be the union of active regions, and let \(E_1,\ldots,E_q\) be regions carrying sound exclusion or exhaustion certificates. A coverage ledger is valid when each recorded region lies in \(D_0\), every subdivision replacement preserves coverage, and \(F\cap D_0\subseteq A\cup\bigcup_{j=1}^q E_j\). If \(A=\varnothing\), this inclusion certifies that every initially feasible point has been assigned to a closed region. Combined with the terminal meaning of each certificate, the ledger certifies completion of the search specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ledger proves completion by showing that active and certified-closed regions cover every initially feasible point, with no uncovered remainder after active regions disappear.
assumptions_latex: \(F\cap D_0\subseteq A\cup\bigcup_{j=1}^q E_j\).
Every \(E_j\) has a sound terminal certificate.
All subdivision ledger updates preserve set coverage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\varnothing\Longrightarrow F\cap D_0\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^q E_j\).

children.title: Coverage-Gap Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Unresolved regions or bookkeeping gaps that prevent exhaustion claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage-Gap Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global certification when excluded and active regions do not cover the feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_0=[0,1]\), \(F=D_0\), and \(f(x)=(x-\tfrac12)^2\). Suppose a closure ledger certifies the two regions \(E_1=[0,\tfrac13]\) and \(E_2=[\tfrac23,1]\), records no active region, but omits the gap \(G=(\tfrac13,\tfrac23)\). Then the ledger's recorded regions do not cover \(F\cap D_0\), and the unique global minimizer \(x^\star=\tfrac12\) lies in \(G\). Thus sound local certificates for all recorded regions cannot establish global completion unless coverage of the initially feasible domain is also certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even valid local closures do not prove completion when their union leaves a gap; the omitted gap may contain the global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The ledger contains only \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) as closed regions.
No active region covers \(G=(\tfrac13,\tfrac23)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap D_0\nsubseteq E_1\cup E_2\), and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)=\{\tfrac12\}\subset G\).

children.title: Dominance Pruning
children.top_down_role: Removal of regions or candidates dominated by certified alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pruning by a verified map to retained feasible points with no worse objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq D\) be a candidate region for deletion and let \(K\subseteq D\setminus E\) be retained. A dominance certificate is a verifiable map \(T:F\cap E\to F\cap K\) satisfying \(f(Tx)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap E\). Then every feasible objective value attainable in \(E\) is weakly improved by a retained feasible point. Consequently deleting \(E\) preserves the global minimum value. If all global minimizers must be enumerated, weak dominance alone is insufficient unless the output identifies equivalence classes or the inequality is strict for every deleted nonrepresentative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region can be deleted when every feasible point in it maps to a retained feasible point with no larger objective, subject to the requested output semantics.
assumptions_latex: \(T(F\cap E)\subseteq F\cap K\).
\(f(Tx)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap E\).
The task requires an optimal value or one representative minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F\cap K}f(x)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap E}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: dominance map from deleted to retained feasible points

children.title: Symmetry Pruning
children.top_down_role: Removal of search states equivalent under recognized symmetries.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-representative pruning under objective- and feasibility-preserving transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a group \(G\) act on the domain \(D\). Assume every \(g\in G\) preserves feasibility and objective value: \(x\in F\) if and only if \(gx\in F\), and \(f(gx)=f(x)\). Let \(C\subseteq D\) be a canonical set meeting every orbit in \(D\). Any region \(E\subseteq D\setminus C\) may be symmetry-pruned if a verifier supplies, for every \(x\in E\), an element \(g_x\in G\) with \(g_xx\in C\). Searching \(F\cap C\) then preserves the global optimum value and at least one representative of every feasible orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exact feasibility and objective symmetries, regions outside a canonical orbit-representative set may be removed without changing the optimal value.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) acts on \(D\) and preserves \(F\).
\(f(gx)=f(x)\) for all \(g\in G\) and \(x\in F\).
\(C\) meets every \(G\)-orbit in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F\cap C}f(x)=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: symmetry group acting on the domain
action of group element g on point x

children.title: Dominance–Symmetry Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined use of order relations and equivalence classes during pruning.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance–Symmetry Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for symmetry canonicalization followed by dominance pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) preserve the feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f\), let \(C\) meet every \(G\)-orbit, and let \(T:F\cap C\to F\cap K\) satisfy \(f(Tx)\le f(x)\) for a retained set \(K\subseteq C\). For any \(y\in F\), choose \(g_y\in G\) with \(g_yy\in C\). The composite map \(S(y)=T(g_yy)\) is feasible and satisfies \(f(S(y))\le f(y)\). Hence symmetry reduction and dominance pruning may be composed without changing the global optimum value, provided both certificates use the same feasibility and objective conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalize each symmetry orbit, then apply a valid dominance map; the composite maps every feasible point to a retained point with no worse objective.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) preserves \(F\) and \(f\), and \(C\) meets every orbit.
\(T(F\cap C)\subseteq F\cap K\).
\(f(Tx)\le f(x)\) on \(F\cap C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(F)\subseteq F\cap K\) and \(f(S(y))\le f(y)\) for every \(y\in F\).

children.title: Invalid-Pruning Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model changes or numerical ambiguities that undermine pruning validity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Revalidation after Model or Numerical-Convention Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporal and numerical validity boundary for previously established dominance and symmetry certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose deletion of a region \(E\) was certified for feasible set \(F\), objective \(f\), and numerical comparison convention \(\tau\). After replacing these data by \((F',f',\tau')\), the old certificate justifies continued deletion only after its predicates are re-established: a symmetry must preserve \(F'\) and \(f'\), and a dominance map must send \(F'\cap E\) into the currently retained feasible set and satisfy the required objective inequality with certified error compatible with \(\tau'\). Uncertified floating-point agreement or an unrevalidated certificate is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing constraints, objectives, or numerical comparison rules invalidates an old symmetry or dominance certificate unless all of its predicates are reverified conservatively.
assumptions_latex: The earlier deletion depended on feasibility, objective, or numerical-comparison predicates.
At least one model component or numerical convention may have changed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\operatorname{Revalidate}(E;F',f',\tau')\Longrightarrow\text{the old certificate does not justify deleting }E\text{ in the modified problem}.
knowledge_statements.title: Revalidation after Model or Numerical-Convention Changes
Invalid-Pruning Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failures when dominance or symmetry hypotheses are not globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two minimal examples delimit valid pruning. First, on \(F=\{-1,1\}\) with \(f(-1)=0\) and \(f(1)=1\), the reflection \(x\mapsto-x\) preserves feasibility but not the objective; pruning \(-1\) as symmetric to \(1\) deletes the unique minimizer. Second, on \(F=[0,1]\) with \(f(x)=x\), the proposed dominance map \(T(x)=1-x\) satisfies \(f(Tx)\le f(x)\) only when \(x\ge\tfrac12\); using it to prune all of \([0,1]\) is invalid. Symmetry must preserve both feasibility and objective, and dominance must hold throughout the entire deleted region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pruning can delete the optimum if a claimed symmetry changes objective values or a dominance inequality holds only on part of the removed region.
assumptions_latex: Pruning is attempted using the transformations displayed in the two examples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(-1)<f(1)\), and \(f(Tx)>f(x)\) for every \(x<\tfrac12\); therefore the proposed global pruning certificates fail.

notation.meaning: proposed but regionally invalid dominance map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained minimization using equality constraints h_m(x)=0 and inequality constraints g_k(x)\ge 0; the source's detailed numbered pseudocode contains apparent transcription or branch inconsistencies, so this candidate records its explicit three-case selection rule and generation structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\Psi(x)=\sum_{m=1}^{M}h_m(x)^2+\sum_{k=1}^{K}G_k(x)g_k(x)^2,
\qquad
G_k(x)=\begin{cases}0,&g_k(x)\ge0,\\1,&g_k(x)<0.\end{cases}

For each tournament pair \((x^r,x^s)\), select the chromosome with smaller \(\Psi\) when both are infeasible; select the feasible chromosome when exactly one is feasible; and, when both are feasible, evaluate \(f\) and select the chromosome with smaller objective value. Repeated tournaments populate the next generation, after which crossover and mutation are applied; this process continues until the prescribed generation limit \(T\). Objective values need not be evaluated when either contestant is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure violation by the sum of squared equality residuals and squared negative inequality residuals. Between two infeasible chromosomes, retain the less-violating one; between a feasible and an infeasible chromosome, retain the feasible one; and between two feasible chromosomes, retain the one with the smaller objective value. Repeat tournaments to form each new population, then apply crossover and mutation until the generation limit. Objective evaluations are avoided in tournaments involving infeasible contestants.

knowledge_statements.title: Local NLP Incumbent Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local constrained minimization used only to improve the global solver's feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given continuously differentiable functions \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), define \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g(x)\leq0,\ h(x)=0\}\). Initialize a local nonlinear-programming solver at \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\). Run its prescribed descent, trust-region, or line-search procedure until it returns a terminal point \(x^+\) or reaches its declared failure or resource limit. Given a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\in F\), replace \(\bar x\) by \(x^+\) exactly when a terminal point is returned, \(x^+\) passes the prescribed feasibility test, and \(f(x^+)<f(\bar x)\); otherwise retain \(\bar x\). Output the retained feasible incumbent without asserting global optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistart Incumbent Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multistart composition of a seed generator and a local constrained solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a search domain, let \(F\subseteq X\) be its feasible subset, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_N\}\subseteq X\) be deterministic or sampled starting points. Let \(L(s_k)\in X\) denote the terminal point returned by a local nonlinear-programming search initialized at \(s_k\). For \(k=1,\ldots,N\), compute \(y_k=L(s_k)\), discard \(y_k\) unless it passes the prescribed feasibility test for \(F\), and compare every retained value with the current feasible incumbent \(\bar x\in F\). Output a point \(\bar x_{\mathrm{out}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):x\in\{\bar x,y_1,\ldots,y_N\},\ x\text{ is retained as feasible}\}\). If no new point is retained, output \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Clustering-Guided Multistart
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative starts are selected from clusters to reduce redundant local solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Descent Incumbents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbents generated by a set-valued descent transformation on feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic Euclidean projections used as an initial feasibility-reduction stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,ldots,C_q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty closed convex constraint sets with computable Euclidean projections \(P_{C_i}(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C_i}\|y-x\|_2\). Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\) and update \(x^{k+1}=P_{C_{1+(k\bmod q)}}(x^k)\). Stop when the aggregate feasibility residual is at most \(\varepsilon_{m proj}\), when progress over a prescribed window is below a threshold, or when a resource limit is reached. Return the final point and its residual; acceptance as an incumbent requires a separate test against every original constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project cyclically onto tractable closed convex constraint sets, stopping at feasibility, stagnation, or a resource limit, then test all original constraints separately.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Every projection \(P_{C_i}\) can be computed to the prescribed accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonprojectable residual constraints are repaired by a local violation subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a projected point \(z\), a violation measure \(v:X\to\mathbb R_+\), and \(\rho>0\), approximately solve \(\min_{x\in X}\,v(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x-z\|_2^2\), initialized at \(z\). Stop successfully at \(x^+\) if \(v(x^+)\leq\varepsilon_{m feas}\); otherwise stop unsuccessfully upon stagnation, local stationarity, or a resource limit. On success, optionally run objective improvement while enforcing feasibility, and accept the result as an incumbent only after complete constraint screening. On failure, retain the previous incumbent and record the unrepaired residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally minimize violation while penalizing displacement from the projected point, then accept only a fully screened successful repair.

\(\rho>0\) and \(\varepsilon_{m feas}\geq0\) are fixed.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-to-Repair Handoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic switching predicate separates projection progress from local repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\geq0\) be the full constraint residual after projection iteration \(k\), let \(w\in\mathbb N\), and choose \(\varepsilon_{m proj},\eta\geq0\). Continue projection while \(r_k>\varepsilon_{m proj}\), the projection budget remains, and \(r_{k-w}-r_k>\eta r_{k-w}\) whenever \(k\geq w\). Hand the current point to repair when \(r_k>\varepsilon_{m proj}\) and either the budget is exhausted, a required constraint lacks a projection operator, or \(r_{k-w}-r_k\leq\eta r_{k-w}\). Bypass repair and proceed to full feasibility screening when \(r_k\leq\varepsilon_{m proj}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local violation stationarity and singular linearizations can block repair despite nonempty feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the feasible equation \(h(x)=x^2-1=0\) on \(\mathbb R\) and the squared violation \(v(x)=h(x)^2\). The feasible set is \(\{-1,1\}\), but \(v'(0)=0\) and \(v(0)=1\). Hence a local repair method initialized at \(x=0\) and terminating at first-order stationarity may stop infeasibly. Moreover, the linearized repair equation at \(x=0\) is \(h(0)+h'(0)d=-1=0\), which is inconsistent. Thus nonempty feasibility alone does not guarantee success of local penalty descent or linearization-based repair; safeguards or alternative starts are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the feasible equation x²−1=0, the origin is an infeasible stationary point of squared violation and has an inconsistent linearized repair equation.
assumptions_latex: Repair uses squared violation descent or the first-order linearization of the equality.
The method may initialize at \(x=0\) and accept first-order stationarity as termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The repair procedure can terminate or fail at \(x=0\) although the feasible set \(\{-1,1\}\) is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Violation Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized residual thresholds classify trial points before incumbent admission.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scales \(s_i,t_j>0\), define \(v(x)=\max\{0,\max_i g_i(x)/s_i,\max_j|h_j(x)|/t_j\}\). Fix \(0\leq\varepsilon_{m accept}<\varepsilon_{m reject}\). Classify a trial point as provisionally feasible when \(v(x)\leq\varepsilon_{m accept}\), send it to restoration when \(\varepsilon_{m accept}<v(x)<\varepsilon_{m reject}\), and reject it when \(v(x)\geq\varepsilon_{m reject}\). Provisional feasibility permits objective comparison but does not replace validated feasibility when certification is required. The scales and thresholds must remain fixed during comparisons among candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use scaled maximum violation and two fixed thresholds to classify a trial point as provisionally feasible, repairable, or rejected.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i,t_j>0\) for every inequality and equality constraint.
\(0\leq\varepsilon_{m accept}<\varepsilon_{m reject}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every evaluated trial point belongs to exactly one of the accept, restore, or reject classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Primal Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward-rounded interval evaluation certifies tolerance-based primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the accepted feasible set be \(F_\varepsilon=\{x:l\leq x\leq u,\ g_i(x)\leq\varepsilon_i, |h_j(x)|\leq\delta_j\}\), where all tolerances are nonnegative. For a machine-representable candidate \(\hat x\), compute outward-rounded interval enclosures \(G_i(\hat x)\ni g_i(\hat x)\) and \(H_j(\hat x)\ni h_j(\hat x)\). A validated primal-feasibility certificate consists of exact bound checks \(l\leq\hat x\leq u\), upper endpoints satisfying \(\sup G_i(\hat x)\leq\varepsilon_i\), and interval magnitude bounds satisfying \(\sup\{|y|:y\in H_j(\hat x)\}\leq\delta_j\). These verifiable inclusions imply \(\hat x\in F_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward-rounded interval bounds certify toleranced feasibility when every inequality upper bound, equality magnitude bound, and variable bound passes its prescribed test.
assumptions_latex: The interval evaluations enclose the exact real constraint values at \(\hat x\).
All arithmetic used for the certificate has directed outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed bound and enclosure tests imply \(\hat x\in F_\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: validated enclosure of an inequality value
validated enclosure of an equality value

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Detection and approximation of an integral-path pitchfork bifurcation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral exchange test, localization NLP, and flat-contour failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the contours flatten but the integral-path flow is not collinear with the level-constraint tangent subspace, monitor the terrain-path eigenvalue and the smallest eigenvalue of \(H\) projected onto that tangent subspace. After an exchange of the minimum eigenvalue from the direction associated with \(J^TF\) to the tangent subspace is detected, approximate the bifurcation on the corresponding level curve \(L^*\) by solving \(\max g^Tg\) subject to \(F^TF=L^*\). Finite predictor steps generally yield only an approximation. Extreme contour flatness can make the Kuhn--Tucker coefficient matrix nearly singular, so careful step-size control is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If contours flatten without path-flow collinearity, monitor the terrain-path eigenvalue and the smallest tangent-projected eigenvalue of H. Once their minimum-eigenvalue roles exchange, approximate the pitchfork bifurcation by maximizing g transpose g on the detected level curve F transpose F equals L star. Finite predictor steps usually give an approximation, and extreme flatness can cause near-singular KKT systems, requiring careful step-size control.
assumptions_latex: \text{The contours flatten while the integral-path flow is not collinear with the level-set tangent subspace.}
L^*\text{ is the level curve on which the eigenvalue exchange is detected.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{After the eigenvalue exchange, solve }\max\{g^Tg:F^TF=L^*\}\text{ to approximate the pitchfork bifurcation; extreme flatness may cause near-singular KKT equations.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locality is defined by invariance under objective modifications outside a neighborhood containing the sampled points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be sufficiently rich. An information functional \(\operatorname{LocInf}\) is local if, for every \((f,S)\in\mathcal P\), every finite sequence \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subseteq S\), every open set \(\mathcal N\) containing all \(x_i\), and every \((g,S)\in\mathcal P\) satisfying \(f(x)=g(x)\) for all \(x\in\mathcal N\), one has \(\operatorname{LocInf}(f,\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\})=\operatorname{LocInf}(g,\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\})\). An information functional failing this invariance is global information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information obtained from finitely many sampled points is local when it cannot distinguish two admissible objectives that agree on an open neighborhood of all sampled points. Information that is not local in this sense is global.

(f,S),(g,S)\in\mathcal P
\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subseteq S
\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subseteq\mathcal N
f|_{\mathcal N}=g|_{\mathcal N}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LocInf}(f,\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N)=\operatorname{LocInf}(g,\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N)

knowledge_statements.title: Fair-Node-Selection Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence when node selection prevents indefinite neglect of competitive regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider branch-and-bound minimization of a continuous function over a nonempty compact feasible set. Suppose lower bounds are valid and consistent, feasible incumbent values are retained, and subdivision makes the diameter tend to zero along every infinite lineage. Call node selection fair if every node that remains unfathomed is selected after finitely many subsequent selections. Then no box containing a global minimizer can be discarded or neglected forever. Consequently, if \(U_k\) is the incumbent and \(L_k\) is the least bound among open nodes, \[L_k\leq f^*\leq U_k,\qquad U_k-L_k\longrightarrow0,\] and every accumulation point of incumbent solutions is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair processing of every persistent node, together with valid consistent bounds and shrinking descendants, forces the global optimality gap to vanish.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite-branching spatial algorithm start from a compact root box, and suppose every retained box \(B\) intersects the feasible set \(F\). Assign to each such box a valid lower bound \(L(B)\leq\min_{x\in F\cap B}f(x)\) and a feasible upper value \(Q(B)=f(x_B)\) for some \(x_B\in F\cap B\). Suppose \[0\leq Q(B)-L(B)\leq\omega(\operatorname{diam}B),\qquad \omega(t)\to0\ \text{as}\ t\downarrow0.\] Assume that there exist an integer \(q\geq1\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that every descendant obtained after \(q\) subdivision levels has diameter at most \(\rho\operatorname{diam}B\). For a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), suppose a box is accepted or pruned, and is not subdivided further, whenever \(Q(B)-L(B)\leq\varepsilon\). Then the resulting subdivision tree has finite depth and finitely many nodes. At termination, if \(L\) is the least lower bound over the final accepted leaves and \(U\) is the least feasible upper value generated, then \[U-L\leq\varepsilon.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Finiteness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why zero-tolerance termination needs exactness beyond ordinary asymptotic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Positive-tolerance finiteness does not imply finite termination at zero tolerance. Let \(F=[0,1]\), choose an irrational \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and minimize \(f(x)=(x-\alpha)^2\). Bisect only at dyadic points, sample only dyadic points, and use the exact interval lower bound \(L(B)=\min_{x\in B}f(x)\). The unique box containing \(\alpha\) always has lower bound \(0\), whereas every sampled feasible point has positive objective value. Hence its gap is positive at every finite iteration although it tends to zero. Exact finite termination therefore requires an additional regime, such as finite representability of an optimizer, exact relaxation attainment, or a finite certificate separating all remaining nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing gaps need not reach zero finitely; exact termination requires representable optimizers, exact relaxations, or another finite separation certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: FBBT Termination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite versus merely asymptotic termination of feasibility-based bound tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let feasibility-based bound tightening iterate \(B^{k+1}=T(B^k)\), where \(T(B)\subseteq B\). If all box endpoints belong to a finite representable set \(E\) and every nonfixed update strictly changes at least one endpoint, then the iteration reaches a fixed box after finitely many updates. Without finite endpoint structure or a positive stopping tolerance, finite termination need not hold: on intervals \(B^k=[0,u_k]\), the contracting update \(T([0,u])=[0,u/2]\) gives \(u_k=2^{-k}u_0\), so \(B^{k+1}\neq B^k\) for every finite \(k\), although \(B^k\) converges to \(\{0\}\). Thus real-arithmetic FBBT may require tolerance-based or iteration-limit termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FBBT terminates finitely on a finite endpoint lattice, but continuous tightening can approach its fixed point forever without attaining it.
assumptions_latex: \(T(B)\subseteq B\) for every box \(B\).
In the finite regime, endpoints lie in a finite set and every nonfixed update is strict.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite endpoint lattices force finite termination; unrestricted real endpoints permit only asymptotic convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive global optimality certificate for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\). Let \(\widehat x\in F\) be a verified feasible point with \(U=f(\widehat x)\), and let \(L\) be a certified global lower bound satisfying \(L\leq f^*\). For a prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\geq0\), the inequality \[U-L\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\] is an absolute-gap certificate. Indeed, the validated enclosure \(L\leq f^*\leq U\) implies \(0\leq f(\widehat x)-f^*\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\). The certificate consists of the feasible point, its validated objective upper bound, the global lower-bound record, and the checked gap inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent and a valid lower bound certify additive optimality whenever their difference does not exceed the prescribed absolute tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat x\in F\) is verified and \(U=f(\widehat x)\).
\(U-L\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) with \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-normalized global optimality certificate with an explicit denominator floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat x\in F\), let \(U=f(\widehat x)\), and let \(L\leq f^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\). Fix a scale floor \(\tau>0\) and define \[g_{\mathrm{rel}}=\frac{U-L}{\max\{|U|,\tau\}}.\] If \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\), then \[0\leq f(\widehat x)-f^*\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{|U|,\tau\}.\] Hence the feasible point, validated values \(L,U\), declared scale floor, and verified ratio constitute a relative-gap certificate. The denominator convention must be recorded because alternative solver conventions can produce different reported relative gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized incumbent-bound gap certifies scaled optimality when its denominator convention and positive scale floor are recorded explicitly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unregularized ratio \((U-L)/|U|\) is undefined when \(U=0\) and can fail to reflect shrinking absolute error as \(U\to0\). For example, minimize \(f(x)=x^2\) over \(F=[-1,1]\), with valid lower bound \(L=0=f^*\). For every integer \(k\geq1\), the feasible incumbent \(x_k=k^{-1/2}\) has \(U_k=f(x_k)=1/k\), so \(U_k-L\to0\), but \[(U_k-L)/|U_k|=1\] for every \(k\geq1\). Therefore, near zero, termination should use an absolute tolerance or a declared scaled denominator such as \(\max\{|U|,\tau\}\) with \(\tau>0\); an unqualified relative-gap claim is not a stable certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a zero optimum, absolute error may vanish while the unregularized relative ratio remains one or becomes undefined, so an absolute tolerance or a declared positive scale floor is needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Certificate Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation requirements for machine-checkable global optimality gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reported pair \((L,U)\) is a validated gap certificate only if four checks succeed: a witness \(\widehat x\) is rigorously verified feasible; outward-rounded evaluation proves \(f(\widehat x)\leq U\); the lower-bound derivation proves \(L\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\); and directed rounding verifies the declared absolute or scaled-relative gap inequality. These checks yield \[L\leq f^*=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\leq f(\widehat x)\leq U.\] Consequently, \(U-L\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) validates absolute optimality, while \((U-L)/\max\{|U|,\tau\}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\) validates the corresponding declared scaled guarantee. Unverified floating-point solver output alone is not a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid gap requires rigorous feasibility, outward-rounded objective evaluation, a globally valid lower bound, and directed-rounding verification of the stated inequality.
assumptions_latex: Feasibility of \(\widehat x\) and the upper evaluation \(f(\widehat x)\leq U\) are rigorously validated.
The lower-bound record proves \(L\leq f(x)\) for all \(x\in F\).

knowledge_statements.title: Region-Exclusion Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic branch-and-bound exclusion of one search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(f^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\), let \(R\subseteq X\) be a search region and let \(U\) be the value of a verified feasible incumbent. A region-exclusion certificate for \(R\) consists of validated data establishing either \(F\cap R=\varnothing\) or a lower bound \(L(R)\leq\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\) with \(L(R)\geq U-\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\geq0\). In either case, no point of \(F\cap R\) can improve the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\), so \(R\) may be removed from the active partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region is safely discarded when it is proved infeasible or its validated lower bound cannot improve the incumbent beyond the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is the feasible set and minimization is intended.
\(U=f(\hat x)\) for a verified point \(\hat x\in F\).
\(L(R)\) is computed with outward-rounded or otherwise validated bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) contains no feasible point \(x\) satisfying \(f(x)<U-\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-cover certificate for infeasibility of a continuous global problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), where every \(g_j:X\to\mathbb R\). A global-infeasibility certificate is a finite family of regions \(R_i\subseteq X\) satisfying \(X=\bigcup_{i=1}^N R_i\), together with validated regional facts such that, for every \(i\), some constraint index \(j(i)\) satisfies \(\inf_{x\in R_i}g_{j(i)}(x)>0\). Each region therefore violates at least one required constraint, and the covering property implies \(F=\varnothing\). The certificate is independently checkable by verifying the cover and every regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite cover of the search domain proves global infeasibility when every covering region has a validated positive lower bound for at least one required inequality constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is covered by finitely many validated regions \(R_i\subseteq X\).
Each constraint function \(g_j\) is real-valued on \(X\).
All regional lower bounds are rigorous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: region in the finite cover of X

knowledge_statements.title: Validated Enclosure Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigorous objective enclosure assembled over a finite domain cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^N R_i\) and \(F\subseteq X\). Suppose validated computations give \(f(F\cap R_i)\subseteq[L_i,U_i]\) whenever \(F\cap R_i\neq\varnothing\), and a verified feasible point \(\hat x\in F\) is available. Then \(L=\min_i L_i\) and \(U=f(\hat x)\) form a validated enclosure \(L\leq f^*\leq U\). The cover, regional interval data, and feasibility check for \(\hat x\) constitute an \(\varepsilon\)-optimality certificate whenever \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated regional ranges and a verified feasible incumbent enclose the global optimum; a sufficiently narrow enclosure certifies prescribed absolute accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\) is finite.
The regions cover \(X\), and all stated enclosures use validated arithmetic.
\(\hat x\) is rigorously verified feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*\in[L,U]\), and \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) implies \(f(\hat x)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: validated objective enclosure on region i
