knowledge_statements.title: Certified-Optimal Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination predicate for rigorous absolute-relative global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, a solver may return certified-optimal status with tolerances \(\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_r\geq0\) only if it has a verified feasible incumbent \(\hat x\), an objective upper bound \(U=f(\hat x)\), and a rigorous global lower bound \(L\leq f^*\), and if \(U-L\leq\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U|\}\). The returned certificate must expose enough validated information to check feasibility, the lower bound, and the gap inequality. With zero tolerances, the status certifies \(f(\hat x)=f^*=L=U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified-optimal status requires a verified feasible incumbent and rigorous global lower bound whose absolute-relative gap meets the declared tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The solver minimizes over a specified feasible set \(F\).
Both incumbent feasibility and the global lower bound are rigorously validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq f(\hat x)-f^*\leq\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U|\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Certified-Infeasible Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination predicate requiring a checkable proof of empty feasibility set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a problem with feasible set \(F\subseteq X\), certified-infeasible status is admissible only when the solver returns a finite, independently checkable certificate implying \(F=\varnothing\). In a partition workflow, it suffices to provide a finite cover \(X\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^N R_i\) and a validated infeasibility certificate for every \(F\cap R_i\). Failure to find a feasible point, exhaustion of sampling, or numerical failure alone does not satisfy this predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified-infeasible status requires a checkable global certificate that every part of the search domain is infeasible; unsuccessful search alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The declared domain \(X\) and all constraints defining \(F\) are fixed.
Every regional certificate is rigorous and the covering claim is verifiable.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Limited Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncertifying termination caused by exhaustion of a declared computational budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a declared budget on time, memory, iterations, nodes, or oracle calls. Resource-limited status applies when execution stops because consumed resource \(C\) reaches \(B\) before a certified-optimal or certified-infeasible predicate is established. The solver may report a verified incumbent \(U\), a valid lower bound \(L\), and the residual gap, but the status itself asserts neither optimality nor infeasibility. Formally, \(C\geq B\) and neither certification predicate holds at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver exhausted a declared budget before proving optimality or infeasibility; any incumbent and bound remain useful, but the status is noncertifying.
assumptions_latex: A measurable resource budget \(B\) is declared before or during execution.
Certified-optimal and certified-infeasible predicates are separately defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\geq B\) while no terminal optimality or infeasibility certificate has been established.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerically Indeterminate Status
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncertifying termination when numerical validation cannot resolve required predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Numerically indeterminate status applies when finite-precision or validation procedures cannot rigorously decide a required predicate, such as feasibility, bound validity, interval sign, or gap closure, and no resource-limit event is the designated cause of termination. If an enclosure \([a,b]\) for a decisive quantity satisfies \(a\leq0\leq b\), neither strict sign may be asserted. Consequently, unresolved numerical evidence must not be promoted to certified-optimal or certified-infeasible status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical enclosures remain too ambiguous to validate a decisive predicate, so neither optimality nor infeasibility may be certified.
assumptions_latex: Certification requires rigorous decisions from finite-precision or validated computations.
At least one decisive predicate remains unresolved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{status}=\mathrm{numerically\ indeterminate}\), with no assertion that the problem is optimal or infeasible.

notation.meaning: validated enclosure of a decisive scalar quantity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the meaningful parameter range, endpoint cases, and invariance under value-preserving reparameterization and positive affine objective transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D\subset\mathbb{R}^n be compact, let f attain its maximum and minimum on D, let x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x), and set p=\max_{x\in D}f(x)-\min_{x\in D}f(x). For \epsilon\in[0,1], a feasible point x^\diamond\in D is an \epsilon-approximate solution if f(x^\diamond)-f(x^*)\le \epsilon p. For \epsilon=0 this requires global optimality, whereas for \epsilon=1 every feasible point qualifies. The criterion is unchanged by translations and positive scalings of f and by feasible-set reparameterizations preserving objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact feasible set, normalize the objective gap by the difference between the maximum and minimum objective values. A feasible point is epsilon-approximate when its gap from a global minimum is at most epsilon times that range. The definition is meaningful for epsilon between zero and one: zero requires a global minimizer, and one admits every feasible point. It is invariant under positive affine changes of objective scale and equivalent reparameterizations of the feasible set.

f\text{ attains }\max_D f\text{ and }\min_D f
x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x)
\epsilon\in[0,1]

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Region-count complexity of a partition-based global solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition algorithm run to accuracy \(\varepsilon\), let \(N_0\) be the number of initial search regions. Its partition complexity \(N_P(\varepsilon)\) is the total number of distinct search regions generated through termination, including the initial regions; processed-region complexity \(N_A(\varepsilon)\) counts regions removed from the active set by processing. If processing any region generates at most \(b\) children, then \(N_P(\varepsilon)\leq N_0+bN_A(\varepsilon)\). The counts exclude objective and constraint evaluations unless region generation itself invokes an oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition complexity counts initial and subsequently generated search regions, while processed-region complexity counts processed regions; with at most b children per processed region, generated regions are bounded by the initial count plus b times the processed count.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm begins with \(N_0<\infty\) explicit search regions.
Termination accuracy \(\varepsilon\) and the counting convention are fixed.
Processing one region generates at most \(b\) child regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_P(\varepsilon)\leq N_0+bN_A(\varepsilon)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation Complexity

Evaluation complexity is the vector \(N_{o}(\varepsilon)\), indexed by \(o\in\mathcal O\), whose component counts calls to oracle \(o\) before termination. Oracles may separately return objective values, constraint values, derivatives, relaxations, or validated enclosures. A scalar evaluation count is meaningful only when the oracle classes have equal declared unit cost; otherwise complexity is reported as the vector or by a weighted oracle-cost model.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition–Evaluation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto comparison of region refinement and oracle evaluation effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At fixed accuracy \(\varepsilon\), associate each certified run with the cost pair \((N_P(\varepsilon),N_E(\varepsilon))\), where the first component counts generated regions and the second counts evaluations under a fixed oracle convention. Run \(A\) dominates run \(B\) when both counts for \(A\) do not exceed those for \(B\), with at least one strict inequality. A partition–evaluation tradeoff is therefore represented by the nondominated cost pairs; no scalar ranking is intrinsic without declared weights or resource constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At fixed accuracy, useful solver configurations form a Pareto frontier between generated regions and oracle evaluations; scalar comparison requires declared costs.
assumptions_latex: All compared runs solve the same problem to the same certified accuracy.
Partition and evaluation counts use identical conventions across runs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tradeoff set is the Pareto-minimal subset of \(\{(N_P(\varepsilon),N_E(\varepsilon))\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Cost Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted complexity model for heterogeneous solver oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\) be a finite set of declared oracle classes, let \(N_o(\varepsilon)\) count calls of type \(o\in\mathcal O\), and let \(c_o\geq0\) be the declared unit cost of such a call. The oracle-cost regime \(c=(c_o)_{o\in\mathcal O}\) induces the weighted cost \[C_{\mathcal O,c}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}c_oN_o(\varepsilon).\] The unit-cost regime has \(c_o=1\) for every \(o\in\mathcal O\). Other regimes assign larger weights to the oracle classes whose expense the model is intended to emphasize. Scalar cost comparisons are valid only when the same oracle taxonomy, counting convention, and weight vector are used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle-cost regime is a declared nonnegative weight for every oracle class; weighted call counts give a scalar cost, and comparisons require the same classes, counting rules, and weights.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal O\) is a finite set of declared oracle classes.
The call counts \(N_o(\varepsilon)\) use a fixed counting convention.
The nonnegative weight vector \(c\) includes every oracle cost intended by the comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathcal O,c}(\varepsilon)\) is the scalar cost induced by the declared oracle-cost regime \(c\).

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Size Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case node count for bounded-depth partition search trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a rooted search tree in which every internal node has at most \(b\geq2\) children and no node has depth exceeding \(D\). The number \(T_D\) of generated nodes satisfies \[T_D\leq\sum_{d=0}^{D}b^d=\frac{b^{D+1}-1}{b-1}.\] Equality holds for a complete \(b\)-ary tree. Thus, if certification may require exploring every node to depth \(D\), worst-case search-tree size is \(O(b^D)\); pruning can reduce realized size but does not improve this bound without additional structural assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search tree of depth D and branching factor at most b has at most a geometric-series number of nodes, exponential in D in the full-tree case.
assumptions_latex: The root has depth \(0\).
Each internal node has at most \(b\geq2\) children.
Maximum generated depth is \(D<\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Refinement Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-count accounting for deterministic lower-bound refinement in a finite spatial search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{N}\) be the finite family of regions processed before an \(\varepsilon\)-global certificate is obtained. For each \(Q\in\mathcal{N}\), let \(r_Q(\varepsilon)\) be the number of successive lower-bound refinements performed on \(Q\), and let \(c(Q,r)\) count the oracle operations used by its \(r\)-th refinement. Bound-refinement complexity is the aggregate refinement cost \(C_{\mathrm{ref}}(\varepsilon)\). If refinement costs and depths admit uniform bounds over all processed regions, the displayed product gives an immediate worst-case upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound-refinement complexity sums all oracle work spent tightening regional lower bounds; uniform per-refinement cost and refinement depth over all processed regions give a product upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm processes a finite set of regions \(\mathcal{N}\).
For each region \(Q\), refinement level \(r\) costs \(c(Q,r)\ge 0\) oracle operations and yields a valid lower bound \(L_{Q,r}\).
The stopping test is \(U-\min_{Q\in\mathcal{N}}L_{Q,r_Q}\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C_{\mathrm{ref}}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{N}}\sum_{r=1}^{r_Q(\varepsilon)}c(Q,r).\] If \(c(Q,r)\le \bar c\) and every processed region \(Q\in\mathcal{N}\) requires at most \(R(\varepsilon)\) refinements, then \[C_{\mathrm{ref}}(\varepsilon)\le |\mathcal{N}|\,\bar c\,R(\varepsilon).\] Thus refinement complexity separates the number of processed regions from the per-region effort needed to make the certified global gap at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Refinement depth used on region Q

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Reduction Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work bound for certified domain-contraction passes across a finite global-search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{N}\) be a finite family of processed regions. For every \(Q\in\mathcal{N}\), apply \(k_Q\) certified contraction passes, and let \(c_{Q,j}\) denote the primitive-operation cost of pass \(j\), including constraint propagation or bound tightening selected by the accounting convention. Domain-reduction complexity is \(C_{\mathrm{red}}=\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{N}}\sum_{j=1}^{k_Q}c_{Q,j}\). Uniform bounds on pass cost and pass count yield the stated worst-case estimate, while certification requires every contraction to preserve all feasible incumbent-improving points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain-reduction complexity is the sum of certified contraction-pass costs over a finite family of processed nodes, bounded by node count times maximum passes and maximum pass cost.
assumptions_latex: The initial search domain is a box \(X_0\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and the processed-node family \(\mathcal{N}\) is finite.
Each reduction pass contracts a box without removing any feasible point capable of improving the incumbent.
For every \(Q\in\mathcal{N}\) and \(1\le j\le k_Q\), pass \(j\) costs \(c_{Q,j}\le c_{\mathrm{red}}\) primitive operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If node \(Q\) receives \(k_Q\) reduction passes, then \[C_{\mathrm{red}}=\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{N}}\sum_{j=1}^{k_Q}c_{Q,j}\le c_{\mathrm{red}}\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{N}}k_Q.\] In particular, if \(k_Q\le K\) for every processed node, then \(C_{\mathrm{red}}\le c_{\mathrm{red}}K|\mathcal{N}|\). This count excludes relaxation solution and branching unless those operations are explicitly included in \(c_{Q,j}\).

notation.meaning: Finite family of processed search regions

assumptions_latex: The search computation is a directed acyclic task graph with total work \(W\) and span \(S\).
At most \(p\ge 1\) identical processors execute ready tasks under a work-conserving scheduler.
Communication, synchronization, and idle time contribute a nonnegative additive cost \(H_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parallel running time satisfies the work-span lower bound \[T_p\ge \max\{W/p,S\}.\] Defining parallel-search overhead by \(O_p=pT_p-W\), one has \(O_p\ge 0\). Under a scheduler guarantee \(T_p\le W/p+S+H_p\), \[O_p\le pS+pH_p.\] Hence useful speedup is limited by both the critical dependency chain and search-specific coordination costs.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a parallel global search by a finite directed acyclic task graph. For execution on \(p\) processors with elapsed time \(T_p\), define overhead as \(O_p=pT_p-W\). Any execution obeys the work-span lower bound. If the scheduler additionally satisfies \(T_p\le W/p+S+H_p\), the displayed upper bound isolates dependency and coordination overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel-search overhead is excess processor-time beyond serial work; work, span, and coordination costs bound attainable running time and speedup.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified orchestration rule for node-relaxation solves, retries, and pruning decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a node region \(Q\), incumbent value \(U\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\). Construct a relaxation with optimum not exceeding the node optimum and invoke the relaxation subsolver. Accept a finite value \(L_Q\) only when its status certifies validity. If \(L_Q\ge U-\varepsilon\), prune \(Q\); otherwise store \(L_Q\) and return \(Q\) to search. On timeout, numerical failure, or uncertified status, retry with an approved formulation or retain \(Q\) without bound-based pruning. Stop managing \(Q\) only after pruning, branching, or certified exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation manager accepts only certified lower bounds, prunes by the incumbent gap, and retains or retries nodes after uncertified subsolver outcomes.

Each backend operation returns an interval enclosure containing its exact real result.
The mathematical model is defined throughout every evaluated input box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every expression \(g\) and box \(Q\), the backend output \([g](Q)\) satisfies \[\{g(x):x\in Q\}\subseteq[g](Q).\] Therefore, \(\inf[g](Q)\) is a valid lower bound and \(\sup[g](Q)\) is a valid upper bound for \(g\) on \(Q\), subject to the stated domain assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion certificate supplied by outward-rounded interval evaluation of expression graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A validated-numerics backend assigns each supported real expression \(g\) an interval extension \([g]\). Given a closed box \(Q\), every elementary operation and library function is evaluated with directed outward rounding, so its returned interval contains the exact range of that operation over its interval inputs. Compositional evaluation must preserve inclusion across the expression graph. The resulting enclosure \([g](Q)\) certifies the displayed range inclusion and may be consumed by bounding, feasibility, and pruning routines.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outward-rounded interval backend encloses every exact expression value on the input box, yielding directly checkable lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Validated-Numerics Backend

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role is suitable for the backend's inclusion guarantee, but the enclosure claim for supported operations and library functions requires a validated-numerics source with a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: Each open node \(Q\) stores a valid lower bound \(L_Q\).
The incumbent value is \(U\), with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
The node-selection key is deterministic after tie-breaking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every iteration, all nodes remaining in the pool satisfy \(L_Q<U-\varepsilon\). If the pool becomes empty, then no unprocessed region can contain a feasible point with objective below \(U-\varepsilon\), so the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal relative to the covered initial domain.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound stored for node Q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-pool lifecycle with incumbent-based pruning and an empty-pool termination certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the open-node pool \(\mathcal{P}\) with the root region and its valid lower bound. Before selection, delete every \(Q\in\mathcal{P}\) satisfying \(L_Q\ge U-\varepsilon\). If \(\mathcal{P}\) is empty, terminate. Otherwise remove a node minimizing the prescribed selection key, process it, and insert each nonpruned child with a valid lower bound. Whenever \(U\) decreases, repeat incumbent-based filtering. The pool state must preserve coverage of every unresolved part of the initial domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The open-node pool stores unresolved regions with valid bounds, prunes them against the incumbent, and certifies completion when no unresolved region remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Open-Node Pool Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits open-node pool management, but empty-pool global certification depends on search coverage, valid child bounds, and sound pruning invariants that are not backed by a cited branch-and-bound source.

children.title: Incumbent Management
children.top_down_role: Storage, replacement, and dissemination of the current best feasible solution.

assumptions_latex: Every accepted incumbent point is validated as feasible.
Objective comparisons use certified values or a stated conservative comparison rule.
The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After every accepted update, \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\in F\), \(U=f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})\), and the sequence of incumbent values is nonincreasing. Thus \(U\) remains a valid upper bound on the global optimum throughout the search.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-best feasible solution state for a minimization workflow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(U=+\infty\) with no incumbent. For each candidate \(x\), independently validate \(x\in F\) and obtain a trustworthy objective value \(f(x)\). If no incumbent exists or \(f(x)<U\), atomically set \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\leftarrow x\) and \(U\leftarrow f(x)\); otherwise retain the current pair. Reject invalid, incomparable, or unevaluated candidates. Export each accepted decrease of \(U\) to pruning and termination tests, while retaining the prior incumbent until the replacement is fully validated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incumbent management atomically replaces the best validated feasible point only on a trustworthy objective improvement, preserving a nonincreasing upper bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits incumbent management, but the trustworthy-objective comparison and atomic publication policy are workflow-specific and uncited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Convergence of a Genetic Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers binary and continuous encodings under the genetic algorithm's monotonicity and positive-probability assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f^*=\min_{x\in\Omega}f(x)$, $X^*=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in\Omega}f(x)$, and let $f_{\mathrm{best}}^k=\min\{f(x):x\in P^k\}$ with $x_{\mathrm{best}}^k\in\operatorname{argmin}\{f(x):x\in P^k\}$. Suppose the genetic algorithm satisfies the monotonicity and positive-probability assumptions. (i) For binary encoding, $\Pr(\lim_{k\to\infty}f_{\mathrm{best}}^k=f^*)=1$ and $\lim_{k\to\infty}\Pr(P^k\cap X^*\neq\varnothing)=1$. (ii) For continuous encoding, if $\Omega$ is compact and $f\in\mathcal C^0$, then every convergent subsequence $x_{\mathrm{best}}^{k_i}\to\bar x$ satisfies $\Pr(\operatorname{dist}(x_{\mathrm{best}}^{k_i},X^*)\to0)=1$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume the genetic algorithm has the stated monotonicity and positive-probability properties. With binary encoding, its best population objective value converges almost surely to the global minimum, and the probability that the population contains a global minimizer tends to one. With continuous encoding on a compact domain and a continuous objective, any convergent subsequence of best population points approaches the global solution set almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \text{The genetic algorithm satisfies the monotonicity and positive-probability assumptions.}
f^*=\min_{x\in\Omega}f(x),\qquad X^*=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in\Omega}f(x).
\text{For part (i), the points are binary encoded.}
\text{For part (ii), the points are continuously encoded, }\Omega\text{ is compact, }f\in\mathcal C^0,\text{ and }x_{\mathrm{best}}^{k_i}\to\bar x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr\!\left(\lim_{k\to\infty}f_{\mathrm{best}}^k=f^*\right)=1,\quad \lim_{k\to\infty}\Pr(P^k\cap X^*\neq\varnothing)=1;\qquad \Pr\!\left(\operatorname{dist}(x_{\mathrm{best}}^{k_i},X^*)\to0\right)=1\ \text{under the assumptions of part (ii).}

children.title: Solution-Pool Management
children.top_down_role: Retention and organization of multiple feasible solutions.

assumptions_latex: Every pool member is a validated feasible point.
The capacity is an integer \(M\ge 1\).
A deterministic ranking rule orders admissible pool members.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained pool \(\mathcal{S}\) contains at most \(M\) validated feasible points and equals the top-ranked subset of all admitted candidates under the declared ranking and duplicate-equivalence rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-limited storage of multiple validated feasible solutions under an explicit ranking rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal{S}=\varnothing\). For each validated feasible candidate \(x\), first apply the declared duplicate-equivalence test. If an equivalent representative exists, retain the better-ranked representative according to \(\rho\); otherwise insert \(x\). Sort candidates using \(\rho\) with deterministic tie-breaking and, when \(|\mathcal{S}|>M\), remove the lowest-ranked members until \(|\mathcal{S}|=M\). Output \(\mathcal{S}\) together with objective values, validation metadata, and ranking keys needed to reproduce every admission and eviction decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution-pool manager validates, deduplicates, ranks, and capacity-limits feasible candidates while retaining metadata that makes admissions and evictions reproducible.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Pool Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits solution-pool management, but ranking, duplicate equivalence, metadata requirements, and the claimed top-ranked-subset invariant need a source or an explicit established system specification.

children.title: Pool Diversity Policies
children.top_down_role: Criteria for preserving structurally or numerically distinct solutions.

assumptions_latex: Candidate points lie in a metric space \((X,d)\).
The separation threshold is \(\delta>0\).
Objective admissibility is tested before diversity admission.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pool \(\mathcal{S}\subset X\) is \(\delta\)-diverse exactly when \[d(x,y)\ge\delta\quad\text{for all distinct }x,y\in\mathcal{S}.\] An admission policy preserves this invariant by accepting a new point only if it is separated from every retained point, or by replacing conflicting points while rechecking all pairwise distances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric minimum-separation condition for diversity among retained feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space and let \(\delta>0\). A finite solution pool \(\mathcal{S}\subset X\) satisfies the minimum-separation diversity policy when every distinct pair of retained points has distance at least \(\delta\). For a candidate \(z\), direct admission is permitted only if \(d(z,x)\ge\delta\) for every \(x\in\mathcal{S}\). Any quality-based replacement among conflicting points must leave the resulting pool pairwise \(\delta\)-separated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum-separation diversity policy retains only solutions whose pairwise metric distances are at least the chosen threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Pool Diversity Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role correctly matches a minimum-separation diversity policy, but no source supports selecting this particular metric policy for the terminal container.

children.title: Incumbent–Pool Synchronization
children.top_down_role: Consistency between the best-known solution and retained solution collections.

assumptions_latex: The incumbent and solution pool contain only validated feasible points.
The pool ranking places smaller objective values first.
Updates are serialized or atomic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After synchronization, either both structures are empty or \[x^{\mathrm{inc}}\in\mathcal{S},\qquad U=f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})=\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}}f(x).\] Hence the incumbent and pool expose the same best validated objective value to all search components.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic consistency invariant between the best-solution state and a ranked feasible-solution pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Synchronize the states as one atomic transaction. Insert every newly validated incumbent into \(\mathcal{S}\), subject to capacity handling that never evicts the best-ranked member. After any pool admission, eviction, or objective correction, select a minimizer of \(f\) over \(\mathcal{S}\) using deterministic tie-breaking and assign it to \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\), with \(U=f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})\). If \(\mathcal{S}=\varnothing\), mark the incumbent absent and set \(U=+\infty\). Publish the transaction only after both states satisfy the displayed invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Atomic synchronization keeps the incumbent inside the pool and equal to its best validated member, including after admissions, evictions, or corrections.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent–Pool Synchronization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the stated consistency invariant, but mandatory incumbent membership, best-member retention, empty-state handling, and atomic synchronization are implementation policies without cited support.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-State Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe reuse of node relaxations in deterministic branch-and-bound search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let node \(v\) have region \(X_v\), relaxation \(R_v\), and certified lower bound \(L_v\). A stored relaxation state may be reused at node \(w\) only after validating that its objective, constraints, variable domains, numerical tolerances, and relaxation construction remain compatible with \(X_w\). Reused cuts or estimators must remain valid on \(X_w\). The resulting bound \(L_w\) may prune \(w\) only when \(L_w\leq \inf_{x\in X_w} f(x)\) is certified and \(L_w\geq U-\varepsilon\), where \(U\) is the incumbent value and \(\varepsilon\geq0\) is the prescribed absolute gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse is safe only after compatibility checks preserve relaxation validity and the resulting bound remains certified for the current node.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is minimized by deterministic spatial branch-and-bound.
Every reused relaxation component is valid throughout the receiving node region.
\(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validated reuse preserves the correctness of node lower bounds and gap-based pruning.

children.title: Checkpoint Management
children.top_down_role: Capture and retention of recoverable global-search state.

knowledge_statements.title: Checkpoint Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic persistence of a deterministic global solver's resumable state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given search state \(S_k=(Q_k,U_k,x_k^{\mathrm{inc}},M_k,C_k)\) at synchronization index \(k\), serialize the open-node pool, incumbent, model metadata, certified relaxation data, and deterministic-control metadata. Attach a format version and integrity digest, write the image to temporary storage, verify its digest, and atomically publish it as checkpoint \(K_k\). A checkpoint is committed only after every component required to resume without invalidating bounds is durable. Retain at least one previously verified checkpoint. The output is the newest committed \(K_k\), together with its compatibility metadata and integrity status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A checkpoint atomically records all state needed for valid resumption and is committed only after integrity and durability checks succeed.
assumptions_latex: The solver state admits a finite serialization at synchronization index \(k\).
The storage layer provides an atomic publication operation.
Persisted bounds and cuts carry sufficient validity metadata.

children.title: Restart Management
children.top_down_role: Resumption of interrupted search from retained state.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated restoration and continuation from a committed search checkpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a committed checkpoint \(K_k\), first verify its integrity digest and format version. Compare its model fingerprint, objective sense, variable domains, tolerances, relaxation configuration, and solver semantics with the current run. Restore only compatible open nodes, incumbent data, certified bounds, cuts, counters, and deterministic-control state; otherwise reject or conservatively discard incompatible components. Revalidate every retained incumbent for feasibility and every retained node bound for validity. Resume from restored state \(S_k'\), preserving the original termination test. If no valid checkpoint exists, initialize a fresh search rather than using uncertified state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart verifies integrity and compatibility, revalidates retained certificates, and resumes only from state that preserves search correctness.
assumptions_latex: \(K_k\) was produced by an atomic checkpoint procedure.
The current solver can test component-level state compatibility.
Revalidation procedures are available for feasible incumbents and certified node bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restored search state \(S_k'\) contains no accepted component whose validity is unsupported under the current run.

children.title: Search Replay

knowledge_statements.title: Search Replay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic reconstruction of a recorded global-search execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_0\) be an initial state and \(E=(e_1,\ldots,e_m)\) an ordered event log containing every nondeterministic choice relevant to search evolution, including node selection, branching, random seeds, message delivery order, and tie breaking. For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), verify that event \(e_i\) is enabled in state \(S_{i-1}\), then apply the recorded transition \(S_i=T(S_{i-1},e_i)\). Stop with a divergence report at the first failed precondition or mismatched state digest. Otherwise output \(S_m\) and the verified digest sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replay reapplies a complete ordered event log and reports the first transition or state digest that diverges.
assumptions_latex: The transition map \(T\) is deterministic once each recorded event is fixed.
The log records all choices capable of changing the search state.
State digests are stable across the replay-compatible execution environment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful replay reconstructs the recorded state sequence \((S_0,\ldots,S_m)\) up to the chosen digest equivalence.

children.title: State-Compatibility Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: State-Compatibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate governing persisted solver-state reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For persisted component \(c\) and current run configuration \(r\), define \(\operatorname{Compat}(c,r)\) to hold exactly when the serialization format is readable, the model identity and objective sense agree, all referenced variables and constraints retain their meanings, numerical conventions preserve the component's claimed validity, and the producing algorithm's semantics are supported. Additionally, a bound, cut, relaxation, or incumbent must pass its component-specific validity check under \(r\). Components failing \(\operatorname{Compat}(c,r)\) must be rejected or transformed into conservative information whose validity is independently recertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persisted state is compatible only when representation, model semantics, numerical conventions, and component-specific validity all survive the configuration change.
assumptions_latex: Each persisted component carries its producing configuration and semantic metadata.
The current run exposes component-specific validation procedures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only components satisfying \(\operatorname{Compat}(c,r)\), or independently recertified conservative transforms, may affect the resumed search.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Memory Tree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel branch-and-bound using shared node and incumbent state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a concurrent open-node pool \(Q\) with the root and a shared incumbent value \(U=+\infty\). Each worker repeatedly removes a node \(v\), computes a certified lower bound \(L_v\), prunes when \(L_v\geq U-\varepsilon\), otherwise generates children and inserts them into \(Q\). A feasible point \(x\) with \(f(x)<U\) updates the incumbent atomically. Terminate only when a concurrency-safe detector establishes that no worker is active and \(Q\) is empty. Output the incumbent and its value; synchronization must make every pruning read consistent with some valid incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers share the node pool and incumbent, using atomic updates and safe termination detection while retaining certified pruning decisions.
assumptions_latex: Every node bound is valid for its node region.
Updates to the incumbent and concurrent node pool are linearizable or equivalently safe.
The node partition and sequential pruning rule define a convergent branch-and-bound method.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed-Memory Tree Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-passing branch-and-bound with partitioned node ownership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the open search nodes among processes as local pools \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_p\). Process \(i\) repeatedly bounds, prunes, and branches nodes in \(Q_i\), sends transferable nodes to other processes according to a load policy, and broadcasts improving feasible incumbents. Each process prunes only with a received or local incumbent value known to be feasible. A distributed termination protocol must establish simultaneously that every \(Q_i\) is empty, every process is idle, and no node-transfer message is in transit. The output is the best globally communicated feasible incumbent and the certified terminal gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Processes own local node pools, exchange work and feasible incumbents, and terminate only after globally detecting no work in transit.
assumptions_latex: Each local node bound is certified on its represented region.
Node transfer preserves complete ownership of every unpruned search region.
Communication is reliable, although delivery may be delayed.

children.title: Asynchronous Bound Exchange

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Bound Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe dissemination of certified global or regional bounds without synchronization barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each process \(i\) maintains a certified lower bound \(B_i\) for its owned unresolved regions and tags every publication with an epoch and ownership descriptor. On receipt of message \((B_j,e_j,D_j)\), a process accepts it only if the certificate applies to descriptor \(D_j\) in epoch \(e_j\). A global lower bound may be formed as the minimum of accepted bounds over a complete, nonoverlapping cover of all unresolved regions. Delayed bounds may weaken this aggregate but must not replace a newer bound unless their covered region and epoch remain valid. No bound may justify pruning outside its certified region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Processes exchange tagged certified bounds asynchronously; aggregation is valid only across a complete current cover of unresolved regions.
assumptions_latex: Every published bound is certified for its stated region descriptor.
Ownership and epoch metadata identify the unresolved regions covered by each message.
Message delay does not alter the mathematical validity of an unchanged regional certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted messages yield only valid regional bounds, and their minimum is a valid global lower bound when their descriptors form a complete current cover.

children.title: Asynchronous Incumbent Exchange

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Incumbent Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-free propagation of feasible incumbent improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, each process stores a feasible incumbent pair \((x_i,U_i)\). When process \(i\) finds feasible \(x\) with \(f(x)<U_i\), it sets \((x_i,U_i)=(x,f(x))\) and asynchronously publishes the pair with model and feasibility metadata. Upon receiving \((x,U)\), process \(j\) validates model identity, feasibility, and objective value, then replaces its incumbent exactly when \(U<U_j\). Thus accepted incumbent values are monotonically nonincreasing. A delayed feasible incumbent may cause extra node processing, but it cannot invalidate pruning performed with an earlier, larger feasible value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers asynchronously publish feasible improvements and accept only validated lower-valued incumbents, making local incumbent values monotonically improve.
assumptions_latex: All processes solve the same minimization model and objective.
An accepted point is independently checkable for feasibility and objective value.
Messages are not required to arrive in publication order.

children.title: Message Freshness Policies
children.top_down_role: Handling of delayed, duplicated, or superseded search-state messages.

knowledge_statements.title: Message Freshness Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance rule for versioned asynchronous search messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a message by \(m=(\tau,s,e,D,P)\), where \(\tau\) is its type, \(s\) its sender, \(e\) its epoch or sequence tag, \(D\) its scope descriptor, and \(P\) its payload. A freshness policy accepts \(m\) only if its model fingerprint matches the receiver, its scope is still meaningful, and its tag is not dominated by the last accepted tag for the same sender, type, and scope. A dominated message may nevertheless be accepted when its payload is independently valid and combined monotonically, such as a strictly improving feasible incumbent. Otherwise it is discarded or retained solely for diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freshness combines model identity, live scope, version ordering, and payload monotonicity to decide whether an asynchronous message may affect search.
assumptions_latex: Messages carry authenticated sender, type, scope, and ordering metadata.
The receiver maintains the last accepted tag for each relevant message stream.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted messages are either current for their stream or independently valid monotone improvements.

Each event chooses either one uniformly random other node for unicast or every other node for broadcast and samples a message size from a normal or uniform burst distribution. It displays F(x)=1-e^{\lambda x}; when \lambda>0 and x>0, this quantity is negative and therefore cannot be a CDF.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Information Boundaries

children.title: Load-Balancing Policies
children.top_down_role: Static, dynamic, centralized, or decentralized policies for distributing search work.

knowledge_statements.title: Load-Balancing Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive redistribution of open search nodes among parallel workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At balancing epoch \(k\), assign each worker \(i\) an estimated remaining load \(W_i(k)=\sum_{v\in Q_i} w(v)\), where \(w(v)\geq0\) estimates node-processing effort. If \(\max_i W_i(k)-\min_i W_i(k)>\theta\), select a donor with high load and a receiver with low load, then transfer a subset \(T\subseteq Q_i\) whose estimated weight reduces the imbalance. Transfer must atomically move ownership of every node in \(T\), including its certified state. Repeat until the imbalance threshold, communication budget, or termination condition is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate worker loads and transfer ownership-preserving node batches from overloaded to underloaded workers until imbalance or communication limits are met.
assumptions_latex: Each open node has a nonnegative workload estimate \(w(v)\).
A node-transfer protocol prevents duplication or loss of ownership.
Balancing does not alter node bounds or branching semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy redistributes estimated work while preserving complete and unique ownership of all open nodes.

notation.meaning: open-node pool owned by worker i
estimated load of worker i at epoch k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parallel tree-search balancing transfers estimated work while preserving unique node ownership
work estimator and trigger threshold are policy-dependent

children.title: Work-Stealing Policies
children.top_down_role: Victim selection, steal granularity, locality, and contention regimes in parallel search.

assumptions_latex: There are \(P\ge 2\) workers and a finite set of independently processable search tasks.
Each task preserves validated lower bounds and incumbent updates under migration between workers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, every generated task has been processed or validly pruned, independently of which worker executed it.

notation.meaning: Deque of pending tasks owned by worker i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard randomized work-stealing scheme specialized to validated search tasks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational policy for migrating validated branch-and-bound tasks among parallel workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize each worker \(i\in\{1,\ldots,P\}\) with a deque \(Q_i\), distributing the initial search tasks among these deques. A busy worker removes a task from its designated owner end, processes it, and places any generated child tasks onto that same end. An idle worker samples a victim \(j\ne i\); if \(Q_j\) contains a stealable task, it atomically removes one from the opposite end and resumes processing, otherwise it samples again or waits. Incumbent updates are merged by taking the best validated feasible objective value. Stop only after a termination detector establishes that every \(Q_i\) is empty and no task or steal operation is in flight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Busy workers process locally generated search tasks; idle workers steal from other deques. Termination requires global quiescence, so migration cannot omit pending validated tasks.
knowledge_statements.title: Work-Stealing Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the policy leaf, but the global-quiescence and task-preservation guarantees depend on a correctly implemented atomic deque and distributed termination protocol. Standard-field rationale alone does not establish these operational guarantees.

children.title: Steal-Policy Load Effects
children.top_down_role: Effects of stealing behavior on utilization, locality, communication overhead, and worker idleness.

assumptions_latex: A successful steal transfers one indivisible task from donor \(d\) to idle worker \(r\).
The transferred task has estimated remaining work \(s>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The steal decreases quadratic load dispersion exactly when \(W_d-W_r>s\).

notation.meaning: Estimated remaining work at worker i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic load-dispersion effect of transferring one task
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step load effect under an additive estimated-work model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the pre-steal estimated loads be \(W_1,\ldots,W_P\ge 0\), and let a steal transfer work \(s\) from donor \(d\) to receiver \(r\), producing \(W_d'=W_d-s\), \(W_r'=W_r+s\), and \(W_i'=W_i\) otherwise. The mean \(\bar W\) is unchanged. For the quadratic dispersion \(V=\sum_{i=1}^P(W_i-\bar W)^2\), the exact change is \[V'-V=2s\bigl(s-(W_d-W_r)\bigr).\] Consequently, the steal reduces dispersion precisely when \(W_d-W_r>s\), leaves it unchanged when equality holds, and increases it when \(W_d-W_r<s\). Thus stealing a coarse task can overshoot load balance even when the donor initially has more work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transferring estimated work s reduces quadratic load imbalance exactly when the donor exceeds the receiver by more than s; coarse steals can increase imbalance.
knowledge_statements.title: Steal-Policy Load Effects

children.title: Parallel-Load Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes featuring persistent imbalance, excessive stealing, resource contention, or depleted work pools.

assumptions_latex: Tasks are indivisible and cannot be preempted or subdivided after assignment.
At least one task has processing time \(H>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The makespan-to-average-load ratio can approach \(P\), so stealing alone provides no uniform near-perfect load balance.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indivisible-task lower bound for parallel load balancing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Granularity boundary for nonpreemptive work stealing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P\ge2\), consider one indivisible task of duration \(H\) and \(P-1\) tasks of duration \(\varepsilon>0\). Every nonpreemptive schedule, including any work-stealing schedule, has makespan \(T_P\ge H\). The total work is \(T_1=H+(P-1)\varepsilon\), so the ideal average-load lower bound is \(T_1/P\), while \[\frac{T_P}{T_1/P}\ge \frac{PH}{H+(P-1)\varepsilon}\longrightarrow P\quad\text{as }\varepsilon/H\to0.\] Hence no victim-selection or deque policy can ensure balanced completion when a dominant task is neither divisible nor preemptible; additional parallelism inside that task or finer task generation is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single dominant indivisible task forces nearly serial completion: relative to average load, the makespan ratio can approach the number of workers.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Load Failure Boundaries
Parallel-Search Reproducibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-independent reproducibility expressed as termination and confluence modulo irrelevant task ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_0\) be the initial search state, let \(\to\) denote an admissible atomic search transition, and let \(\operatorname{can}\) remove only semantically irrelevant representation differences such as task ordering. For each fair terminating schedule \(\sigma\), let \(S_\sigma\) be its terminal state. The search is reproducible modulo canonicalization when, for every pair of such schedules \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\), \[\operatorname{can}(S_\sigma)=\operatorname{can}(S_\tau).\] A sufficient condition is that the reachable transition system terminates and is confluent modulo canonicalization: whenever \(S_0\to^*A\) and \(S_0\to^*B\), there exist states \(A'\) and \(B'\) such that \(A\to^*A'\), \(B\to^*B'\), and \(\operatorname{can}(A')=\operatorname{can}(B')\). Deterministic arithmetic, fixed tie-breaking, schedule-independent stopping criteria, and deterministic associative, commutative, and idempotent state merges are useful implementation requirements but must collectively establish this confluence property, including for incumbent-dependent pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel search is reproducible when every fair terminating schedule reaches the same canonical terminal state. Termination and confluence modulo irrelevant task ordering are sufficient; deterministic merges alone are not.
assumptions_latex: The transition relation \(\to\) includes task expansion, pruning, communication, incumbent updates, and termination-relevant state changes.
Every schedule under comparison is admissible, fair, and terminating.
The canonicalization \(\operatorname{can}\) removes only representation differences that do not affect the solver result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all compared schedules \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\), \(\operatorname{can}(S_\sigma)=\operatorname{can}(S_\tau)\).

notation.meaning: Terminal state reached under schedule sigma
Canonicalization removing semantically irrelevant representation differences

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: termination and confluence modulo canonicalization imply schedule-independent terminal states

children.title: Directed-Rounding Modes
children.top_down_role: Rounding-mode choices used to preserve conservative numerical enclosures.

assumptions_latex: The floating-point format \(\mathbb F\) contains signed infinities and supports correctly rounded directed operations.
The exact real result lies within the format's representable extended range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every real \(x\), \(\operatorname{RD}(x)\le x\le\operatorname{RU}(x)\).

notation.meaning: Floating-point numbers in the chosen format

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard IEEE-style definitions of directed rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed rounding for constructing floating-point enclosures of real quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real number \(x\), define downward and upward rounding in the extended floating-point set by \[\operatorname{RD}(x)=\max\{f\in\mathbb F\cup\{-\infty\}:f\le x\},\qquad \operatorname{RU}(x)=\min\{f\in\mathbb F\cup\{+\infty\}:f\ge x\}.\] Thus \(\operatorname{RD}(x)\le x\le\operatorname{RU}(x)\). Rounding toward zero and rounding to nearest do not, by themselves, select the required enclosure direction. For a primitive real operation \(x\circ y\), its outward floating-point enclosure is \([\operatorname{RD}(x\circ y),\operatorname{RU}(x\circ y)]\), provided both directed evaluations implement the specified real operation without unmodeled transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Downward rounding returns the greatest floating-point value no larger than the exact result; upward rounding returns the least one no smaller.
knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Rounding Modes

children.title: Outward-Bound Construction
children.top_down_role: Construction of conservative lower, upper, interval, or residual bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Outward-Bound Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Natural interval evaluation of a supported expression over an interval box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an interval box \(X\) and a finite expression tree defining a real-valued expression \(f\). Replace each variable by its component interval and each real constant \(c\) by an interval containing \(c\), such as \([\operatorname{RD}(c),\operatorname{RU}(c)]\). Traverse the tree from leaves to root. For a primitive \(\phi\) with child intervals \(I_1,\ldots,I_k\), compute an interval \(J\) satisfying \[\{\phi(z_1,\ldots,z_k):z_j\in I_j\text{ and }\phi(z_1,\ldots,z_k)\text{ is defined}\}\subseteq J,\] rounding every finite lower bound downward and every finite upper bound upward. The required extrema may involve several endpoint combinations or a validated range algorithm; they are not generally obtained from corresponding lower and upper input endpoints. If a domain singularity or unsupported exceptional case prevents a valid enclosure, split the input or return an enclosure-failure status. The root interval is \(F(X)\), and successful completion guarantees \(f(x)\in F(X)\) for every \(x\in X\) where the expression is defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the expression tree with validated primitive interval extensions, rounding result bounds outward. Each primitive must enclose its full range over the child intervals; unsupported domain cases require splitting or failure.
assumptions_latex: The expression \(f\) is a finite composition of supported real primitive operations over an interval box \(X\).
Each primitive implementation encloses its full defined range over its input intervals and rounds finite result bounds outward.
Domain singularities, overflow, and other exceptional cases are represented by valid extended intervals, resolved by splitting, or reported as enclosure failures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\) at which the expression is defined, successful construction returns \(F(X)\) with \(f(x)\in F(X)\).

notation.meaning: Child intervals supplied to a primitive operation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: natural interval extension using outward-rounded validated primitive range enclosures

children.title: Containment Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks supporting enclosure preservation across arithmetic, libraries, and solver interfaces.

assumptions_latex: Every leaf interval contains its represented real input or constant.
Every primitive operation supplies a checkable local enclosure contract.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance of all local contracts certifies \(f(X)\subseteq F(X)\).

notation.meaning: Exact range of node v over the input box
Computed interval stored at node v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compositional certificate for interval-expression containment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional validation certificate for an outward-rounded expression tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A containment certificate assigns an interval \(I_v=[\ell_v,u_v]\) to every node \(v\) of the expression tree. Each leaf certificate verifies that its represented value lies in \(I_v\). For an internal node \(v\) with primitive operation \(\phi_v\) and children \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\), the local certificate verifies \[\{\phi_v(z_1,\ldots,z_k):z_j\in I_{v_j}\text{ and the operation is defined}\}\subseteq I_v.\] It must also record any domain exclusion, overflow, or entire-interval convention used. If every local check succeeds, the root interval \(F(X)=I_{\mathrm{root}}\) certifies containment of the exact range \(f(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intervals attached to expression-tree nodes certify containment when every leaf contains its value and every parent encloses the exact operation on its child intervals.
knowledge_statements.title: Containment Validation

children.title: Outward-Bound Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical environments where rounding control or enclosure containment becomes unreliable.

assumptions_latex: Arithmetic uses binary floating point with precision \(p\) and round-to-nearest.
Both interval endpoints are computed without directed rounding or an equivalent error enlargement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nearest-rounded endpoint evaluation can return an interval that excludes the exact range.

notation.meaning: Unit roundoff scale at one for precision p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: midpoint tie demonstrates failure of nearest rounding for outward enclosures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete containment failure when outward rounding is replaced by nearest rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the binary format have precision \(p\), let \(X=[1,1]\), and let \(Y=[2^{-p},2^{-p}]\). The exact Minkowski sum is \(X+Y=[1+2^{-p},1+2^{-p}]\). At magnitude one, this value is halfway between consecutive floating-point numbers \(1\) and \(1+2^{1-p}\). Under ties-to-even round-to-nearest, both naively computed endpoints may round to \(1\), producing \([1,1]\). Since \(1+2^{-p}\notin[1,1]\), containment fails. The same risk arises from compiler reassociation, hidden precision changes, or unsupported exceptional values whenever the claimed directed-rounding semantics are not preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding two singleton intervals at a rounding midpoint can yield [1,1] under nearest rounding even though the exact sum is strictly larger than one.
knowledge_statements.title: Outward-Bound Failure Boundaries

children.title: Feasibility Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Absolute, relative, scaled, or constraint-specific thresholds for feasibility assessment.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Tolerances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled absolute feasibility test for finite nonlinear constraint and variable-bound families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). For finite index sets \(I\), \(J\), and \(K\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) for \(i\in I\) be inequality constraints \(g_i(x)\le0\), let \(h_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) for \(j\in J\) be equality constraints \(h_j(x)=0\), and let \(\ell_k\le x_k\le u_k\) for \(k\in K\) be variable bounds. Choose scales \(s_i>0\), \(t_j>0\), and \(b_k>0\), and define \([a]_+=\max\{a,0\}\). For \(\varepsilon_f\ge0\), define \[r_f(x)=\max\left\{\max_{i\in I}\frac{[g_i(x)]_+}{s_i},\ \max_{j\in J}\frac{|h_j(x)|}{t_j},\ \max_{k\in K}\frac{[\ell_k-x_k]_+}{b_k},\ \max_{k\in K}\frac{[x_k-u_k]_+}{b_k}\right\},\] with the maximum of an empty family defined as zero. The point \(x\) is tolerance-feasible exactly when \(r_f(x)\le\varepsilon_f\). Unless \(\varepsilon_f=0\) or separate validated enclosures establish the exact constraints, this operational status does not imply exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is tolerance-feasible when its largest scaled inequality, equality, or variable-bound violation is no greater than the configured feasibility tolerance; positive tolerance alone does not certify exact feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The decision vector satisfies \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
The constraint index sets \(I\), \(J\), and \(K\) are finite.
Every scale \(s_i\), \(t_j\), and \(b_k\) used in the test is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), tolerance-feasibility is equivalent to \(r_f(x)\le\varepsilon_f\).

notation.meaning: Finite inequality, equality, and bounded-variable index sets
Strictly positive constraint and bound scales
Positive part of a real scalar
Maximum scaled constraint and bound violation

children.title: Bound Tolerances
children.top_down_role: Thresholds used when comparing lower bounds, upper bounds, incumbents, or reported gaps.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with certified global lower bound \(L\).
The incumbent value \(U\) comes from a certified feasible point, so \(L\le f^\star\le U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U-L\le\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U|\}\), then \(U-f^\star\) obeys the same bound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-relative certified optimality-gap test for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^\star\) be the exact global minimum, with certified bounds \(L\le f^\star\le U\). For tolerances \(\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_r\ge0\), define \(\tau_b(U)=\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U|\}\). The bound-gap stopping condition is \[U-L\le\tau_b(U).\] When it holds, the incumbent satisfies \(0\le U-f^\star\le\tau_b(U)\). If no certified feasible incumbent exists, \(U\) cannot be used in this test; if \(L\) is merely heuristic, the displayed inequality is not a certificate of global near-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower bound and feasible incumbent may stop when their gap meets an absolute-relative tolerance, which then bounds incumbent suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Tolerances

children.title: Tolerance-Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of feasibility thresholds with bound, gap, integrality, and termination thresholds.

assumptions_latex: A minimization solver uses feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon_f\) and bound-gap tolerance \(\tau_b\).
Constraint and objective enclosures have known worst-case errors \(\eta_f\) and \(\eta_b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified status requires feasibility and gap margins to dominate their respective enclosure errors; otherwise only an operational status is justified.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separates operational tolerances from validation-error budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling operational feasibility and bound gaps with numerical enclosure errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Tolerance settings must preserve the logical roles of the incumbent and lower bound. An incumbent may support a certified gap only after exact feasibility is validated, or after its constraint enclosures lie within the feasible side with margin at least \(\eta_f\). Likewise, pruning or termination from \(U-L\le\tau_b\) is certified only when outward-enclosure errors are already included in \(U\) and \(L\), or when the comparison retains a margin of at least \(\eta_b\). If \(\varepsilon_f\) merely defines a relaxed feasible set, a point accepted using \(\varepsilon_f>0\) may be reported operationally feasible but must not supply a certified \(U\) for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility and gap tolerances must account for enclosure errors, and a merely tolerance-feasible point cannot furnish a certified incumbent for the exact problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Coupling Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the coupling-regimes leaf, but the meanings of eta_f and eta_b are insufficiently specified. It is unclear whether they are one-sided errors, combined endpoint errors, or already included in outward enclosures, so the asserted required margins cannot be evaluated reliably without a precise authoritative formulation.

children.title: Tolerance-Induced Status Risks
children.top_down_role: Status instability, premature acceptance, or missed certification caused by incompatible tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Induced Status Risks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: False global-optimality status caused by using relaxed feasibility as exact feasibility in incumbent-based pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R} x\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\ge0.\] The exact optimum is \(f^\star=0\), and the root problem has the certified lower bound \(B=0\). Let \(\varepsilon_f>0\), and suppose the operational rule accepts every \(x\ge-\varepsilon_f\). Then \(\hat x=-\varepsilon_f/2\) is tolerance-feasible but not exactly feasible. If the solver incorrectly installs it as an exact incumbent, it obtains \(U=f(\hat x)=-\varepsilon_f/2<f^\star\). A minimization branch-and-bound rule that prunes a node whenever its lower bound satisfies \(B\ge U\) then prunes the root because \(0\ge-\varepsilon_f/2\). If empty-tree termination trusts this invalid incumbent, the solver can report global optimality with value \(U\), even though no exactly feasible point has that value. Thus relaxed feasibility must not be used to form a certified incumbent for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimizing x subject to x being nonnegative, accepting a slightly negative point as an exact incumbent places the incumbent below the true optimum. Ordinary incumbent-based pruning can then discard the whole search tree and cause a false global-optimality report.
assumptions_latex: The solver applies a feasibility tolerance \(\varepsilon_f>0\) to the constraint \(x\ge0\).
A tolerance-feasible point is incorrectly installed as an exactly feasible incumbent.
A node with certified minimization lower bound \(B\) is pruned when \(B\ge U\), and empty-tree termination trusts the installed incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solver can report global optimality at \(U=-\varepsilon_f/2\), although the true feasible optimum is \(f^\star=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit false-optimality counterexample from an invalid tolerance-based incumbent

children.title: Variable Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices for decision-variable ranges, units, and transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal affine scaling of a box-constrained smooth minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\ge 1\), \(l,u,c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with \(l_j<u_j\) and \(d_j>0\) for every \(j\). Define \(x=c+Dz\) and \(Z=[D^{-1}(l-c),D^{-1}(u-c)]\). Then \(z\mapsto c+Dz\) is a bijection from \(Z\) to \([l,u]\). If \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \([l,u]\) and \(\phi(z)=f(c+Dz)\), then \(
abla\phi(z)=D
abla f(c+Dz)\) and \(
abla^2\phi(z)=D
abla^2f(c+Dz)D\). Consequently, the global minimizers of \(f\) over \([l,u]\) correspond bijectively to the global minimizers of \(\phi\) over \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive diagonal affine change of variables bijectively maps the scaled box to the original box; for a twice continuously differentiable objective it gives the stated gradient and Hessian transformations and preserves box-constrained global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(n\ge 1\), \(l,u,c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(l_j<u_j\) for every \(j\).
\(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) with \(d_j>0\) for every \(j\).
\(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \([l,u]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map \(z\mapsto c+Dz\) bijects \(Z\) with \([l,u]\), transforms derivatives by the stated chain-rule formulas, and bijectively preserves global minimizers of the box-constrained problem.

notation.meaning: Translation vector and positive diagonal scaling matrix.

children.title: Constraint Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices for residuals, rows, coefficients, and feasibility tests.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive row scaling for finite families of equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(K\) be finite index sets, with constraints \(g_i(x)\le 0\) for \(i\in I\) and \(h_k(x)=0\) for \(k\in K\). For scale factors \(s_i>0\) and \(t_k>0\), define \(\widetilde g_i(x)=s_i g_i(x)\) and \(\widetilde h_k(x)=t_k h_k(x)\). Then, for every \(x\), exact feasibility of all original constraints is equivalent to exact feasibility of all scaled constraints. If \(\tau_i\ge0\) and \(\eta_k\ge0\), the tests \(\widetilde g_i(x)\le\tau_i\) and \(|\widetilde h_k(x)|\le\eta_k\) are respectively equivalent to \(g_i(x)\le\tau_i/s_i\) and \(|h_k(x)|\le\eta_k/t_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row scaling preserves exact feasibility for every constraint, while nonnegative scaled residual tolerances convert to original units by division by the corresponding positive scale factor.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(K\) are finite index sets for inequality and equality constraints.
\(s_i>0\) for every \(i\in I\), and \(t_k>0\) for every \(k\in K\).
\(\tau_i\ge0\) and \(\eta_k\ge0\) are residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive row scaling preserves the exact feasible set, and each scaled residual tolerance converts to original units by division by its scale factor.

notation.meaning: Finite inequality- and equality-constraint index sets.
Positive inequality and equality scale factors.
Nonnegative tolerances in scaled residual units.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multiplication by positive constants preserves inequality signs and equality zeros
REQUEST_SOURCES: authoritative numerical optimization reference with a specific constraint-scaling locator

children.title: Objective Scaling
children.top_down_role: Objective normalization relevant to bounds, gaps, penalties, and solver tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive affine scaling of a real-valued minimization objective on a fixed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a nonempty feasible set, let \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\), and define \(\widetilde f(x)=\alpha f(x)+\beta\) with \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\). For all \(x,y\in F\), \(f(x)\le f(y)\) if and only if \(\widetilde f(x)\le\widetilde f(y)\). Hence \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\widetilde f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\). If \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), then \(\widetilde f^\star=\alpha f^\star+\beta\). Original-unit bounds \(L\le f^\star\le U\) transform to \(\alpha L+\beta\le\widetilde f^\star\le\alpha U+\beta\), so the absolute gap becomes \(\alpha(U-L)\); relative stopping tolerances require a separately declared normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive affine transformation of a real-valued objective on a fixed feasible set preserves ordering and minimizers, transforms the optimal value and bounds affinely, and multiplies absolute gaps by the positive scale.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty feasible set and \(f:F\to\mathbb{R}\).
\(\widetilde f(x)=\alpha f(x)+\beta\), where \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\).
