children.title: Conditioning Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of sensitivity, coefficient disparity, cancellation, and unstable numerical behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A declared local diagnostic based on a scaled active-constraint Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a point \(x\), let the active constraints be differentiable and let their Jacobian be \(J(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), where \(m\ge n\ge1\) and \(J(x)\) has full column rank. Let \(D_x\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(D_g\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) be positive diagonal matrices, and define \(J_s=D_gJ(x)D_x\). Set \(I_+=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:\|(J_s)_{i:}\|_2>0\}\) and \(R=\max_{i\in I_+}\|(J_s)_{i:}\|_2/\min_{i\in I_+}\|(J_s)_{i:}\|_2\). For declared thresholds \(K\ge1\) and \(R_{\max}\ge1\), call the local scaling diagnostically acceptable exactly when \(\kappa_2(J_s)\le K\) and \(R\le R_{\max}\), where \(\kappa_2(J_s)=\sigma_{\max}(J_s)/\sigma_{\min}(J_s)\). Failure means that at least one declared diagnostic threshold is exceeded; it does not establish solver failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-column-rank active Jacobian, this declared local diagnostic accepts a scaling exactly when the scaled Jacobian's spectral condition number and its nonzero row-norm spread do not exceed their recorded thresholds.
assumptions_latex: The active constraints are differentiable at \(x\), and \(J(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full column rank with \(m\ge n\ge1\).
\(D_x\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(D_g\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) are positive diagonal matrices.
\(K\ge1\) and \(R_{\max}\ge1\) are declared workflow thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaling passes this diagnostic exactly when \(\kappa_2(D_gJ(x)D_x)\le K\) and \(R\le R_{\max}\).

notation.meaning: Indices of nonzero rows of the scaled Jacobian.
Ratio of the largest to smallest nonzero scaled row norm.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: spectral condition numbers and row-norm spreads are standard local diagnostics
REQUEST_SOURCES: numerical optimization reference supporting these diagnostic quantities

children.title: Scaling-Induced Distortion
children.top_down_role: Regimes where scaling obscures residuals, weakens bounds, or destabilizes reported status.

assumptions_latex: An equality constraint is \(g(x)=x=0\) on \(\mathbb{R}\).
The solver applies the fixed scaled residual test \(|s g(x)|\le\tau\), with \(s,	au>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted original residual tube is \(|x|\le\tau/s\), which becomes arbitrarily loose as \(s\downarrow0\) and arbitrarily narrow as \(s\uparrow\infty\).

notation.meaning: Fixed tolerance in scaled residual units.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct algebra gives the tolerance distortion family
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by retaining fixed scaled tolerances under extreme scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the exact constraint \(g(x)=x=0\) and the scaled residual \(\widetilde g(x)=s g(x)\), with \(s>0\). Under the fixed numerical test \(|\widetilde g(x)|\le\tau\), the accepted points are exactly those satisfying \(|x|\le\tau/s\). Thus \(s\downarrow0\) makes the accepted tube arbitrarily large in original units, while \(s\uparrow\infty\) makes it arbitrarily narrow. Positive scaling preserves the exact feasible set, but it distorts numerical feasibility unless tolerances are transformed with the scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed scaled-space tolerances create an original residual tube of radius tolerance divided by scale, so extreme scaling can falsely loosen or tighten feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Distortion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebra, scope, failure-boundary role, and plain/LaTeX correspondence are correct, but the record supplies no inspectable citation. An authoritative scaling or feasibility-tolerance source is required.

assumptions_latex: The minimization problem has optimal value \(f^\star\).
A validated computation proves \(L\le f^\star\) and encloses \(L\) in \([\widehat L-\delta,\widehat L+\delta]\), with \(\delta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The downward-rounded value \(L_{\mathrm{safe}}=\operatorname{rd}_{-}(\widehat L-\delta)\) certifies \(L_{\mathrm{safe}}\le f^\star\).

notation.meaning: Computed approximation and certified absolute error radius.
Rounding toward negative infinity in the output format.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: enclosure monotonicity and downward rounding preserve a minimization lower bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward postprocessing of a validated lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a validated relaxation or dual argument establishes \(L\le f^\star\), while numerical validation establishes \(L\in[\widehat L-\delta,\widehat L+\delta]\) with \(\delta\ge0\). Define \(L_{\mathrm{safe}}=\operatorname{rd}_{-}(\widehat L-\delta)\), where \(\operatorname{rd}_{-}\) rounds toward negative infinity in the stored output format. Then \(L_{\mathrm{safe}}\le\widehat L-\delta\le L\le f^\star\). Reporting \(\widehat L\) itself is not certified unless its rounding and total error have already been enclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtract the validated error radius and round downward; the resulting stored number remains a rigorous lower bound on the minimization optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Safe Dual-Bound Postprocessing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The outward-rounded lower-bound certificate is mathematically sound and fits the terminal container, but no source with a specific locator supports the validated-arithmetic postprocessing convention.

assumptions_latex: A solver claims a certified lower bound \(L\), feasible upper bound \(U\), or optimality gap \(U-L\).
All numerical validations use identified arithmetic and tolerance conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A trail is auditable when replay reconstructs the claimed inequalities \(L\le f^\star\le U\) under the recorded conventions.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and feasible upper bounds.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: replayable inputs, derivations, arithmetic conventions, and hashes are standard certificate provenance requirements
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum replayability condition for a numerical global-optimization certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate audit trail is an immutable bundle \(\mathcal A\) containing the exact model and data identifiers, transformations and scale factors, solver and library versions, parameter and tolerance values, arithmetic and rounding modes, generated relaxation or dual certificate data, incumbent feasibility checks, postprocessing operations, and hashes of replay inputs and outputs. It is auditable if an independent replay using \(\mathcal A\) reconstructs every asserted enclosure and hence verifies \(L\le f^\star\le U\), or explicitly identifies the first unverifiable step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An audit trail records enough immutable model, software, numerical, certificate, and hashing data for an independent replay to reconstruct every claimed bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Audit Trails

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind is suitable, but the proposed minimum contents and replayability criterion are normative and uncited. A certificate or reproducible-computation standard with a specific locator is needed.

assumptions_latex: The search domain \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is explicitly bounded.
The objective \(f\) is given by an analytic formula on an open neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((f,X)\) is an analytic multimodal test instance when \(f\) has at least two distinct isolated local minimizers in \(X\).

notation.meaning: Analytic objective and bounded search domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded analytic objectives with multiple isolated local minima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An analytic multimodal test function instance is a pair \((f,X)\), where \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is an explicitly specified bounded search domain and \(f\) is real analytic on an open neighborhood of \(X\), such that \(f\) has at least two distinct isolated local minimizers \(x^{(1)},x^{(2)}\in X\). A reproducible benchmark record also specifies all constants, dimension restrictions, boundary conventions, optimization sense, and the provenance and accuracy of any claimed global minimizer or optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An analytic multimodal benchmark has an explicit bounded domain, an analytic objective, and at least two distinct isolated local minima, with reference optima separately documented.
knowledge_statements.title: Analytic Multimodal Test Functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition is internally coherent and fits the benchmark-family container, but requiring two isolated local minimizers is a particular convention rather than a universally fixed meaning of multimodality. A benchmark or global-optimization source must support the selected definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines two quantitative descriptors for an objective on the unit interval and records the weight criterion's monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ have global minimum value $m=f(x_*)$. For $\beta>0$ and $\epsilon>0$, define
\[
\Gamma_f(\beta,\epsilon)=\int_0^1\left(1+\frac{f(x)-m}{\epsilon}\right)^{-\beta}\,dx.
\]
Then $0<\Gamma_f(\beta,\epsilon)\le 1$; it is decreasing in $\beta$ and increasing in $\epsilon$. If, for some $\alpha>0$, the following limit exists, define the minimum-sharpness criterion by
\[
\Lambda_f=\lim_{n\to\infty}n^\alpha\sup_{|x|\le 1/n}\bigl[f(x_*+x)-m\bigr]\ge 0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gamma measures the size of the region whose objective values are near the global minimum; it decreases with beta and increases with epsilon. When the stated limit exists, Lambda measures the local sharpness of the global minimum.
assumptions_latex: f:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}
\beta>0
\epsilon>0
\exists\alpha>0\text{ for which the defining limit of }\Lambda_f\text{ exists}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<\Gamma_f(\beta,\epsilon)\le1,\quad \Gamma_f\downarrow\text{ in }\beta,\quad \Gamma_f\uparrow\text{ in }\epsilon,\quad \Lambda_f\ge0

assumptions_latex: A deterministic or seeded generator \(G\) and admissible parameter set \(\Theta\) are specified.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A procedurally generated benchmark set is \(\mathcal B=\{G(\theta,\omega):(\theta,\omega)\in I\}\), where \(G\) is a versioned instance generator, \(\theta\in\Theta\) is a declared parameter vector, \(\omega\) is a recorded random seed or null deterministic seed, and \(I\) is a finite recorded index set. Reproduction requires the generator source or immutable identifier, parameter schema, pseudorandom algorithm, seeds, rejection rules, and postgeneration filters; changing any of these defines a different set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A procedurally generated benchmark set is determined by a versioned generator and a finite record of parameters, seeds, random algorithm, rejection rules, and filters.

knowledge_statements.title: Generation-Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-based stratification of procedurally generated continuous optimization instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a benchmark generator be a map \(G:\Theta\times\Xi\to\mathcal I\), where \(\theta\in\Theta\) contains structural parameters and \(\xi\in\Xi\) is a random seed. Fix a finite, declared measurable partition \(\Theta=\bigsqcup_{k=1}^{K}R_k\). The generation-parameter regime indexed by \(k\) is \(\mathcal B_k=\{G(\theta,\xi):\theta\in R_k,\ \xi\in\Xi\}\). If instances are sampled, the sampling law on \(R_k\times\Xi\), sample count, and rejected or infeasible generations are part of the regime specification; changing any of these defines a different experimental regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generation regime is the set of generated instances associated with one declared parameter region, seed policy, sampling law, and rejection rule.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and every parameter region \(R_k\) are explicitly specified.
The seed space \(\Xi\) and any rejection rule are fixed before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B_k=G(R_k\times\Xi)\) is the benchmark class for regime \(k\).

children.title: Source-Domain Coverage

knowledge_statements.title: Source-Domain Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted coverage of declared application or scientific source domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a benchmark collection be \(\mathcal B=\{I_1,\ldots,I_N\}\), let \(\mathcal D\) be a finite declared set of source domains, and let \(L(I_i)\subseteq\mathcal D\) contain the documented domains of instance \(I_i\). For nonnegative instance weights \(w_i\) with \(\sum_i w_i>0\), define domain coverage by \(c_d=(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_i\mathbf 1\{d\in L(I_i)\})/(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_i)\). The coverage report is the vector \((c_d)_{d\in\mathcal D}\), accompanied by the unlabeled mass and the rule used for multiply labeled instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Source-domain coverage reports the weighted fraction of benchmark instances documented as originating from each declared domain, together with unlabeled and multi-label handling.
assumptions_latex: Each asserted source-domain label is supported by instance provenance metadata.
All weights \(w_i\) are fixed independently of solver outcomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_d\in[0,1]\) quantifies collection coverage of domain \(d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Structure Taxonomy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural, potentially overlapping labels for continuous global optimization models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent an instance \(I\) as minimizing \(f(x)\) over \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq 0\ (i\in P),\ h_j(x)=0\ (j\in Q)\}\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(P,Q\) are finite index sets. Its model-structure signature \(\tau(I)\) records separately every applicable declared representation class of \(f\), each \(g_i\), and each \(h_j\), using classes such as affine, quadratic, polynomial, factorable, or black-box. It also records separability, the declared sparsity pattern, and explicit composite structure when available. Because these properties can overlap, \(\tau(I)\) is a tuple of label sets rather than one exclusive class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy records all applicable representation labels for the objective and constraints separately, together with separability, sparsity, and composite structure; compatible labels may overlap.
assumptions_latex: All variables are continuous, \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is explicitly represented, and \(P,Q\) are finite.
Representation classes and recognition rules are declared before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structural class of \(I\) is the declared signature \(\tau(I)\), not merely the class of its objective.

notation.meaning: finite inequality- and equality-constraint index sets

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reproducible dimension strata based on declared variable-count thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance \(I\) with a positive finite number \(n(I)\) of continuous decision variables after a declared preprocessing convention, fix thresholds \(0=b_0<b_1<\cdots<b_{K-1}<b_K=+\infty\), where \(b_1,\ldots,b_{K-1}\) are positive integers. Define \(D_k=\{I:b_{k-1}<n(I)\leq b_k\}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,K\). Fixed and eliminated variables are counted according to the stated convention. The thresholds and convention must be reported and held constant across solvers; labels such as small or large are otherwise undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dimension classes partition positive-dimensional instances by declared variable-count intervals under a fixed preprocessing and counting convention.
assumptions_latex: Every classified instance satisfies \(n(I)\in\mathbb N\) and \(n(I)\geq1\).
The thresholds and preprocessing convention are fixed independently of performance observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{D_k\}_{k=1}^{K}\) is a disjoint exhaustive partition of the classified instances.

declared dimension threshold in the extended nonnegative integers

knowledge_statements.title: Instance-Scale Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-size strata distinct from decision-space dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a represented instance \(I\), define the scale signature \(s(I)=(n(I),m(I),z(I),e(I))\), where the components count continuous variables, scalar constraints, stored nonzero coefficients, and expression-graph nodes. A scale-class map is a declared function \(\sigma:\mathbb N^4\to\{1,\ldots,L\}\); its classes are \(S_\ell=\{I:\sigma(s(I))=\ell\}\). The representation format, presolve state, counting conventions, and map \(\sigma\) must be fixed, since equal-dimensional models can have substantially different encoded sizes.

children.title: Dimension–Scale Cross-Strata
children.top_down_role: Joint benchmark strata used to distinguish dimensional growth from other forms of scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension–Scale Cross-Strata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint benchmark strata formed from dimension and encoded-scale classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_1,\ldots,D_K\) be a fixed partition by variable dimension and \(S_1,\ldots,S_L\) a fixed partition by encoded instance scale. The dimension–scale cross-stratum indexed by \((k,\ell)\) is \(C_{k\ell}=D_k\cap S_\ell\). Empty intersections are retained or omitted according to a declared reporting rule. For any reported statistic, the number of instances and aggregate weight in each nonempty \(C_{k\ell}\) must be disclosed so that dimension effects are not confounded with representation-scale effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dimension–scale cross-stratum contains exactly those instances belonging simultaneously to one dimension class and one encoded-scale class.
assumptions_latex: \(\{D_k\}_{k=1}^{K}\) and \(\{S_\ell\}_{\ell=1}^{L}\) classify the same benchmark universe.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{C_{k\ell}\}_{k,\ell}\) is the common refinement of the two partitions.

children.title: Scale-Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ranges where resource use, solver behavior, or certificate difficulty changes materially with size.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transitions of dimension–scale class along a parameterized instance family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I(t)\), with \(t\in T\subseteq\mathbb R\), be a parameterized benchmark family, and let \(d(t)\) and \(s(t)\) denote its dimension-class and scale-class indices. A scale-transition point is \(t_0\in T\) for which the pair \((d(t),s(t))\) is not locally constant at \(t_0\). A scale-transition regime is a maximal connected subset \(R\subseteq T\) on which \((d(t),s(t))\) is constant. Reported transitions must distinguish changes in the generated model from changes caused only by preprocessing or representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scale-transition regime is a maximal parameter interval with constant dimension and scale classes; its boundaries are class-change points.
assumptions_latex: The family \(I(t)\) and both classification maps are defined on a common parameter set \(T\).
Representation and preprocessing conventions remain fixed over \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each regime \(R\) is maximal subject to \((d(t),s(t))=(k,\ell)\) for all \(t\in R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scale-transition terminology and regime convention are not standardized and have no cited support. The plain statement additionally specializes maximal connected subsets of an arbitrary parameter set to intervals, which is not valid without further assumptions on the parameter set.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Geometry Taxonomy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric signature of the feasible region under a fixed model representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq0,\ h_j(x)=0\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define its constraint-geometry signature to record whether \(F\) is empty, full-dimensional, convex, polyhedral, connected, bounded, and locally smooth. Local smoothness at a feasible point means that the active constraint gradients satisfy the declared constraint qualification and generate the stated tangent or normal representation. children.title: Nonconvexity Classes

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvexity Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four-way classification by objective and feasible-set convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) over a nonempty feasible set \(F\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), with \(X\) convex. Define \(o(I)=0\) when \(f\) is convex on \(X\), and \(o(I)=1\) otherwise. Define \(c(I)=0\) when \(F\) is convex, and \(c(I)=1\) otherwise. The nonconvexity class of \(I\) is the pair \(\nu(I)=(o(I),c(I))\), distinguishing convex models, objective-only nonconvexity, feasible-set-only nonconvexity, and joint nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An instance is classified by whether its objective is nonconvex and whether its feasible set is nonconvex, yielding four classes.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and \(F\neq\varnothing\).
Convexity is assessed on the declared continuous formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu(I)\in\{0,1\}^2\) uniquely determines the four-way nonconvexity class.

children.title: Regularity Classes
children.top_down_role: Benchmark strata based on smoothness, continuity, differentiability, or local structural regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint regularity levels for all functions defining an instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi_I\) be the finite collection containing the objective and every scalar constraint function, restricted to an open neighborhood \(U\) of the feasible region. Assign \(I\) to the highest common level in the nested ladder \(C^2(U)\subset C^1(U)\subset\operatorname{Lip}_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)\subset C^0(U)\): twice continuously differentiable, continuously differentiable but not twice, locally Lipschitz but not continuously differentiable, continuous but not locally Lipschitz, or discontinuous. Thus the classes are disjoint, and one irregular function determines the common level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularity is the highest smoothness level shared by the objective and all constraints near the feasible set, using a disjoint five-level hierarchy.
assumptions_latex: Every defining function is real-valued on a common open neighborhood \(U\).
Regularity is assessed before solver-specific reformulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularity label \(\rho(I)\) is the minimum regularity level attained by any \(\phi\in\Phi_I\).

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-Cost Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cost strata independently of the information exposed by an oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a declared per-evaluation cost statistic \(c_I\in[0,\infty]\) for each benchmark instance \(I\), such as median wall time or a normalized operation count, and thresholds \(0=\tau_0<\tau_1<\cdots<\tau_m=\infty\). Define \(E_1=\{I:\tau_0\leq c_I\leq\tau_1\}\) and, for \(j=2,\ldots,m\), \(E_j=\{I:\tau_{j-1}<c_I\leq\tau_j\}\). These evaluation-cost classes partition the instances for which \(c_I\) is defined. Every reported class must retain the statistic, unit, aggregation rule, hardware and software environment, and threshold version; otherwise classifications obtained in different environments are not directly comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation-cost classes partition instances with a defined cost statistic using a first interval that includes zero and subsequent fixed-threshold intervals, under a recorded computational environment.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the admissible query domain.
A fixed machine, implementation, and cost unit are used throughout the comparison.
The cost statistic \(c_I\) is defined for every classified instance \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\in E_1\) exactly when \(0\leq c_I\leq\tau_1\), and for \(j=2,\ldots,m\), \(I\in E_j\) exactly when \(\tau_{j-1}<c_I\leq\tau_j\).

children.title: Feasibility Records
children.top_down_role: Recorded feasibility classifications, residual summaries, tolerances, and supporting evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a tolerance-aware, independently checkable feasibility record.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_g\) and \(I_h\) be finite index sets for the declared constraints \(g_i(x)\leq0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\), and let \(\tau_i\geq0\) and \(\eta_j\geq0\) be fixed tolerances. A feasibility record for \(x\) contains the evaluated constraint values, declared tolerances, arithmetic and evaluation method, and the residual \[v(x)=\max\!\left(\{0\}\cup\{g_i(x)-\tau_i:i\in I_g\}\cup\{|h_j(x)|-\eta_j:j\in I_h\}\right).\] The record classifies \(x\) as feasible exactly when \(v(x)=0\), provided every required evaluation succeeds. A missing, nonfinite, or failed required evaluation yields an indeterminate record rather than a feasible one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility record stores all required constraint evaluations, tolerances, and their maximum positive violation. Zero violation establishes tolerance-feasibility; a failed, missing, or nonfinite required evaluation makes the result indeterminate.
assumptions_latex: The instance declares finite constraint families \(g_i(x)\leq0\) for \(i\in I_g\) and \(h_j(x)=0\) for \(j\in I_h\).
Nonnegative feasibility tolerances \(\tau_i\) for \(i\in I_g\) and \(\eta_j\) for \(j\in I_h\) are fixed before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Provided every required evaluation succeeds, \(v(x)=0\) if and only if \(g_i(x)\leq\tau_i\) for every \(i\in I_g\) and \(|h_j(x)|\leq\eta_j\) for every \(j\in I_h\).

children.title: Version-Lineage Links

knowledge_statements.title: Version-Lineage Links
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines directed lineage among immutable benchmark-metadata versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a set of immutable benchmark-metadata versions. A version-lineage relation is a directed relation \(E\subseteq V\times V\) in which \((u,v)\in E\) means that \(v\) was directly derived from \(u\). Valid lineage requires that \((V,E)\) be acyclic, every nonroot version have at least one identified predecessor, and each edge reference the revision-history record describing the derivation. The transitive closure \(E^{+}\) records indirect ancestry; hence \((u,v)\in E^{+}\) means that the contents of \(v\) descend through one or more recorded revisions from \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Version-lineage links form an acyclic directed graph whose edges identify direct derivations and whose transitive closure identifies ancestry.
assumptions_latex: Each version in \(V\) is immutable and persistently identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relation \(E^{+}\) determines the recorded ancestry of every benchmark-metadata version.

notation.meaning: transitive closure of the lineage relation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the lineage leaf, but acyclicity, predecessor coverage, and mandatory revision-record linkage are substantive governance requirements with no cited source.

children.title: Revision-Impact Flags
children.top_down_role: Indicators of whether a revision affects comparability, validity, status, or reference values.

knowledge_statements.title: Revision-Impact Flags
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies whether a metadata revision can alter benchmark interpretation or comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a revision with field-change set \(\Delta\), define the impact flag \(I(\Delta)\in\{\mathrm{none},\mathrm{reporting},\mathrm{comparability},\mathrm{validity}\}\). Assign \(\mathrm{validity}\) if any change can alter the feasible set, objective, reference solution, or asserted solution status; assign \(\mathrm{comparability}\) if validity is unchanged but instance identity, metric definition, stopping rule, or resource accounting changes; assign \(\mathrm{reporting}\) if only labels, formatting, or nonsemantic annotations change; and assign \(\mathrm{none}\) exactly when \(\Delta=\varnothing\). If several clauses apply, use the greatest impact under \(\mathrm{none}<\mathrm{reporting}<\mathrm{comparability}<\mathrm{validity}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A revision receives its highest applicable impact level according to whether it changes validity, comparability, reporting only, or nothing.
assumptions_latex: Every semantic field change is represented in \(\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(\Delta)\) is the maximum applicable revision-impact category.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the four-level impact taxonomy, precedence order, and field-to-impact assignments are project-specific conventions lacking authoritative support.

children.title: Optimality-Measure Protocols
children.top_down_role: Reporting conventions for objective quality, certified gaps, bounds, or optimality status.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality-Measure Protocols
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies absolute and relative objective gaps for minimization benchmarks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization instance with accepted reference value \(f^{\mathrm{ref}}\) and a feasible reported point \(x\), the protocol reports the signed gap \(g(x)=f(x)-f^{\mathrm{ref}}\), absolute gap \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}(x)=|g(x)|\), and scaled relative gap \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}(x)=|g(x)|/\max\{1,|f^{\mathrm{ref}}|\}\). A run meets absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon_a\) and relative tolerance \(\varepsilon_r\) when \(g(x)\leq \varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r|f^{\mathrm{ref}}|\). The report must identify the reference-value version and must not assign an objective gap to an infeasible point without separately labeling the value as provisional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For feasible minimization outputs, report signed, absolute, and scaled relative gaps against a versioned reference value and state the combined tolerance test.
assumptions_latex: The objective \(f\) and reference value \(f^{\mathrm{ref}}\) use the same minimization model and scaling.
The reported point \(x\) has passed the declared feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\), \(g_{\mathrm{abs}}(x)\), and \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}(x)\) provide reproducible optimality measures.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited section on epsilon-global minima does not evidently support the record's signed, absolute, and scaled-relative gap formulas or its combined tolerance and infeasible-point reporting rules. These conventions require a directly supporting benchmark-protocol source.

children.title: Feasibility-Measure Protocols
children.top_down_role: Reporting conventions for constraint residuals, violations, tolerances, or feasibility status.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Measure Protocols
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines scale-aware maximum violation for mixed continuous constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(i\in I\), and \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j\in J\), choose positive declared scales \(s_i,t_j\). Define \(v_i(x)=\max\{0,g_i(x)\}/s_i\) and \(w_j(x)=|h_j(x)|/t_j\), and report \(V_\infty(x)=\max(\{v_i(x):i\in I\}\cup\{w_j(x):j\in J\}\cup\{0\})\). Given tolerance \(\tau\geq0\), the point is protocol-feasible exactly when \(V_\infty(x)\leq\tau\). The report must state all scales, the tolerance, and whether constraint values were recomputed independently or copied from solver output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale each inequality and equality violation, report their maximum, and declare feasibility exactly when that maximum does not exceed the stated tolerance.
assumptions_latex: All constraint functions are evaluated on the reported point using the benchmark model.
Every scale \(s_i\) and \(t_j\) is finite and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is protocol-feasible if and only if \(V_\infty(x)\leq\tau\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the selected scaling, maximum-violation aggregation, feasibility threshold, and reporting requirements have no cited authoritative protocol source.

children.title: Cross-Metric Reporting
children.top_down_role: Joint presentation of primal feasibility, objective quality, bounds, and certification outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Metric Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents each run by paired feasibility and optimality measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each run \(r\), report the ordered metric vector \(M_r=(V_r,G_r,S_r)\), where \(V_r\geq0\) is the declared feasibility violation, \(S_r=\mathbf{1}\{V_r\leq\tau\}\), and \(G_r\) is the declared objective-gap measure when \(S_r=1\), otherwise \(G_r=\mathrm{NA}\). Comparisons use the lexicographic order \((S_r,-V_r,-G_r)\): a feasible run dominates an infeasible run; among infeasible runs, smaller violation is better; among feasible runs, smaller objective gap is better. Reports must also publish the unaggregated values so that alternative orderings remain computable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report feasibility, feasibility status, and objective gap together; rank feasibility first, then violation for infeasible runs or objective gap for feasible runs.
assumptions_latex: All runs use identical metric definitions and tolerances.
Objective gaps are comparable only for points passing the feasibility protocol.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_r=(V_r,G_r,S_r)\) preserves the joint feasibility-optimality outcome of run \(r\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed convention. Moreover, lexicographic ordering by (S_r,-V_r,-G_r) compares V_r before G_r for feasible runs, contrary to the stated rule, while -G_r is undefined when G_r=NA.

children.title: Measure-Aggregation Conventions
children.top_down_role: Conventions for summarizing per-constraint, per-instance, per-run, or per-solver measurements.

knowledge_statements.title: Measure-Aggregation Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines reproducible aggregation of repeated-run benchmark measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For run-level scalar measurements \(z_1,\ldots,z_m\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), record the sample size \(m\), failures, and censored observations before aggregation. For finite observations, report the median \(Q_{0.5}(z)\) and interquartile interval \([Q_{0.25}(z),Q_{0.75}(z)]\) using a declared quantile rule. Separately report the success fraction \(\widehat p=m^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{m}\mathbf{1}\{S_r=1\}\). A failed or censored run must not be silently deleted or replaced by zero; any finite penalty substitution must be declared before examining results and reported alongside the unmodified data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate repeated runs with declared quantiles and a separate success fraction, while retaining and explicitly labeling failures and censoring.
assumptions_latex: Runs use the same instance, configuration, stopping rule, and resource limit.
The quantile interpolation rule is fixed before comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Q_{0.5},[Q_{0.25},Q_{0.75}],\widehat p,m)\) is the required aggregate report.

notation.meaning: declared sample quantile at level q

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but no source supports the mandated median, interquartile interval, success fraction, or censoring treatment. The conclusion also does not specify whether its quantiles use all observations or only the stated finite subset.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Limit Protocols
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies uniform stopping limits and accounting rules for solver runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A resource-limit protocol is a tuple \(L=(T,W,M,N,\rho)\), where \(T\) is the wall-clock limit, \(W\) the CPU-time limit, \(M\) the peak-memory limit, \(N\) a solver-independent work limit when available, and \(\rho\) the accounting rule. Before any run, the applicable finite limits and measurement boundaries are fixed. A run is resource-censored at the first measured event violating an active limit. Setup, model translation, preprocessing, and validation time are included or excluded only according to \(\rho\), applied identically to every compared solver, and each run reports consumption and its termination cause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix time, memory, work, and accounting limits before execution; stop at the first exceeded limit and report both consumption and termination cause.
assumptions_latex: Resource counters are measured by a common mechanism across compared runs.
At least one of \(T,W,M,N\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every run has a reproducible censoring event and resource-consumption record under \(L\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the protocol container, but the resource tuple, first-violation censoring rule, and uniform inclusion or exclusion of workflow phases require an authoritative benchmarking source.

children.title: Hardware-Environment Controls
children.top_down_role: Controls for processor type, accelerators, memory hierarchy, storage, and system configuration.

knowledge_statements.title: Hardware-Environment Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the recorded hardware and software environment for comparable runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hardware-environment control record \(H\) identifies the processor model and count, accelerator model and count, installed and usable memory, storage class, operating system and kernel, compiler and numerical-library versions, solver binary and dependencies, and power or frequency policy. Two runs are environment-controlled only if their declared comparison permits every differing component of \(H\); otherwise the difference is a confounder that must be reported. Dynamic properties, including clock throttling and memory pressure, are sampled during execution when they can affect elapsed time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Record the full hardware and software stack; undeclared differences are confounders, and influential dynamic conditions must be monitored during runs.
assumptions_latex: Each compared run is associated with a persistent environment record \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Declared equality or differences between environment records determine whether hardware conditions are controlled.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the required environment fields, confounder criterion, and dynamic-monitoring obligation are substantive reproducibility rules without cited support.

children.title: Parallelism Controls
children.top_down_role: Controls for worker counts, thread counts, process counts, and concurrency limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallelism Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixes permitted concurrency and reports effective parallel resource use.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every run, fix a parallelism budget \(P=(p_{\mathrm{proc}},p_{\mathrm{thread}},p_{\mathrm{acc}},p_{\mathrm{nested}})\), giving maximum processes, threads per process, accelerator devices, and nested-library threads. Environment variables, solver options, and library settings must jointly enforce \(P\). A run conforms only if its observed concurrent workers and devices never exceed the corresponding limits. The report includes both configured limits and observed peak concurrency; automatic thread selection is admissible only when explicitly declared and applied under the same resource budget to all compared runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set and enforce process, thread, accelerator, and nested-parallelism limits, then report both configured and observed peak concurrency.
assumptions_latex: Concurrency can be observed or audited during each run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A conforming run uses no more parallel resources than specified by \(P\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is internally consistent, but no source supports the specific budget components, enforcement standard, peak-concurrency requirement, or treatment of automatic thread selection.

children.title: Topology-Affinity Controls
children.top_down_role: Controls for placement, pinning, locality, interconnect topology, and nonuniform memory access.

knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Affinity Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrains worker placement relative to machine memory and processor topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be the set of run workers and \(U\) the set of permitted processing units. A topology-affinity control is a fixed mapping \(A:W\to2^U\setminus\{\varnothing\}\), together with a declared memory-placement policy. A run conforms when every worker executes only on units in \(A(w)\), accelerator assignments remain fixed as declared, and memory allocation follows the specified NUMA policy. For comparative experiments, \(A\), simultaneous-multithreading use, socket distribution, and memory policy must be identical up to a documented topology-preserving relabeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pin each worker to declared processing units and a declared memory policy; comparisons require equivalent placement across machine topology.
assumptions_latex: The machine topology and worker identities are observable.
Affinity enforcement is available for the execution environment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conformance means observed placement agrees with \(A\) and the declared memory policy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the topology-affinity leaf, but the mapping model, NUMA conformance criterion, and topology-preserving equivalence requirement lack a cited systems-benchmarking source.

children.title: Parallel-Resource Isolation
children.top_down_role: Controls limiting interference from shared machines, competing jobs, scheduling, or resource oversubscription.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Resource Isolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exclusive or quota-enforced access to performance-critical shared resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the set of performance-critical resources allocated to a benchmark run, including processing units, accelerators, memory capacity and bandwidth domains, and relevant storage or network channels. The run is parallel-resource isolated when every competing workload is excluded from \(R\), or is constrained by declared quotas whose interference bound is accepted by the protocol. Isolation is verified over the measurement interval by scheduler allocation records and utilization counters. Any interval with undeclared oversubscription, device sharing, memory pressure, or external I/O contention invalidates timing comparability and must be flagged or rerun.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reserve or quota all performance-critical resources, verify isolation during measurement, and flag runs exposed to undeclared contention.
assumptions_latex: Scheduler records and resource-utilization counters cover the complete measurement interval.
The protocol declares whether isolation is exclusive or quota-based.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A run is timing-comparable only if no undeclared workload interferes with its allocated resource set \(R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but exclusive or quota-based isolation, verification requirements, and automatic invalidation of timing comparability lack cited support; the protocol's accepted interference bound is also not defined.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Translation Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controls isolating solver behavior from artifacts introduced while translating a benchmark model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each benchmark instance, fix a canonical mathematical model and a translation map \(T_s\) for every solver \(s\). A controlled translation must preserve variable domains, objective sense and scaling, constraint semantics, and declared tolerances. If \(F\) and \(F_s\) are the canonical and translated feasible sets, respectively, require a documented correspondence \(\phi_s:F\to F_s\) such that objective values and feasibility classifications agree within the prespecified translation tolerance. Any solver-specific reformulation, presolve, or unsupported-feature substitution must be recorded before execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a fixed, documented translation that preserves domains, objectives, constraints, and tolerance-based feasibility; disclose every solver-specific reformulation or substitution.
assumptions_latex: A canonical benchmark model and its numerical tolerances are specified.
Each solver interface admits a documented translation map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Translation-induced differences are either bounded by the declared tolerance or explicitly identified as experimental factors.

notation.meaning: translation from the canonical model to solver s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: controlled benchmarking requires semantic equivalence of solver inputs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the terminal container, but no inspectable source supports the proposed semantic-correspondence requirement, tolerance treatment, or disclosure protocol. Source support is needed before the mathematical and experimental requirements can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Solver-Configuration Controls
children.top_down_role: Controls for solver versions, options, presets, subsolvers, tolerances, and enabled features.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Configuration Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines when solver parameter settings constitute a controlled comparison factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta_s\) be the admissible configuration set for solver \(s\). Before observing benchmark outcomes, select a configuration \(\theta_s\in\Theta_s\), record every nondefault parameter, software version, numerical tolerance, preprocessing option, and stopping rule, and hold \(\theta_s\) fixed across all assigned instances and replicates. If several configurations are evaluated, treat each ordered pair \((s,\theta_s)\) as a distinct method and apply the same selection rule and resource limits to every pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predeclare and record each solver configuration, hold it fixed across assigned runs, and treat separately evaluated configurations as distinct methods.
assumptions_latex: The admissible solver parameters and defaults are identifiable.
Resource and stopping protocols are fixed independently of observed outcomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reported run is attributable to one reproducible method \((s,\theta_s)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reproducible solver comparisons require predeclared fixed configurations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope are appropriate, and the statement is internally coherent. However, the fixed-configuration and distinct-method prescriptions have no cited benchmarking source.

children.title: Repetition Controls
children.top_down_role: Controls for replicate counts, rerun eligibility, failed runs, and repeated measurements.

knowledge_statements.title: Repetition Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controls replicate counts and aggregation for repeated stochastic or system-variable runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every eligible method-instance pair \((m,p)\), prescribe a replicate count \(R_{m,p}\geq 1\) before execution. Replicates must use the same model, configuration, resource limit, stopping test, and measurement rule, differing only in explicitly designated replicate factors. Report all replicate outcomes or a prespecified aggregate, together with dispersion and the numbers of successful, failed, and censored runs. Replicate counts may vary only according to a rule fixed independently of the observed performance values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predeclare replicate counts, keep nonreplicate factors fixed, and report outcomes or prespecified summaries with dispersion, failures, and censoring.
assumptions_latex: Eligible method-instance pairs are specified before execution.
A rule identifies factors permitted to vary between replicates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated outcomes are comparable samples under a fixed experimental condition.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: repeated-run experiments require fixed replicate counts and aggregation rules
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is appropriately expressed as an experimental condition, but the replicate-count, aggregation, dispersion, failure, and censoring requirements are unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Randomness Controls
children.top_down_role: Controls for random seeds, nondeterministic execution, randomized heuristics, and sampling variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomness Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controls pseudorandom inputs and seed allocation across solver runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_{m,p,r}\) denote the pseudorandom seed assigned to method \(m\), instance \(p\), and replicate \(r\). Fix and archive the seed-allocation function before execution, prohibit seed changes prompted by outcomes, and record the generator and software version. Use common random numbers when meaningful paired randomness exists; otherwise assign independent, nonoverlapping streams. Each reported observation must be reproducible from \((m,p,r,u_{m,p,r})\) and the archived configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predefine and archive seed allocation and generators; use paired or independent streams consistently and never replace seeds based on outcomes.
assumptions_latex: The solver exposes or permits control of its pseudorandom stream.
Replicate identifiers are fixed before execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Random variation is reproducible and cannot be selected retrospectively to favor a method.

notation.meaning: seed for method m, instance p, and replicate r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: controlled randomized experiments require reproducible nonadaptive random streams
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits Randomness Controls, but the choice between common random numbers and independent streams, including the claimed reproducibility requirements, needs an authoritative experimental-design or benchmarking source.

children.title: Configuration–Replicate Linkage
children.top_down_role: Association of each replicate with its exact solver configuration, seed, environment, and outcome.

assumptions_latex: Complete solver configurations and replicate identifiers have stable identifiers.
A prespecified policy identifies which attempt, if any, supplies the reported outcome for each replicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The attempt-level mapping \(Y:K\to\mathcal{Y}\), together with the prespecified selection map \(D\), preserves the association among configurations, replicates, attempts, and reported outcomes.

notation.meaning: base key identifying an instance, solver, configuration, and replicate
prespecified map selecting the reported attempt for a base key
space of outcomes and terminal statuses

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: attempt-level immutable keys are needed for auditable configuration-replicate attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the immutable association among solver configurations, replicates, attempts, and reported outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each replicate by a base key \(b=(p,s,\theta,r)\), where \(p\) is the instance, \(s\) the solver, \(\theta\) its complete configuration, and \(r\) the replicate identifier. For each base key \(b\), let \(A_b\) be its set of attempt identifiers and define the attempt-level key set \(K=\{(b,a):a\in A_b\}\). The outcome table is a partial function \(Y:K\to\mathcal{Y}\), so each attempt-level key has at most one terminal record and no retry, restart, or resumed execution replaces an earlier record. A prespecified partial selection map \(D\) associates each reportable base key with at most one attempt in \(A_b\). Replicate aggregation uses only the outcomes selected by \(D\) within groups having identical \((p,s,\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Key every attempt by instance, solver, complete configuration, replicate, and attempt identifier; preserve earlier attempts and use a prespecified rule to select at most one reported outcome per replicate.
knowledge_statements.title: Configuration–Replicate Linkage

children.title: Search-Tree Progress Profile
children.top_down_role: Internal-search diagnostics used to distinguish primal progress, dual progress, reduction effects, and tree growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Open-Node Population Profile
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-tree diagnostic indexed by elapsed time or processed-node count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a branch-and-bound run, let \(\mathcal{O}(t)\) be the set of generated nodes that are neither processed nor pruned at progress index \(t\). The open-node population profile is \(N_{\mathrm{open}}(t)=|\mathcal{O}(t)|\), recorded against a declared index such as elapsed time, relaxation count, or processed-node count. The protocol must specify whether a node under active processing belongs to \(\mathcal{O}(t)\) and how simultaneous parallel-worker events are ordered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile records how many generated search nodes remain unprocessed and unpruned at each declared progress index.
assumptions_latex: The solver exposes timestamped search-tree events.
Generated nodes have unambiguous processed and pruned states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{open}}(t)\) is a nonnegative integer-valued search-tree trajectory.

notation.meaning: open-node set at progress index t

source_refs.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

source_witnesses.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with global optimum value \(f^*\).
Every value entered into \(\mathcal{B}(t)\) is a valid lower bound on \(f^*\), and \(\mathcal{B}(t)\) is nonempty at every reported index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every reported index \(t\), \(L(t)\leq f^*\), and \(L(t_2)\geq L(t_1)\) whenever \(t_2\geq t_1\).

notation.meaning: set of certified global lower bounds available by progress index t
best certified global lower bound available by progress index t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best certified global lower bound attained during a minimization search.

source_refs.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization run with global optimum value \(f^*\), let \(\mathcal{B}(t)\) be the nonempty set of all certified global lower bounds recorded by progress index \(t\). The global lower-bound profile is \(L(t)=\sup\mathcal{B}(t)\). In branch-and-bound, a value such as \(\min_{v\in\mathcal{O}(t)}\ell_v(t)\) may enter \(\mathcal{B}(t)\) only when the open-node bounds, fathoming decisions, and terminal accounting jointly certify it as a lower bound on \(f^*\). The protocol must state the progress index and the convention used when the open-node set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile tracks the greatest certified lower bound recorded by each progress index; an open-node minimum is included only when the complete branch-and-bound accounting makes it globally valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Lower-Bound Profile

source_witnesses.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114
11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Improvement Profile
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trajectory of the best feasible objective value found during minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization run, let \(I(t)\) be the set of feasible points accepted by the declared feasibility test by progress index \(t\). The incumbent profile is \(U(t)=\min_{x\in I(t)}f(x)\), with \(U(t)=+\infty\) before the first accepted point. Its improvement-event representation is the ordered sequence \((t_j,U_j)\) for which \(U_j<U_{j-1}\). With fixed feasibility and objective-evaluation rules, \(U(t)\) is nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile records the best accepted feasible objective value over progress, including each time that value strictly improves.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
Feasibility and objective values are assessed by fixed rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(t_2\geq t_1\), then \(U(t_2)\leq U(t_1)\), and every finite \(U(t)\) is attained by an accepted feasible point.

notation.meaning: accepted feasible points found by progress index t

source_refs.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

source_witnesses.locator: 3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with finite bounds satisfying \(L(t)\leq U(t)\) at every reported index.
The profiles use a common progress index, \(L(t)\) is nondecreasing, and \(U(t)\) is nonincreasing.
A reference index \(t_0\) is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(g(t_0)>0\), then \(C(t_0)=0\); if \(g(t_0)=0\), then \(C(t)=1\) for all \(t\geq t_0\); and certified equality \(U(t)=L(t)\) gives \(C(t)=1\).

notation.meaning: fraction of the reference gap closed

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized progress from a declared finite primal-dual gap toward a certified zero gap.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87
3.12 The GOP in a Branch and Bound Framework p. 114

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite minimization bounds \(L(t)\leq U(t)\), define \(g(t)=U(t)-L(t)\). Fix a reference index \(t_0\). If \(g(t_0)>0\), define \(C(t)=1-g(t)/g(t_0)\) for \(t\geq t_0\). If \(g(t_0)=0\), define \(C(t)=1\) for \(t\geq t_0\). If either bound is unavailable or nonfinite at \(t_0\), the profile is undefined. Any clipping of computed values to \([0,1]\) must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gap closure is one minus the current finite primal-dual gap divided by its finite positive reference value; when the reference gap is already zero, closure is one, and unavailable or nonfinite reference bounds leave the profile undefined.

Every measured post-reduction region satisfies \(X_v^{\mathrm{post}}\subseteq X_v^{\mathrm{pre}}\) and \(\mu(X_v^{\mathrm{pre}})>0\).
The positive aggregation weights are fixed before measurement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every measured node \(v\), \(0\leq e_v\leq1\); whenever \(R(t)\) is finite and nonempty, \(0\leq E(t)\leq1\).

fractional reduction effectiveness at node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a declared aggregation of search-region contraction during global search.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a nonnegative size functional \(\mu\) that is monotone under set inclusion. For a node region \(X_v^{\mathrm{pre}}\) before reduction and \(X_v^{\mathrm{post}}\subseteq X_v^{\mathrm{pre}}\) afterward, with \(\mu(X_v^{\mathrm{pre}})>0\), define \(e_v=1-\mu(X_v^{\mathrm{post}})/\mu(X_v^{\mathrm{pre}})\). Let \(R(t)\) be the finite set of nodes measured by progress index \(t\), and fix positive weights \(w_v\). When \(R(t)\) is nonempty, define \(E(t)=\bigl(\sum_{v\in R(t)}w_ve_v\bigr)/\bigl(\sum_{v\in R(t)}w_v\bigr)\). The protocol must separately report the count of nodes with empty post-reduction regions and declare how such nodes enter \(E(t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile is a prespecified weighted mean of the fraction of region size removed at each measured node, using an inclusion-monotone size measure and an explicit convention for eliminated nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Performance Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dolan–Moré-style empirical distribution of solver performance ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite benchmark set, \(S\) a finite solver set, and \(t_{p,s}>0\) the resource used by solver \(s\) on problem \(p\) under a common success test. Set \(r_{p,s}=t_{p,s}/\min_{u\in S}t_{p,u}\), assigning \(r_{p,s}=+\infty\) to failures. The performance profile of \(s\) is \(\rho_s(\tau)=|P|^{-1}|\{p\in P:r_{p,s}\leq\tau\}|\) for \(\tau\geq1\). Thus \(\rho_s(1)\) is its winning fraction and \(\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\rho_s(\tau)\) its success fraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A performance profile gives the fraction of benchmark problems solved within each factor of the best observed resource use.
assumptions_latex: All solvers use the same problem set, success test, and resource definition.
Successful resource measurements are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(s\), \(\rho_s(\tau)\) is nondecreasing, lies in \([0,1]\), and is defined for \(\tau\geq1\).

notation.meaning: performance ratio for solver s on problem p
measured resource under the common success test

knowledge_statements.title: Data Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget-based empirical profile for solver benchmarking on continuous global-optimization instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be a finite benchmark set. For solver \(s\), let \(t_{p,s}\in[0,+\infty]\) be the resources used to satisfy a fixed success test on problem \(p\), and let \(b_p>0\) be a declared problem-size normalization. The data profile of \(s\) is
\[d_s(\alpha)=\frac{1}{|P|}\left|\left\{p\in P:t_{p,s}/b_p\leq \alpha\right\}\right|,\qquad \alpha\geq0.\]
An unsuccessful run has \(t_{p,s}=+\infty\). Thus \(d_s(\alpha)\) is the fraction of benchmark problems solved within normalized budget \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A data profile reports the fraction of benchmark problems a solver successfully completes within each normalized resource budget.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite and nonempty.
The success test, resource unit, and normalization \(b_p\) are fixed across solvers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_s:[0,+\infty)\to[0,1]\) is nondecreasing.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: empirical budget-distribution definition is standard, but the intended normalization convention is not sourced

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but data-profile normalization conventions are substantive and no benchmark-profile source is cited.

children.title: Reliability Profiles
children.top_down_role: Profiles of successful completion, stable status, certificate production, or reproducible outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Reliability Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical success probability as a function of a declared tolerance or target level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be a finite benchmark set, let \(R_p\) be the finite set of runs performed on problem \(p\), and let \(Q_{p,r}\geq0\) be a run-quality error, with smaller values better. The reliability profile at tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) is
\[R(\varepsilon)=\frac{\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{r\in R_p}\mathbf 1\{Q_{p,r}\leq\varepsilon\}}{\sum_{p\in P}|R_p|}.\]
Runs ending by timeout, numerical error, or invalid output count as unsuccessful unless the reporting protocol explicitly specifies another censoring rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reliability profile gives the empirical fraction of runs meeting each quality tolerance, under a declared rule for failed or censored runs.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and every \(R_p\) are finite, with at least one recorded run.
The quality measure and failure-handling rule are fixed before comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(\varepsilon)\in[0,1]\) and is nondecreasing in \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: quality error of run r on problem p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: empirical reliability curves are standard, but weighting and censoring conventions vary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The run-weighted reliability curve is coherent, but alternative problem-weighted and censoring conventions yield different profiles; a protocol source is required.

children.title: Failure-Incidence Profiles
children.top_down_role: Profiles of failure frequency across instances, runs, solvers, or resource regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Incidence Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cumulative empirical incidence of unsuccessful solver runs across a benchmark population.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite collection \(I\) of benchmark runs, let \(F_i\in\{0,1\}\) indicate failure and let \(z_i\in\mathbb R\) be a declared stratification variable, such as problem size or resource limit. The failure-incidence profile is
\[I_F(z)=\frac{\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{z_i\leq z\}F_i}{\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{z_i\leq z\}},\]
whenever the denominator is positive. Failure must be defined prospectively and may include timeout, infeasibility misclassification, invalid certificate, numerical termination, or failure to attain the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile records the observed failure fraction among runs up to each declared problem or resource stratum.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and each run has a recorded failure indicator.
The failure predicate and stratification variable are fixed across compared solvers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_F(z)\in[0,1]\) whenever it is defined.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is a natural empirical incidence estimator, but profile indexing conventions are unspecified

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The estimator is well defined, but calling the prefix-stratified failure fraction a failure-incidence profile depends on an unsourced indexing convention.

children.title: Failure-Mode Stratification
children.top_down_role: Breakdowns by numerical failure, resource exhaustion, invalid status, crash, stall, or missing certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Mode Stratification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of overall solver failure into mutually exclusive diagnostic modes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be a finite set of runs and let \(M_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,K\}\), where \(M_i=0\) denotes success and \(M_i=k\) denotes failure mode \(k\). For any nonempty stratum \(A\subseteq I\), define
\[\widehat p_k(A)=\frac{1}{|A|}\sum_{i\in A}\mathbf 1\{M_i=k\},\qquad k=1,\ldots,K.\]
If failure modes are exhaustive and mutually exclusive, then the overall failure incidence decomposes as
\[\widehat p_F(A)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\widehat p_k(A).\]
Strata and the precedence rule for runs exhibiting multiple symptoms must be declared before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overall failure incidence equals the sum of mode-specific incidences when every failed run receives exactly one predeclared failure label.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and \(A\) is nonempty.
Failure labels are exhaustive and mutually exclusive under a fixed precedence rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat p_F(A)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\widehat p_k(A)\).

notation.meaning: outcome or failure-mode label of run i
empirical incidence of failure mode k in stratum A
overall empirical failure incidence in A

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: categorical incidence decomposition is elementary, but the intended diagnostic taxonomy is unsourced

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The categorical decomposition is correct and representation is the appropriate kind, but the intended failure taxonomy and precedence convention lack a source.

children.title: Censoring-Treatment Profiles
children.top_down_role: Treatment of timeouts, memory limits, interrupted runs, missing outcomes, or unresolved statuses.

knowledge_statements.title: Censoring-Treatment Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Profile specifying how resource-limited runs enter time-to-event solver comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For runs \(i=1,\ldots,n\), let \(Y_i=\min(T_i,C_i)\), where \(T_i\) is time to the prescribed success event and \(C_i\) is the censoring time, and let \(\delta_i=\mathbf 1\{T_i\leq C_i\}\). Under independent right censoring, the censoring-aware success profile is
\[\widehat F(t)=1-\prod_{u\leq t}\left(1-\frac{d(u)}{n(u)}\right),\]
where \(d(u)\) is the number of observed successes at time \(u\) and \(n(u)\) is the number at risk immediately before \(u\). Timeouts therefore reduce the risk set after censoring rather than becoming observed successes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A censoring-treatment profile estimates time-to-success while retaining timeout information as right-censored observations rather than fabricated event times.
assumptions_latex: Runs are independently right-censored conditional on any modeled strata.
Success and censoring times use a common resource scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat F(t)\) is the Kaplan–Meier estimate of the cumulative success distribution.

notation.meaning: event count and risk-set size at u

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Kaplan–Meier treatment is standard, but no survival-analysis or benchmarking source was supplied

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Kaplan–Meier formula and interpretation are standard, but an authoritative survival-analysis or benchmarking source is required for the censoring assumptions and applicability.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Quality Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical distribution of certified or reference-based optimality gaps attained under a fixed budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be a finite benchmark set. At a fixed resource budget, solver \(s\) returns an incumbent upper bound \(U_{p,s}\) and a valid lower bound \(L_{p,s}\) for each minimization problem \(p\). Define the stabilized relative gap
\[g_{p,s}=\frac{\max\{0,U_{p,s}-L_{p,s}\}}{\max\{1,|U_{p,s}|,|L_{p,s}|\}}.\]
The gap-quality profile is
\[G_s(\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{|P|}\left|\{p\in P:g_{p,s}\leq\varepsilon\}\right|,\qquad \varepsilon\geq0.\]
Missing or invalid bounds are assigned \(g_{p,s}=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile gives the fraction of benchmark problems for which a solver achieves a certified normalized gap no larger than each tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite and nonempty.
Every finite \(L_{p,s}\) is a valid global lower bound and \(U_{p,s}\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_s(\varepsilon)\in[0,1]\) and is nondecreasing in \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: incumbent upper and certified lower bounds

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: empirical gap distributions are standard, but gap normalization conventions differ

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The empirical profile is coherent, but the stabilized relative-gap formula is one of several materially different conventions and is unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Time-to-Certificate Profiles
children.top_down_role: Elapsed-time distributions or curves indexed by certificate attainment.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-to-Certificate Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical time distribution for attaining a prescribed global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a certificate tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) and a finite benchmark set \(P\). For solver \(s\), let
\[T_{p,s}(\varepsilon)=\inf\{t\geq0:U_{p,s}(t)-L_{p,s}(t)\leq\varepsilon\},\]
with value \(+\infty\) if no valid certificate is produced. The time-to-certificate profile is
\[C_s(t;\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{|P|}\left|\{p\in P:T_{p,s}(\varepsilon)\leq t\}\right|.\]
Only times at which the incumbent is feasible and the lower bound is globally valid qualify as certificate times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile reports the fraction of problems globally certified to a fixed gap tolerance by each elapsed-time threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite and nonempty.
The clock, tolerance, feasibility test, and bound-validity test are common across solvers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_s(t;\varepsilon)\) is nondecreasing in \(t\) and takes values in \([0,1]\).

notation.meaning: incumbent and global lower bounds at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: first-passage certificate profiles are natural, but no benchmark-protocol source was supplied

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The first-passage profile fits the leaf, but the absolute-gap certificate predicate and benchmarking protocol require a source.

children.title: Memory-to-Certificate Profiles
children.top_down_role: Peak or cumulative memory profiles indexed by certificate attainment.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-to-Certificate Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical memory requirement for attaining a prescribed global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\varepsilon\geq0\) and a finite benchmark set \(P\). For each successful run of solver \(s\) on \(p\), let \(M_{p,s}(\varepsilon)\) be the peak allocated memory up to the first time a feasible incumbent and valid global lower bound satisfy \(U_{p,s}-L_{p,s}\leq\varepsilon\). Set \(M_{p,s}(\varepsilon)=+\infty\) if no such certificate occurs. The memory-to-certificate profile is
\[C_s^{M}(m;\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{|P|}\left|\{p\in P:M_{p,s}(\varepsilon)\leq m\}\right|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile gives the fraction of problems certified within each peak-memory allowance at a fixed optimality tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite and nonempty.
Memory accounting and certificate validity rules are common across solvers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_s^{M}(m;\varepsilon)\) is nondecreasing in \(m\) and lies in \([0,1]\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: empirical resource distributions are standard, but memory-accounting conventions require a protocol source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent, but peak-memory accounting and certificate-event conventions vary across benchmark protocols and are not sourced.

children.title: Resource-Tradeoff Profiles
children.top_down_role: Joint views of time, memory, completion rate, and certificate quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Tradeoff Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-resource attainment surface for valid global-optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a certificate tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) and finite benchmark set \(P\). Let \(T_{p,s}(\varepsilon)\) and \(M_{p,s}(\varepsilon)\) be elapsed time and peak memory through the first valid \(\varepsilon\)-certificate, with both set to \(+\infty\) when certification fails. The joint resource-tradeoff profile is
\[H_s(t,m;\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{|P|}\left|\{p\in P:T_{p,s}(\varepsilon)\leq t,\ M_{p,s}(\varepsilon)\leq m\}\right|.\]
Its upper level sets describe time-memory budgets achieving a prescribed certified-success fraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The joint profile measures the fraction of problems certified while simultaneously respecting given time and peak-memory limits.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite and nonempty.
Time, memory, and certificate rules are measured consistently across solvers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_s(t,m;\varepsilon)\) is coordinatewise nondecreasing in \((t,m)\).

notation.meaning: time and peak memory through certification

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: joint empirical attainment surfaces are mathematically natural, but the intended tradeoff convention is unsourced

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint empirical attainment surface is mathematically valid and representation is appropriate, but the time-memory tradeoff convention lacks a supporting source.

children.title: Certificate-Censoring Profiles
children.top_down_role: Resource-profile treatment of runs ending before a requested certificate is obtained.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Censoring Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-censoring representation for runs that terminate before producing a prescribed certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix certificate tolerance \(\varepsilon\). For run \(i\), let \(T_i(\varepsilon)\) be its latent time to a valid certificate and let \(C_i\) be its imposed termination time. Record
\[Y_i=\min\{T_i(\varepsilon),C_i\},\qquad \delta_i=\mathbf 1\{T_i(\varepsilon)\leq C_i\}.\]
Under independent right censoring, define the certificate-attainment profile by
\[\widehat F_\varepsilon(t)=1-\prod_{u\leq t}\left(1-\frac{d_\varepsilon(u)}{n(u)}\right),\]
where \(d_\varepsilon(u)\) counts certificates at \(u\) and \(n(u)\) is the preceding risk set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The profile estimates certificate attainment over time while treating terminated uncertified runs as right-censored observations.
assumptions_latex: Censoring is independent of latent certificate time, conditionally on any declared strata.
All runs use the same certificate predicate and resource clock.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat F_\varepsilon(t)\) estimates the cumulative distribution of time to a valid \(\varepsilon\)-certificate.

notation.meaning: certificate count and risk-set size at u
