knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Relaxation Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of branch-and-bound progress when regional relaxations do not tighten under refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimization by spatial branch-and-bound with incumbent upper bounds \(U_k\) and active-node relaxation bounds \(L_k=\min_{B\in\mathcal A_k}\ell(B)\). Weak-relaxation stagnation occurs along nested regions \(B_1\supset B_2\supset\cdots\), with diameters tending to zero, when there exist \(\eta>0\) and a feasible accumulation point \(x^*\) such that
\[f(x^*)-\ell(B_k)\geq\eta\quad\text{for infinitely many }k.\]
Then refinement alone cannot force the certified global gap below \(\eta\); finite termination at any tolerance \(\varepsilon<\eta\) requires stronger relaxations, additional cuts, or another valid bounding mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If regional lower bounds remain uniformly separated from attainable values despite shrinking regions, branching alone cannot deliver arbitrarily accurate certificates.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\ell(B)\) is a valid lower bound on region \(B\).
The nested regions have a feasible accumulation point \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k\) cannot be forced below every \(\varepsilon<\eta\) by refinement of this branch alone.

notation.meaning: relaxation lower bound on region B
global incumbent and active lower bound

source_refs.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282

review_flags: failure-boundary formulation inferred from the consistency requirement underlying convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A persistent gap on one nested branch does not by itself imply that the global incumbent gap cannot fall below eta: the incumbent may be below f(x*) through another region. The cited convergence section must be inspected, and the claim needs an additional hypothesis linking this branch to the global lower bound and incumbent, or a branch-local conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconsistent Regional Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation of asymptotic consistency between regional lower bounds and pointwise objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization problem on \(X\), a valid regional bounding rule \(\ell\) is consistent if every nested sequence \(B_1\supset B_2\supset\cdots\subseteq X\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\) and \(\bigcap_k B_k=\{x\}\) satisfies \(\ell(B_k)\to f(x)\). A nonconsistent regional bound admits such a sequence and an \(\eta>0\) for which
\[f(x)-\ell(B_k)\geq\eta\]
infinitely often. Even when every \(\ell(B_k)\) is valid, this failure prevents shrinking-region arguments from proving convergence of the lower bounds to the objective at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regional bounds are nonconsistent when they fail to converge to the point value as nested regions shrink to that point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a metric feasible domain and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\).
\(\ell(B)\leq\inf_{y\in B}f(y)\) for every nonempty region \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonconsistency invalidates convergence arguments that infer \(\ell(B_k)\to f(x)\) solely from \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Dual-Bound Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure criterion for recovering regional lower bounds from approximate dual solutions in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_R\) be the regional minimization value and \(p_R\) the value of a valid relaxation, so \(p_R\le v_R\). Suppose \(y\) is certified feasible for a dual problem whose objective \(q\) satisfies weak duality, and an approximation \(\widehat q(y)\) satisfies the certified error bound \(|\widehat q(y)-q(y)|\le\eta\) for some \(\eta\ge0\). Then \(\ell=\widehat q(y)-\eta\le q(y)\le p_R\le v_R\), so \(\ell\) is a valid regional lower bound. Without certificates establishing the relevant feasibility, weak-duality, and numerical-error conditions, the recovered number is not justified as a relaxation-derived lower bound; pruning from \(\ell\ge U\), where \(U\) is a feasible incumbent value, may then discard a region containing a better feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual value recovered through a relaxation is pruning-safe when certified dual feasibility, weak duality, and an evaluation-error bound place the corrected value below the relaxation and regional optima. Without those certificates, pruning from the recovered value is unsafe.
assumptions_latex: \(v_R\) is the regional minimization value and \(p_R\le v_R\) is the value of a valid relaxation.
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
\(y\) is dual feasible, weak duality gives \(q(y)\le p_R\), and \(|\widehat q(y)-q(y)|\le\eta\) is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell=\widehat q(y)-\eta\le p_R\le v_R\), so the pruning test \(\ell\ge U\) is justified under the stated certificates.

notation.meaning: optimal value of the regional minimization problem
optimal value of the regional relaxation
exact dual objective at the recovered dual vector

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Dependency Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical repeated-variable failure of natural interval evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[a,b]\) with \(a<b\), and consider the expression \(f(x)=x-x\). Its exact range is \(f(X)=\{0\}\). Natural interval arithmetic treats the two occurrences independently and returns \[F(X)=X-X=[a-b,b-a].\] Hence \(\operatorname{wid}(F(X))=2(b-a)\), although the exact range has width zero. The enclosure remains inclusion-valid, but its excess width is caused entirely by losing the equality between repeated occurrences of the same variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating x minus x with ordinary interval arithmetic produces a nonzero interval because repeated occurrences are treated independently, despite the exact value always being zero.
assumptions_latex: \(X=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R\) and \(a<b\).
\(F\) is the natural interval extension using independent interval operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(X)=[a-b,b-a]\supsetneq\{0\}=f(X)\).

notation.meaning: natural interval evaluation of the expression over X
upper endpoint minus lower endpoint of interval I

children.title: Bound-Overestimation Pathologies

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Overestimation Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies excess width of an inclusion interval relative to the exact range hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real function \(f\) on a box \(X\), let \(F(X)\) be an inclusion interval and let \(H_f(X)=\operatorname{hull}\{f(x):x\in X\}\). Define the width overestimation by \[\omega_F(X)=\operatorname{wid}(F(X))-\operatorname{wid}(H_f(X)).\] Inclusion implies \(\omega_F(X)\ge0\). The excess can be arbitrarily large across a family of boxes: for \(f(x)=x-x\) and \(X_M=[0,M]\), natural interval evaluation gives \(\omega_F(X_M)=2M\), whereas \(H_f(X_M)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inclusion bound may be arbitrarily wider than the exact range; the excess width is nonnegative and can grow without limit across expanding boxes.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(X\) is a nonempty box.
\(H_f(X)\subseteq F(X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\omega_F(X)\ge0\), and \(\sup_{M>0}\omega_F(X_M)=+\infty\) for the displayed family.

notation.meaning: interval hull of the exact range of f on X

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Driven Inflation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic classification of dependency-induced interval excess under box refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nested boxes \(X_k\) with \(h_k=\operatorname{diam}(X_k)\to0\), define \(e_k=\operatorname{wid}(F(X_k))-\operatorname{wid}(H_f(X_k))\ge0\). Dependency inflation is called vanishing when \(e_k\to0\), first-order persistent when \(0<\liminf e_k/h_k\le\limsup e_k/h_k<\infty\), and superlinear relative inflation when \(e_k/h_k\to\infty\). If \(\operatorname{wid}(H_f(X_k))>0\), the relative factor \(r_k=\operatorname{wid}(F(X_k))/\operatorname{wid}(H_f(X_k))\) distinguishes bounded inflation from divergent relative inflation through boundedness or divergence of \(r_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval inflation can be classified by how excess enclosure width scales with box diameter and by whether its ratio to exact range width stays bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(X_{k+1}\subseteq X_k\) and \(h_k\to0\).
\(H_f(X_k)\subseteq F(X_k)\) for every \(k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Overestimation Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdivision-and-sampling diagnostic for persistent interval overestimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an expression \(f\), box \(X\), inclusion extension \(F\), finite sample set \(S\subset X\), threshold \(\tau>0\), and depth \(d\). Compute \(W_I=\operatorname{wid}(F(X))\), \(W_S=\max_{s\in S}f(s)-\min_{s\in S}f(s)\), and \(g=(W_I-W_S)/\max\{W_I,1\}\). Bisect the widest coordinate, repeat these quantities on every descendant through depth \(d\), and track repeated-variable occurrences. Output a persistent-overestimation flag when \(g\ge\tau\) along a descendant chain and the excess decreases no faster than its box diameter; otherwise output no flag. Sampling diagnoses but does not certify the exact range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare interval width with sampled variation through repeated subdivision; persistent normalized gaps that shrink no faster than box diameter indicate likely dependency overestimation.
assumptions_latex: \(F(Y)\supseteq f(Y)\) for every tested descendant box \(Y\).
Each sample set is nonempty and contained in its tested box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\ge\tau\) persistently triggers an overestimation diagnostic, not a range certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Subsolver Inaccuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pruning boundary for inexact solutions of regional relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_R\) be the exact value of a regional minimization relaxation, and let a subsolver report \(\widehat p_R\). If a computable one-sided error bound \(\varepsilon_R\ge0\) certifies \(p_R\ge\widehat p_R-\varepsilon_R\), then \(L_R=\widehat p_R-\varepsilon_R\) is a usable relaxation lower bound. The report \(\widehat p_R\) alone does not justify pruning unless some certificate establishes \(\widehat p_R\le p_R\). For example, minimizing \(x\) on \([0,1]\) has value zero; treating the uncertified report \(\widehat p_R=0.1\) as a lower bound would prune against an incumbent \(U=0.05\), even though the region contains the better value zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reported approximate relaxation value is not by itself a pruning certificate. A certified one-sided error bound can convert it into a guaranteed lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The regional relaxation is a minimization problem with exact value \(p_R\).
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
\(\varepsilon_R\ge0\) is a certified one-sided subsolver error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_R=\widehat p_R-\varepsilon_R\le p_R\) must be certified before using \(L_R\ge U\) to prune.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point criterion for unsuccessful interval or feasibility-based bound propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the current variable box and let \(T\) be a sound contractor satisfying \(T(B)\subseteq B\) while retaining every feasible point in \(B\). Propagation stagnates at \(B\) when \[T(B)=B\] although \(B\) is neither certified infeasible nor sufficiently reduced for the solver's stopping tolerances. For a cyclic sequence of contractors \(T_1,\ldots,T_m\), the corresponding condition is \((T_m\circ\cdots\circ T_1)(B)=B\) with the same unresolved status.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonfinite FBBT Limit Approach
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sound propagation sequence whose limiting box is never attained finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x\in[0,1]\) subject to \(x=x/2\), whose unique feasible value is zero. A sound forward feasibility-based bound-tightening pass that replaces the current interval \(X_k\) by \(X_k\cap(X_k/2)\) produces \[X_0=[0,1],\qquad X_k=[0,2^{-k}]\quad(k\ge1).\] Thus \(X_{k+1}\subsetneq X_k\) for every finite \(k\), and \(\bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}X_k=\{0\}\), but no finite pass reaches the limiting hull \(\{0\}\). Finite termination therefore requires a tolerance, stronger propagation, or an additional inference rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated sound bound tightening can converge geometrically to the exact feasible hull without attaining that hull after any finite number of passes.
assumptions_latex: Propagation uses only the update \(X\leftarrow X\cap(X/2)\).
Intervals are evaluated in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_k=[0,2^{-k}]\ne\{0\}\) for every finite \(k\), while \(X_k\downarrow\{0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Excessive Tightening Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work criterion comparing repeated tightening with immediate branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose processing a search node without tightening costs \(C_B\), each complete tightening pass costs \(C_T\), and applying \(q\) passes leaves \(N(q)\) nodes to be processed. Under this additive work model, total work is bounded by \[W(q)=N(q)(C_B+qC_T).\] Relative to immediate branching, the tightening budget \(q\) is excessive whenever \(W(q)>W(0)=N(0)C_B\). Equivalently, tightening is cost-justified only if the fractional reduction in processed nodes compensates for the per-node overhead \(qC_T\); bound improvement alone does not establish this.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening is excessive when its per-node cost outweighs the reduction it causes in the number of search nodes processed.
assumptions_latex: Node-processing and tightening costs are nonnegative and additive.
\(N(q)\) counts nodes processed after using \(q\) tightening passes per node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(q)(C_B+qC_T)>N(0)C_B\) characterizes excessive tightening in the stated model.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Domain Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of a feasible point by a non-solution-preserving contractor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the constraint \(x^2=0\) on \(B=[-1,1]\), whose feasible set is \(S=\{0\}\). For any \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), the proposed reduction \(C(B)=[\varepsilon,1]\) satisfies \(C(B)\subset B\) but violates solution preservation because \[S\cap B=\{0\}\not\subseteq C(B).\] Consequently, declaring the removed region \(B\setminus C(B)\) infeasible eliminates the unique feasible point. Box contraction alone is therefore insufficient: every domain reduction used for global certification must retain all feasible points in the input box.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact node count when binary spatial branching receives no early pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a binary branch-and-bound tree in which every node at depths \(0,\ldots,d-1\) is branched and no node is pruned before depth \(d\). The tree then contains exactly \(2^k\) nodes at depth \(k\), hence \[N_d=\sum_{k=0}^{d}2^k=2^{d+1}-1\] processed nodes and \(2^d\) leaves. Thus work and memory are exponential in the unresolved branching depth whenever their per-node requirements are bounded below by positive constants. Stronger bounds or reductions avoid this count only by pruning or terminating branches earlier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With binary branching and no pruning through depth d, the solver processes exactly 2^(d+1)-1 nodes and generates 2^d leaves.
assumptions_latex: Every nonleaf node has exactly two children.
No node at depth less than \(d\) is pruned or terminated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_d=2^{d+1}-1\) and the leaf count is \(2^d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth penalty caused by repeatedly following the larger child of an unequal split.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an interval of width \(w>0\) be split into children with widths \(\alpha w\) and \((1-\alpha)w\), where \(0<\alpha<1\), and define \(b=\max\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\). If the larger child is repeatedly selected and the same relative split is used, its width after \(k\) branches is \(b^kw\). Reaching width at most \(\varepsilon<w\) therefore requires \[k\ge\left\lceil\frac{\log(\varepsilon/w)}{\log b}\right\rceil.\] This required depth diverges as \(b\uparrow1\), formalizing the slow spatial reduction caused by highly imbalanced branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly following the larger side of an unequal split reduces width geometrically, but the required depth diverges as the split becomes maximally imbalanced.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<w\) and \(1/2\le b<1\).
The same relative split is applied along the selected branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\ge\left\lceil\log(\varepsilon/w)/\log b\right\rceil\), which tends to infinity as \(b\uparrow1\).

A status-reversal regime is a pair \((\theta,\theta')\) preserving the exact model and candidate but satisfying \(S_{\theta}(x)\neq S_{\theta'}(x)\). If the discrepancy disappears when residuals are evaluated with certified error bounds and a common physical-unit tolerance, the reversal is numerical; otherwise the runs do not implement equivalent status predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A status-reversal regime exists when equivalent solver runs assign different feasibility statuses to the same candidate because their numerical status predicates are not invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: Status-Reversal Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general-concepts chapter does not support this numerical diagnostic. Moreover, persistence after certified reevaluation does not by itself prove that the runs implement inequivalent status predicates; other model, candidate, or execution differences remain possible.

children.title: Certificate-Misclassification Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Evidence used to localize residual interpretation, tolerance, arithmetic, or postprocessing errors.

assumptions_latex: The original model, reported candidate, solver tolerances, and claimed certificate are available.
Residuals and objective values can be independently reevaluated with controlled numerical error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The diagnostic returns confirmed only when every recomputed certificate inequality holds with outward-rounded error bounds; otherwise it returns misclassified or unresolved.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent audit of numerical feasibility and optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a reported certificate \(C\), reevaluate every constraint and objective quantity in the original model, producing outward-rounded enclosures \([\underline r_i,\overline r_i]\). Normalize tolerances in original physical units and verify all logical implications used by \(C\), including incumbent feasibility, lower-bound validity, and the stated gap test. Set \(D(C)=\mathrm{confirmed}\) only if every required inequality holds throughout its enclosure; set \(D(C)=\mathrm{misclassified}\) if any required inequality is contradicted; otherwise set \(D(C)=\mathrm{unresolved}\). The output is \((D(C),\mathcal F)\), where \(\mathcal F\) lists failed or indeterminate checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute every certificate quantity independently with error bounds, then classify the certificate as confirmed, misclassified, or unresolved and report failed checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Misclassification Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is plausible and fits the diagnostic leaf, but no source supports the proposed three-way protocol. Validating a global lower bound may also require proof artifacts beyond reevaluation of residuals and objective quantities.

assumptions_latex: A minimization solver maintains a claimed global lower bound \(L\) and feasible incumbent value \(U\).
Termination uses absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon_a\geq0\) and relative tolerance \(\varepsilon_r\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A small reported gap certifies global accuracy only if \(L\leq f^\star\leq U\); without both inequalities, gap closure is premature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalid termination caused by closing a numerically small but uncertified global gap.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The termination test \(U-L\leq\gamma(U)\), with \(\gamma(U)=\varepsilon_a+\varepsilon_r\max\{1,|U|\}\), yields a valid global certificate only when \(U\) comes from a feasible point and \(L\leq f^\star\). Premature gap closure occurs when the test passes but either incumbent feasibility is unverified, \(L\) exceeds \(f^\star\), or floating-point comparison understates \(U-L\). In those cases the displayed gap does not imply \(U-f^\star\leq\gamma(U)\), even though the solver reports tolerance satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver closes the gap prematurely when its numerical gap test passes although the incumbent or lower bound lacks the validity needed for global accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Gap Closure

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

assumptions_latex: Each inequality \(g_i(x)\leq0\) is replaced by the equivalent exact inequality \(d_i g_i(x)\leq0\), with \(d_i>0\).
The solver applies a fixed numerical residual tolerance \(\tau>0\) after scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact equivalence does not ensure numerical status invariance: whenever \(0<g_i(x)\leq\tau<d_i g_i(x)\), the unscaled test accepts and the scaled test rejects the same candidate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status changes caused by applying non-covariant numerical tolerances after exact rescaling.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d_i>0\), the exact predicates \(g_i(x)\leq0\) and \(d_i g_i(x)\leq0\) are equivalent. Under the fixed numerical test \(g_i(x)\leq\tau\), however, the scaled implementation accepts precisely when \(g_i(x)\leq\tau/d_i\). Thus any candidate with \(0<g_i(x)\leq\tau<d_i g_i(x)\) is accepted before scaling and rejected afterward. Numerical status is scaling-invariant only when tolerances transform covariantly, for example as \(\tau_i'=d_i\tau_i\), with rounding errors also bounded consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent constraint scalings can reverse feasibility when residual tolerances are fixed in scaled units instead of transformed with the constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Status Instability

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

assumptions_latex: Parallel runs solve the same model with identical declared parameters and random seed.
The certificate depends on schedule-sensitive floating-point reductions, bound updates, or incumbent arrival order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If two admissible schedules produce certificates \(C_{\sigma}\neq C_{\sigma'}\) or different validity outcomes, the parallel certificate is nonreproducible and requires schedule-independent revalidation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-dependent variation in nominally identical global-optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{\sigma}\) denote the certificate emitted under admissible parallel schedule \(\sigma\). The certificate is reproducible when every pair \(\sigma,\sigma'\) yields identical certified claims and \(V(C_{\sigma})=V(C_{\sigma'})=\mathrm{valid}\) under an independent deterministic validator \(V\). It is nonreproducible when some pair yields different termination statuses, bounds, incumbents, or validator outcomes. Schedule-sensitive discovery times may change performance, but any claimed global certificate must remain valid after deterministic reconstruction from logged bound and feasibility evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parallel certificate is nonreproducible when admissible schedules change its claim or validation outcome, even with the same model, parameters, and seed.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonreproducible Parallel Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the parallel-certificate criterion. The statement also makes validity part of reproducibility, although a certificate can be reproducibly emitted yet consistently invalid; reproducibility and independent validity should be distinguished.

assumptions_latex: A benchmark supplies a claimed feasible reference point \(x^{\mathrm{ref}}\) and objective value \(v^{\mathrm{ref}}\).
The benchmark is a minimization problem with true optimum \(f^\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reference is incorrect if feasibility fails, its stored value disagrees with reevaluation beyond tolerance, or a valid bound contradicts its claimed optimality.

notation.meaning: reference point and stored reference value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detecting benchmark reference points or objective values that cannot support comparisons.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A claimed reference solution \((x^{\mathrm{ref}},v^{\mathrm{ref}})\) is admissible only if \(x^{\mathrm{ref}}\) satisfies every original constraint within a declared validation tolerance and \(|f(x^{\mathrm{ref}})-v^{\mathrm{ref}}|\leq\eta\). A claim of \(\eta\)-global optimality additionally requires \(v^{\mathrm{ref}}-f^\star\leq\eta\). The reference is incorrect if any feasibility check fails, the stored objective disagrees with independent reevaluation, or a verified lower bound \(L\) and feasible competitor \(x\) imply either \(L>v^{\mathrm{ref}}+\eta\) or \(f(x)<v^{\mathrm{ref}}-\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reference solution is incorrect when independent checks refute its feasibility, stored objective, or claimed global accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Incorrect Reference Solutions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

assumptions_latex: An original model \(P\) is translated into a solver model \(\widehat P\).
A map \(T\) relates original variables to translated variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Translation preserves benchmark meaning only when feasible sets and objective values correspond under \(T\); failure of either correspondence constitutes model-translation drift.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic inequivalence introduced while encoding a benchmark for a solver.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) and \(\widehat F\) be the feasible sets of \(P\) and \(\widehat P\). The translation is benchmark-equivalent when \(T(F)=\widehat F\) and there exist constants \(a>0\) and \(b\) such that \(\widehat f(Tx)=a f(x)+b\) for every \(x\in F\), with reported solutions mapped back consistently. Model-translation drift occurs when these conditions fail because of altered bounds, constraint signs, constants, domains, tolerances, or nonlinear expressions. Then feasibility, objective gaps, or rankings measured on \(\widehat P\) need not describe \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model-translation drift occurs when a solver encoding changes feasible solutions or objective ordering relative to the original benchmark.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Translation Drift

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited model-structure section does not establish the proposed equivalence criterion. The affine objective relation is a sufficient convention for preserving gaps and rankings, not a necessary condition for every notion of benchmark meaning, so failure of it cannot universally define drift. As a named failure phenomenon, failure_boundary would fit better than condition.

assumptions_latex: Two solvers report optimality measures \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) for the same minimization instance.
Each measure may use different bounds, scaling, denominator, or feasibility convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The measures are comparable only after a common valid bound pair and a common normalization are used; otherwise their numerical ordering has no invariant performance meaning.

notation.meaning: feasible upper and valid global lower bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparability of reported global-optimality gaps across solvers or studies.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reported optimality measures \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) are directly comparable only if they are computed from the same feasible upper bound \(U\), the same valid lower bound \(L\), the same objective orientation and units, and the same normalization. For example, \(g_a=U-L\) and \(g_r=(U-L)/\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\) answer different accuracy questions. If either solver permits infeasible incumbents, uses a different relative-gap denominator, or transforms the objective without converting tolerances, an inequality such as \(m_1<m_2\) does not establish superior optimality accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality measures are incomparable when they use different valid bounds, units, feasibility rules, or gap normalizations.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomparable Optimality Measures

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Requiring both measures to use the identical bound pair is too strong: solver-specific valid bounds can be compared after applying the same defined metric, units, orientation, and feasibility convention. A direct source is needed to select and justify the intended comparability convention.

assumptions_latex: Runtime \(R\geq0\) is observed only up to a timeout \(C>0\).
The recorded data are \(Y=\min\{R,C\}\) and \(\delta=\mathbf 1\{R\leq C\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mean computed only from completed runs estimates \(\mathbb E[R\mid R\leq C]\), not \(\mathbb E[R]\), and is downward biased whenever timeouts have positive probability and longer runtimes occur beyond \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias from excluding or misrepresenting solver runs terminated by time limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With right-censored runtime data \((Y,delta), where \(Y=\min\{R,C\}\) and \(\delta=\mathbf 1\{R\leq C\}\), averaging only completed runs converges to \(\mathbb E[R\mid R\leq C]\). If \(\mathbb P(R>C)>0\) and runtimes beyond \(C\) are stochastically larger, then \(\mathbb E[R\mid R\leq C]<\mathbb E[R]\). Recording each timeout as exactly \(C\) instead estimates \(\mathbb E[\min\{R,C\}]\), which is also no greater than \(\mathbb E[R]\). Unbiased comparison therefore requires an explicitly censored-data estimand and method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarding timed-out runs, or treating them as completed at the limit, systematically understates runtime unless the censored estimand is reported explicitly.
knowledge_statements.title: Censored Timeout Bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standard censoring claim lacks a cited survival-analysis source. The statement also contains an undelimited plain-text variable in “(Y,delta)” and needs existence and nondegeneracy assumptions for the conditional and unconditional expectations.

assumptions_latex: Target benchmark instances follow distribution \(p\), while evaluated instances follow selection distribution \(q\).
Instance-level performance is \(h(z)\), with finite target expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unweighted benchmark mean targets \(\mathbb E_q[h(Z)]\), not \(\mathbb E_p[h(Z)]\); it is unbiased for the target only under matching distributions or equal relevant expectations.

notation.meaning: importance weight where q is positive

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional bias caused by nonrepresentative benchmark-instance selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the desired performance be \(\mu_p=\mathbb E_p[h(Z)]\), but let benchmark instances be sampled from \(q\). The ordinary sample mean estimates \(\mu_q=\mathbb E_q[h(Z)]\), so its target bias is \(\mu_q-\mu_p\). It is unbiased for \(\mu_p\) only if \(p=q\) or the two expectations coincide. When \(p\) is absolutely continuous with respect to \(q\) and weights are known, \(\mathbb E_q[w(Z)h(Z)]=\mu_p\) for \(w(z)=p(z)/q(z)\); unsupported target regions cannot be corrected by reweighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A benchmark average describes the selected instance distribution, not the target population, unless selection is representative or valid reweighting is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Benchmark Selection Bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distribution-shift and importance-weighting formulas are mathematically standard and property fits the leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for this nontrivial statistical claim.

children.title: Cross-Family Failure Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Signals and evidence used to distinguish failures spanning bounding, reduction, search, numerical, or benchmarking families.

assumptions_latex: A failed run provides the original model, logs, bounds, incumbents, and numerical configuration.
Each diagnostic rerun changes one controlled factor while preserving the mathematical problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns the smallest observed failure family set consistent with violated invariants, together with any unresolved interactions requiring joint tests.

notation.meaning: violated invariants under diagnostic run k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled localization of interacting bounding, search, numerical, and benchmarking failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal F\) with all candidate failure families and evaluate invariants \(\mathcal I\): original-model feasibility, valid lower bounds, monotone incumbent quality, exhaustive active-region accounting, and reproducible certificate validation. Perform controlled reruns that separately change precision, scaling, concurrency, local-solver use, reduction rules, and benchmark translation. For run \(k\), record the violated set \(V_k\subseteq\mathcal I\). Remove a family from \(\mathcal F\) only when its defining intervention leaves every relevant violation unchanged and another tested mechanism explains it. Output the minimal retained family set plus interactions not separated by the performed interventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check shared invariants and use controlled reruns to isolate which failure families, possibly interacting, explain a solver failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Family Failure Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the diagnostic container, but no source supports its intervention and elimination rules. Those rules do not establish that the returned family set is mathematically minimal, particularly when mechanisms interact or interventions are incomplete.

children.title: Certificate-Impact Triage
children.top_down_role: Organization of failures by certificate invalidation, progress degradation, comparison distortion, or recoverability.

assumptions_latex: Each detected issue has documented effects on feasibility, bounds, termination, reproducibility, and performance reporting.
Certificate validity takes precedence over speed or solution-quality comparisons.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Issues with \(v=0\) receive highest priority; among equal validity classes, larger scope and irreproducibility are triaged before performance-only effects.

notation.meaning: number or measure of affected instances

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority rule for failures according to their effect on certificate trustworthiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each issue, independently revalidate feasibility, lower bounds, and termination, then assign \(v=1\) only if the claimed certificate remains valid. Estimate affected scope \(s\), set \(r=1\) only if the result is reproducible, and record whether the issue changes merely runtime or also the reported solution. Order issues lexicographically by \((v,-s,r)\), with smaller tuples receiving earlier investigation. Within a tie, prioritize mechanisms capable of invalidating shared bounds or pruning decisions over local performance effects. Output the ordered issues, their affected claims, and the evidence required to restore each certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triage first any issue that can invalidate a certificate, then prioritize broad and irreproducible effects before performance-only discrepancies.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Impact Triage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lexicographic triage algorithm is coherent and locally relevant, but it is a normative priority rule with no cited source or established rationale for the particular ordering and tie-breaking criteria.

children.title: Failure-Propagation Paths
children.top_down_role: Routes through which local solver failures affect downstream search, validation, reporting, or benchmarking outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Propagation Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tracks an invalid regional bound through pruning to a false global-optimality certificate in a deterministic partition-based solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonempty compact search region \(R\subseteq X\), define \(\phi(R)=\min_{x\in R} f(x)\); a valid reported lower bound must satisfy \(\ell(R)\leq\phi(R)\). Let \(\varepsilon\geq 0\), and suppose that \(R^*\) is the only active region containing a global minimizer \(x^*\), but an erroneous bound satisfies \(\ell(R^*)\geq U\) and causes \(R^*\) to be pruned. If the resulting active family \(\mathcal A\) is nonempty and subsequently satisfies \(U-\min_{R\in\mathcal A}\ell(R)\leq\varepsilon\) while \(U-f(x^*)>\varepsilon\), then the reported gap test yields a false \(\varepsilon\)-global-optimality certificate. Thus bound overestimation propagates through erroneous pruning and loss of optimizer coverage to invalid gap termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an overestimated bound prunes the only active region containing a true global optimizer, a later reported-gap test can pass even though the incumbent is more than the prescribed tolerance above the true optimum, thereby producing a false global-optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact, and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
The deterministic solver maintains nonempty compact search regions, reported regional lower bounds, a feasible incumbent value \(U\), and an active-region family.
A region is permanently pruned whenever its reported lower bound is at least \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An overestimated regional lower bound can propagate through pruning and active-set updates to produce a false \(\varepsilon\)-global-optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: Feasible domain, objective function, and a global minimizer, respectively.
A search region, its true regional minimum value, and its reported lower bound.
Feasible incumbent value, active-region family, and global-optimality tolerance.
